Raised out of the EOP-14 Slice E review (PR #49). @architecture-guardian, as DoD gate 5, found these and deliberately deferred them rather than let them be smuggled into a remediation pass already carrying 1564 changed lines. Its reasoning was that the arguments these citations support are unaffected — ADR-025's pre-flight table reasons about which Trick.acceptPlay refusals need pre-flighting, and that logic stands on Trick, not on line numbers — and that ADR-024 is not in Slice E's diff at all.

Part 1 — seven anchors that land inside javadoc @throws blocks (was gate 5's AG3-5)

These do not miss by a line or two. They land on @throws tags in the javadoc, roughly 26 lines above the statement the prose describes, so a reader following one is not reading a near-miss — they are reading documentation instead of code.

Citation Lands on Should be
ADR-025:214 → PlayCardUseCase.java:140 @throws SessionNotFoundException :166
ADR-025:216 → :147-149 @throws CardNotInHand/OutOfTurn/MustFollowSuit :173-175
ADR-025:219 → :156 @throws CardAlreadyPlayedException :185
ADR-025:215 → :181-190 card lookup and leader-seat read the candidate construction
ADR-025:218 → :168-170 a blank line and the hands read the leader-seat comparison
ADR-024:158 → :139 @throws NullPointerException :165
ADR-024:160 → :140-141 @throws SessionNotFound/PlayerNotRecognised :166-167

Carry this caveat, which is why the ticket is not cosmetic. ADR-024:156-160 is the blockquote that discharges that ADR's security obligation — that authorisation precedes any read — and @security-auditor's Slice D condition is still open. A future auditor verifying that obligation follows :139, lands on a @throws tag, and cannot confirm it.

Part 2 — two anchors that EOP-14 Slice E itself invalidated

Gate 5 overruled the Tech Lead on the premise here: these were correct at `b39e6a7` and are wrong only because Slice E's rewrite of the flag comment in src/main/resources/application.yml grew the block by eight lines and moved trick-play: false from line 91 to line 99.

  • ADR-023:759 — "false at application.yml:91" → :99
  • ADR-023:1304 — same (note `:1304`, not :1305; :1305 is the separate UseCaseConfiguration.java:196-260 clause, which is explicitly framed "As of EOP-14 Slice D" and so is dated rather than false)

Both sit inside > historical blockquotes whose substantive claim — that the flag is false — remains true, which is why gate 5 upheld the deferral.

Part 3 — the "first statement of all three" ordinal (was gate 5's AG3-3)

ADR-025:96 (a live decision heading), ADR-025:105, docs/adr/README.md:34 and ADR-024:157 all say authorisation is the first statement of the three trick-play use cases. It is the first statement in DealHandsUseCase:133, ResolveTrickUseCase:133, ReadOwnHandUseCase:64 and GetTrickStateUseCase:83, but not in PlayCardUseCase.execute (opens :161), where :162 Objects.requireNonNull(command, …) and :163 final var sessionId = command.sessionId(); precede the port call at :165.

Slice E already corrected this wording to "first port call" in the three places it had itself authored — PlayCardUseCase.java:22, CHANGELOG.md:32 and docs/adr/README.md:35 — on the principle that a line you rewrite is a line you own. The four above were not touched by that branch, so they were left. Note docs/adr/README.md:34 was explicitly checked: git diff HEAD -U0 showed the changed rows to be 23, 30, 33, 35 and 38, so line 34 is genuinely untouched.

Mitigating in all four: each pairs the phrase with a qualifier that is true ("before any hand, trick or card is read"), so the security property holds and only the ordinal is wrong.

Acceptance

  • Every citation above re-derived from source and corrected, or reframed as dated history in the style ADR-020 and ADR-025 already use.
  • The ordinal corrected to "first port call", or to wording true of all five use cases.
  • ADRs amended in place with dated notes — never rewritten, never renumbered.
  • ./mvnw verify green; AdrIndexConsistencyTest in particular still passes.
  • No cardinal or citation introduced without being re-derived from source first.

renderedFields.description:
Problem

docs/adr/ADR-013-feature-flags.md carries a binding mandate: every @ConditionalOnProperty on a feature flag in this repository must carry havingValue = "true". That mandate has now been violated twice, in two independent commits, while the ADR already said so:

  • TrickController — corrected to havingValue = "true" in 56c31b1 (EOP-14 Slice D).
  • SessionController plus four unconditional use-case beans — corrected in 34d30d7/50850d1 (EOP-48).

Both were caught by a reviewer, not by the build. A defect class with a demonstrated recurrence rate of two, guarded only by reviewer attention, is a defect class the build should be guarding.

Why it matters — the failure is silent and fails open

Verified against the resolved spring-boot-autoconfigure-4.1.0 bytecode during EOP-48. OnPropertyCondition$Spec.isMatch reduces, when havingValue is empty, to:

!"false".equalsIgnoreCase(value)

So the loose form enables the feature for every present value except the literal false — including off, no, 0, disabled, and the empty string (which is what EOP_FEATURES_SOMETHING= exported empty produces, the likeliest way an operator unsets a variable while leaving it present). off is the worst case: it is simultaneously the spelling an operator reaches for as a kill switch and a YAML 1.1 boolean false, so it reads as "disabled" to a human and "enabled" to Spring.

matchIfMissing already defaults to false, so an absent property was never the hole. The hole is confined to the present-but-not-false case, which is exactly the case a reviewer's eye skips over.

Scope

1. Automated check (the substance of this ticket)

Assert that every @ConditionalOnProperty in src/main/ carries havingValue = "true", and fail the build when one does not. Current state, for the baseline: eleven annotation sites, eleven compliant — SessionController:60, TrickController:69, and nine in UseCaseConfiguration (:101, :124, :167, :182, :218, :249, :268, :300, :319).

Consider also asserting the second half of the strengthened ADR-013 mandate — that a flag is repeated on every bean that opens or mutates the state behind it, not on the controller alone. This is the harder half and may not be mechanically checkable; if it is not, say so in the ADR rather than silently dropping it.

2. One-line addition to .opencode/rules/feature-flags.md

That file currently contains no occurrence of the string `havingValue` at all, and it is what every agent reads without opening ADR-013. Two independent commits fell into the trap while ADR-013 already carried the rule — which is the definition of a rule living in the wrong place. Proposed wording, from @architecture-guardian:

Every @ConditionalOnProperty on a flag MUST carry havingValue = "true" — the loose form enables the feature for every present value but the literal false, the empty string included — and MUST be repeated on every bean that opens or mutates the flagged state, not on the controller alone; pure reads and collaborators shared with a second flag stay ungated with the reason in their javadoc (ADR-013, EOP-48).

This needs its own ADR before implementation

The tool choice is a genuine decision with alternatives, costs and consequences, and it is why this was deliberately kept out of the EOP-48 fix commit. @architecture-guardian's position: amending ADR-013 was sufficient for the mandate, because the decision (flags as Spring configuration properties, having rejected Unleash, Flipt and FF4J) did not change. But "the mandate shall be machine-enforced" is a new decision, and the mechanism has real trade-offs.

Alternatives to weigh in the ADR:

  • ArchUnit — a new test dependency; reads annotations properly through reflection rather than by text matching; the conventional choice for exactly this kind of rule. Cost: a new dependency, and the enforcer's DependencyConvergence rule must still pass.
  • A docs-style test in the manner of `AdrIndexConsistencyTest` — zero new dependencies, follows a pattern this repo already uses and trusts, but it means parsing Java source as text, which is brittle against formatting (a multi-line annotation, an unusual attribute order).
  • Checkstyle regex — cheapest of the three, already in the build, but the least expressive and the worst failure messages.
  • Do nothing and rely on the rule file addition alone — the null option, and it deserves an honest hearing: the rule addition alone may be enough now that the mandate is where agents actually read it. The counter-argument is that the same claim was true of ADR-013 and it did not hold.

Explicitly out of scope

Startup validation of `eop.features.` values.* @security-auditor argued against this during EOP-48, not merely deferred it, and that reasoning should be respected rather than relitigated here. The remaining failure modes after havingValue = "true" — an operator writing on/yes/1, or misspelling the key — all fail closed and are loud (the feature is visibly absent within seconds of the restart the flag requires anyway). A validator would convert a self-announcing operability annoyance into a boot crash, which in an incident is strictly worse. It would also need to enumerate every flag by name, creating a second register that can drift — a new instance of the very defect class it is meant to guard against. And @ConditionalOnProperty is evaluated before any @ConfigurationProperties bean is bound, so a @Validated properties class cannot govern these keys at all; it could only observe them afterwards and throw.

Acceptance criteria

  • An ADR exists recording the decision, the alternatives above, and the trade-off accepted.
  • A build-failing check asserts every @ConditionalOnProperty in src/main/ carries havingValue = "true".
  • The check is proven to fail: demonstrate it against a deliberately loosened annotation, and record the actual failure output in the PR. A check that has only ever been seen passing is not evidence.
  • .opencode/rules/feature-flags.md carries the rule.
  • If the second half of the mandate (bean-level repetition) is not mechanically checkable, the ADR says so and says why.
  • ./mvnw verify green.

Related

  • ADR-013 (feature flags) — carries the mandate and, since 50850d1, the strengthened two-sentence form.
  • EOP-48 — the second violation, and the source of the bytecode analysis above.

*Delivered on PR 118(https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/118)* — branch eop-50-having-value-build-enforcement, three commits (322455d → a03a522 → a4a4462), awaiting human approval.

Acceptance criteria

Criterion Status
An ADR exists recording the decision, the alternatives, and the trade-off accepted ✅ ADR-052, all four alternatives weighed
A build-failing check asserts every @ConditionalOnProperty in src/main/ carries havingValue = "true" ✅ ConditionalOnPropertyHavingValueTest
The check is proven to fail, with the actual output recorded in the PR ✅ three deliberately loosened sites, verbatim output in the PR body
.opencode/rules/feature-flags.md carries the rule ✅ inserted as bullet 2, your verbatim wording plus the enforcement asymmetry
If bean-level repetition is not mechanically checkable, the ADR says so and why ✅ ADR-052 states it openly, with the three reasons
./mvnw verify green ✅ BUILD SUCCESS, 1289 tests, 0 failures

Mechanism

Spring's own ASM metadata reader (SimpleMetadataReaderFactory over a FileSystemResource per .class file, walking target/classes with Files.walk) — zero new dependencies, since spring-core is already on the test classpath. Because it reads bytecode rather than source text, annotation defaults are applied: an omitted havingValue reads back as "" and is caught by the same positive comparison against "true", and no formatting, attribute order or line wrapping can defeat it. This is what sank the docs-style text-parsing alternative. ArchUnit was a close call, rejected as a new dependency for what spring-core already does, and noted in the ADR as the natural upgrade if a second architectural invariant ever needs enforcing.

Two corrections to the ticket's own framing

  1. The "eleven sites" baseline is stale. There are 21 on origin/main (6 class-level + 15 method-level in UseCaseConfiguration), across three flags — trick-play and game-over both landed after this ticket was filed on 2026-08-14. All 21 already comply, so the gate is preventive: it fixes no live defect and locks in a property the code already has.
  2. A second invariant was added during this story's own review round. @security-auditor rejected the first implementation with a BLOCKER: a site written havingValue = "true", matchIfMissing = true satisfies the ADR-013 mandate to the letter while enabling the feature whenever the property is absent — inverting the fail-closed default, and needing no operator action at all to fire, which is worse in that one respect than a loose havingValue. This does not contradict EOP-48's finding that matchIfMissing "already defaults false"; it qualifies it to the loose form, since a default is not a prohibition and a later commit can override one. The gate now asserts both invariants separately, and their independence was verified empirically — loosening matchIfMissing fails 1 of 4 tests, leaving the havingValue assertion passing.

On @architecture-guardian's MAJOR, the prohibition is recorded in ADR-013 (dated 2026-08-23 amendment) rather than ADR-052, so the whole flag mandate reads in one place; ADR-052 owns the mechanism for both invariants.

Out of scope, as the ticket directed

Startup validation of eop.features.* values was *not implemented. @security-auditor's EOP-48 reasoning was respected, not relitigated.

Honest limits

  • The gate is preventive, not corrective.
  • Only the first half of the strengthened ADR-013 mandate is mechanised. Bean-level repetition remains reviewer-enforced — @architecture-guardian agreed it is not mechanically checkable: "opens or mutates the flagged state" is a semantic judgement no signature encodes, the carve-outs are justified in unparseable javadoc prose, and mechanising it would recreate the drift-prone per-flag bean register that EOP-48's security analysis rejected.
  • No src/main/ file was touched.

@tester-unit-and-quality · @tester-api · @security-auditor (approved on re-dispatch, BLOCKER closed) · @code-reviewer (Warning closed) · @architecture-guardian (MAJOR closed). Both above-NIT findings were remediated and the raising agents re-dispatched, rather than downgraded to caveats.

Raised by the @tester-api Definition-of-Done gate on EOP-26 (severity [MINOR]).

Finding

ForwardedForThrottleBypassIntegrationTest.java:43-45 states in the class Javadoc that "each nested class carries its own @SpringBootTest with a dedicated in-memory database". That claim is false for one of the three nested classes.

Nested class Dedicated spring.datasource.url
RotationAttackBlocked (line 86) yes — bypass-test
PerAddressIsolationUnderTrustedProxy (line 196) yes — isolation-test
HeaderHonouredFromTrustedProxy (line 133) no

HeaderHonouredFromTrustedProxy sets only eop.web.trusted-proxies=127.0.0.1/32 and relies on @DirtiesContext(BEFORE_CLASS) alone for InMemoryJoinAttemptLimiter isolation.

Why it matters

A dedicated datasource URL makes the Spring context cache key unique, which guarantees a separate limiter singleton. @DirtiesContext(BEFORE_CLASS) only clears whatever context was cached — it does not stop a future test class with the same cache key (no datasource override, no trusted-proxies) from sharing one. The isolation is weaker than the two sibling classes and weaker than the Javadoc asserts.

This matters more than a normal flakiness risk on this particular story: EOP-26's own history is that the integration suite's freshAddress() helper had been deriving its per-test throttle isolation from the vulnerability being fixed, so a green build was evidence the bug was still present. Throttle-test isolation resting on inference rather than on a guarantee is exactly the failure mode that story already produced once.

Current state

The test passes in isolation and in the full suite — verified by the gate across four runs. This is not a live failure; it is an isolation mechanism that does not match its stated contract.

Acceptance criteria

  • HeaderHonouredFromTrustedProxy gets its own spring.datasource.url (e.g. jdbc:h2:mem:honoured-test), matching the pattern of the other two nested classes.
  • Prefer fixing the code over correcting the Javadoc, since the datasource-URL approach is the proven pattern here. If the Javadoc is amended instead, it must describe what the code actually does.
  • Full suite still green, and the class still passes in isolation.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by the @tester-api Definition-of-Done gate on EOP-26 as the one API-boundary gap not covered by any existing ticket (EOP-43, EOP-44 and EOP-45 cover the others).

Finding

ADR-021 limitation 4 records that the deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 form ::10.0.0.1 canonicalises to a different string than 10.0.0.1, and therefore lands in a different throttle bucket. The limitation is real and the ADR is honest about it.

The ADR argues it is unreachable in the shipped configuration: nothing in the request path generates that form, and the header is read only from an allow-listed proxy writing a socket address into it. That reasoning is accepted — the gate did not dispute it, and this ticket is not a security fix.

The actual gap

The limitation is documented but not machine-pinned. No test asserts that IpLiterals.canonical("::10.0.0.1") and IpLiterals.canonical("10.0.0.1") currently produce different strings.

Consequence: a future refactor — and EOP-45 is precisely such a refactor, extracting an IP value object out of IpLiterals — could "helpfully" fold the compatible form onto the mapped form and thereby change bucket semantics with nothing going red. The change might even be correct, but it would be accidental, and the ADR's unreachability argument would silently stop matching the code it describes.

Note the mapped form ::ffff:10.0.0.1 is tested and does fold correctly, which makes the asymmetry easy to mistake for a bug and "fix" without reading ADR-021.

Acceptance criteria

  • A test asserts the current two-bucket behaviour for ::10.0.0.1 versus 10.0.0.1, so the limitation is visible in the suite rather than only in the ADR.
  • The test names ADR-021 limitation 4 in its @DisplayName or Javadoc, so anyone who makes it fail knows they are changing a documented decision and must amend the ADR.
  • Do not change the canonicalisation behaviour under this ticket. Pinning the limitation and changing it are separate decisions; changing it needs an ADR amendment first.
  • Sequence this before EOP-45, or the refactor it is meant to protect will land unprotected.

Raised by the @tester-api Definition-of-Done gate on EOP-26 (output 6, ranked coverage-gap list). These are the gaps that are not already covered by EOP-43 (gap 1, 0.0.0.0/0 rejection) or by EOP-52 (gap 2, IPv4-compatible IPv6 pinning).

All of them are boundary inputs that reach TrustedProxies or ClientAddressResolver. None is a live defect; each is an untested path.

Gaps, in the gate's priority order

1. Malformed `trusted-proxies` fails startup — unit-tested only, never integration-tested. TrustedProxiesTest.InvalidEntries proves TrustedProxies.of() throws IllegalArgumentException for a bad entry. Nothing proves that a bad entry in configuration actually fails the Spring context. Add @SpringBootTest(properties = "eop.web.trusted-proxies=not-an-ip") asserting startup failure.

This is the difference between the parser rejecting bad input and the application refusing to boot misconfigured. It matters because of an asymmetry specific to this control: a security allow-list that silently degraded to empty on a typo would fail closed, which is safe — but an empty allow-list is also the correct default, so the misconfigured state is indistinguishable from correct operation. Nobody would notice the proxy configuration had stopped taking effect.

2. IPv6 CIDR with a non-/128 prefix is untested. TrustedProxiesTest.CidrEntries covers IPv4 bit arithmetic thoroughly (boundary, broadcast, /0, /32) and has exactly one IPv6 case — ::1/128 at TrustedProxiesTest.java:179, which is a single-address prefix and therefore exercises no masking at all. Add a genuine 16-byte masking case such as fe80::/10. @code-reviewer independently verified the IPv4 sign-extension arithmetic on this story; the IPv6 masking path has had neither that scrutiny nor a test.

3. Forwarded chain with non-literal intermediate entries. ClientAddressResolverTest.java:208 covers a three-hop chain of valid literals. A chain like unknown, 203.0.113.1 — where the last entry is still a valid literal — is untested. Real proxies do emit unknown.

4. Whitespace around forwarded entries, end to end. ClientAddressResolver.forwardedFor splits on , and relies on the candidate.strip() inside IpLiterals.parse (line 62) to tolerate , 203.0.113.1. That strip is load-bearing for essentially every multi-entry header in existence, and it is currently exercised only incidentally. Add a case with spaces around the last entry.

5. Mapped-form forwarded value against an existing bucket. ClientAddressResolverTest.java:187 covers mapped-versus-plain canonicalisation for the peer address. The same equivalence for a forwarded value — a trusted proxy writing ::ffff:203.0.113.1 when 203.0.113.1 already has a bucket — is untested. This is the bucket-splitting concern applied to the header rather than to the socket.

Acceptance criteria

  • A test for each of the five gaps above, at the layer named in each.
  • The startup-failure test asserts Spring context failure, not merely a thrown exception from a direct constructor call.
  • Full suite green; no reduction in JaCoCo coverage.
  • If any gap turns out to be a real defect rather than a test gap, split it into its own ticket rather than fixing it silently here.

Found by @security-auditor while reviewing EOP-17. Pre-existing; not introduced by EOP-17.

GlobalExceptionHandler.java:224 sets problem.setDetail(exception.getMessage()), and SessionFullException.java:26 builds that message as:

super("Session " + sessionId + " already seats the maximum of " + capacity + " players");

So the 409 body reads "Session 3f2a…-… already seats the maximum of 6 players". A caller joining a lobby supplies only a join code and never holds the session UUID, so this hands them an internal identifier — exactly the disclosure EOP-17 was written to avoid, already realised by a sibling 409 on the very same join endpoint.

Fix: retrofit the shape EOP-17 established in handleSeatAlreadyTaken — a fixed detail string, exception.getMessage() deliberately unread. ADR-023 names this shape ("the shape to follow is handleUnknownJoinCode: fixed strings, the exception's own message deliberately unused").

Definition of Done: detail is a compile-time literal naming neither session id nor capacity; a test asserts the detail does not contain the session UUID; appended to shouldNeverLeakACredential; ./mvnw verify green.

Must be fixed before the eop.features.session-lifecycle flag flips (EOP-25).

renderedFields.description:
Found by @security-auditor while reviewing EOP-17. Pre-existing; not introduced by EOP-17.

CreateSessionUseCase has no JoinAttemptLimiter or equivalent — the limiter guards only the join path. An anonymous caller can therefore create lobbies at full request rate, giving unbounded row growth in game_session with no control in front of it.

It also matters for the mapping EOP-17 just added. handleJoinCodeUnavailable logs at WARN with the throwable, and that choice is justified by the path being non-provokable. That non-provokability currently rests on collision probability alone — roughly (N / 2^30)^5 for N live lobbies, given MAXIMUM_CODE_ATTEMPTS = 5 — and not on any rate limit. Sound against the code as it stands, but undefended if the attempt budget, the alphabet or the code length ever changes.

Fix: apply a limiter to the create path, keyed on client address (the ClientAddressResolver and InMemoryJoinAttemptLimiter machinery already exists). Note JoinAttemptLimiter's documented decision to count only failures does not transfer: on create there is no failure to count, so this needs a rate limit on successes, which is a different policy and deserves its own ADR paragraph.

Definition of Done: create path is rate-limited; a test asserts the limit fires; the 503's log-level justification is updated to cite the control rather than only the arithmetic; ./mvnw verify green.

Should be resolved before the eop.features.session-lifecycle flag flips (EOP-25).

Delivered in PR #116 (branch eop-56-503-log-level-justification, commit c2e9c8b). Two corrections to this ticket are worth recording before the summary, because both would cause harm if copied forward.

1. Three of the four acceptance criteria were already met when this ticket was written

The rate limit shipped under EOP-19 (commit 963a10b, 2026-08-15), which this ticket does not reference. That commit added SessionCreationLimiter (port), InMemorySessionCreationLimiter (sliding window, 5 creations per address per 60s, fail-closed on saturation), RateLimitedException → 429, and ADR-033.

So against the stated Definition of Done:

Criterion Status
The create path is rate-limited Already done — EOP-19
A test asserts the limit fires Already done — 19 unit tests in InMemorySessionCreationLimiterTest, plus SessionControllerIntegrationTest.ThrottlingCreation asserting 429 + Retry-After
The 503's log-level justification cites the control Delivered here
./mvnw verify green Delivered here — 1285 tests, 0 failures

The ticket also said the success-vs-failure counting policy "deserves its own ADR paragraph". ADR-033 already carries it, under the heading "Why successes are counted, not failures."

The premise in the ticket body — that `CreateSessionUseCase` has no limiter, so anonymous callers create lobbies at full rate — was already false when the ticket was filed. Worth knowing for any sibling ticket raised in the same review pass.

2. The ticket's arithmetic understates the keyspace by a factor of 1024

The body states the collision probability as roughly (N / 2^30)^5. The exponent is right; the base is not.

JoinCode.ALPHABET is 32 characters (Crockford base32) and JoinCode.LENGTH is 8, so the code space is 32⁸ = *2⁴⁰* = 1,099,511,627,776 — forty bits, not thirty. The correct expression is (N / 2^40)^5. ADR-019's "finite and forty bits wide" was always correct.

This matters beyond pedantry: thirty bits was the superseded six-character width, retired by EOP-24 precisely because it was enumerable by a distributed attacker. Quoting 2^30 as current reads as though that decision had never been taken. The figure is now derived from the constants by a build gate rather than restated, so the ticket's version cannot be copied back in.

What shipped

The justification now rests on a control. SessionController consults the limiter before CreateSessionUseCase.execute, so every request reaching the join-code retry loop has already passed it. The rate at which the WARN-with-stack-trace can be driven is bounded by the configured per-address allowance and by the limiter's 10,000-key ceiling, which fails closed on an unrecognised address. The arithmetic is why an occurrence is evidence worth logging; the limiter is why it cannot become a flood, and it is the half that survives a change to the attempt budget, the alphabet or the code length — which is exactly the fragility this ticket raised.

A build gate keeps the arithmetic honest. JoinCodeSpaceClaimsTest derives the width from the two constants and fails if a live claim stops quoting it, over two layers: three phrase-anchored checks on the sentences whose argument depends on the figure, and a sweep of every .java, .md and .yml file under src/main/java, docs/architecture, docs/adr and docs/api, requiring each English-word bit figure to equal the derived width or sit on a seven-entry allowlist of deliberately historical mentions that fails in both directions. With LENGTH temporarily set to 7 it enumerates 27 stale sites — the hand-audit EOP-24 performed, now printed by the build.

Changed: GlobalExceptionHandler (Javadoc only), docs/adr/ADR-019-session-lifecycle-and-join-codes.md (new dated amendment), CHANGELOG.md, and the new test. No behaviour changed — status, Retry-After and log level are as EOP-17 left them.

Limits, stated rather than implied

  • The gate pins two of three constants. MAXIMUM_CODE_ATTEMPTS is private to CreateSessionUseCase and reachable only by reflection, so the attempt budget stays a reviewer's concern.
  • It verifies that prose and constants agree, never that forty bits is adequate. That judgement stays in ADR-019.
  • It reads English number words only, so 2^40 or 40 bits passes unexamined, and the allowlist is keyed on filename plus number word rather than on a passage — so a file legitimately quoting the superseded "thirty bits" would also tolerate a second, genuinely stale mention beside it. Narrowing that key is the named next move.
  • The limiter is keyed per address while the occupied fraction of the code space is global, so it bounds the rate of this log line and not the number of live lobbies. Stated in the ADR rather than collapsed.

Review

All five Definition-of-Done gates approved the shipping tree. Two findings changed the work materially rather than being noted and waved through: @tester-api found that docs/api/openapi.yml states the width three times and sat outside the sweep's roots — closed rather than deferred, since a contract is what a client integrates against — and @code-reviewer rejected an earlier revision over four blockers, including a miscount in the very prose announcing this fix. Both are recorded in ADR-019 and the changelog rather than quietly corrected.

This ticket blocks EOP-25, which is already Done, so no downstream work is waiting on it.

renderedFields.description:
Found by @security-auditor while reviewing EOP-17. Pre-existing.

.opencode/rules/observability.md mandates "Structured JSON output via Logback (logback-spring.xml) for production profiles" and an MDC correlation id on every line. Verified first-hand:

  • find . -name "logback*" (excluding target/, .git/) returns nothing — no logback-spring.xml anywhere in the repo.
  • No logging.level.* key in application.yml, application-prod.yml, or src/test/resources/application.properties.

Production therefore runs at Spring Boot's default INFO with plain-text output, not the structured JSON the rules promise, and with no correlation id.

Why this surfaced now: it is what makes EOP-17's new LOG.debug("Seat {} in session {} …") line safe — the DEBUG event is never written in production. Corroborated empirically: GlobalExceptionHandlerTest cannot observe the event without calling logger.setLevel(Level.DEBUG) itself. But that safety is incidental, not designed: an operator raising the root level to DEBUG while troubleshooting would begin writing internal session UUIDs to the log.

Definition of Done: logback-spring.xml exists with structured JSON for the prod profile and an X-Correlation-Id → MDC filter; explicit level configuration so the DEBUG line's suppression is a decision rather than a default; a note beside that DEBUG call recording the coupling; ./mvnw verify green.

docs/architecture/runtime-view.md:357 reads:

SC-->>P2: 201 sessionId, identityToken, seatOrder

But SessionController.joinSession returns a bare SessionAdmissionDto with no @ResponseStatus, so Spring answers 200. Two independent sources agree against the diagram: docs/api/openapi.yml declares '200' on {{POST /api/v1/sessions/

{joinCode}

/players}}, and SessionContentionIntegrationTest asserts status().isOk().

Fix: 201 → 200 on that line.

Also worth folding into the same commit, both raised as NITs on EOP-17:

  1. JoinSessionUseCase.java:34-37 and GlobalExceptionHandler's new handleSeatAlreadyTaken Javadoc give mildly contradictory accounts ~700 lines apart — the former says a joiner "can lose the race for a seat at most five times before the table is full", the latter that a caller "can provoke this at will". Both are true (the fullness check reads a stale snapshot), but one clause noting that heavy concurrency defeats the fullness check would settle it.
  2. MAXIMUM_SEAT_ATTEMPTS = 8 (JoinSessionUseCase.java:39) exceeding GameSession.MAXIMUM_PLAYERS = 6, with no seat-vacating method on SessionRepository, is what makes SeatAlreadyTakenException effectively unreachable over HTTP. That attempts > capacity relationship is an unwritten invariant and deserves a comment or an assertion — lowering the budget below 6, or adding a leave-lobby feature, would make the path live.

Definition of Done: the status is correct, the two Javadocs agree, the invariant is written down; ./mvnw verify green.

comments.body:
Delivered on main as merge commit 2b65d52 (PR #99, squash-free merge of e33e9a3).

All three deliverables discharged

  1. Status fix. docs/architecture/runtime-view.md:536 now reads SC-->>P2: 200 sessionId, identityToken, seatOrder. Verified against production rather than against the ticket: SessionController.java:151-160 is a @PostMapping returning a bare SessionAdmissionDto with no @ResponseStatus, so Spring answers 200 — and docs/api/openapi.yml:185-229 and four integration-test helpers already agreed. Swept the rest of docs/architecture/ for the same defect: the two remaining 201}}s ({{runtime-view.md:481 for createSession, C4-Diagrams.md:516 for POST /plays) are both correct and were left alone. No third site.
  2. Javadoc contradiction reconciled. Both JoinSessionUseCase.MAXIMUM_SEAT_ATTEMPTS (lines 45-51) and GlobalExceptionHandler.handleSeatAlreadyTaken (lines 841-848) now carry the clause the ticket asked for — that GameSession.join's fullness check reads the snapshot taken at the top of the attempt, so heavy concurrency defeats it — and each names the other, which is what closes a ~700-line separation. The handler's "provoke this at will" wording was deliberately kept: handleJoinCodeUnavailable twenty lines below draws an explicit contrast against it.
  3. Invariant written down — and enforced. MAXIMUM_SEAT_ATTEMPTS is now GameSession.MAXIMUM_PLAYERS + 2 (same value, 8), following the precedent at SseSessionEventPublisher.java:70. Plus explicit Javadoc naming the negative condition — SessionRepository deliberately offers no seat-vacating method, verified: nine methods, none of them removes a player — and a new test, JoinSessionUseCaseTest.shouldBudgetMoreAttemptsThanTheTableHasSeats, asserting the relationship. An assertion rather than a runtime guard, per ADR-006's anti-vacuity lesson.

Five files, 51 insertions, 7 deletions: docs/architecture/runtime-view.md, JoinSessionUseCase.java, GlobalExceptionHandler.java, JoinSessionUseCaseTest.java, CHANGELOG.md. No version bump — documentation and Javadoc only, no behavioural change ships.

Definition of Done — five gates, all APPROVE

Each gate re-ran the build itself rather than taking it on report.

Gate Verdict Highest finding
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE none
@tester-api APPROVE MINOR (pre-existing)
@security-auditor APPROVE INFO ×4
@code-reviewer APPROVE Warning ×1
@architecture-guardian APPROVE MINOR ×4

./mvnw verify → BUILD SUCCESS; Tests run: 1250, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0; Checkstyle 0 violations; SpotBugs BugInstance size is 0; JaCoCo All coverage checks have been met. New test confirmed executed at target/surefire-reports/TEST-org.maglez.eop.usecase.JoinSessionUseCaseTest.xml:73. All five documentation-integrity gates green, including MermaidSequenceTextTest on the very label this commit edits. CI on PR #99: build pass 1m19s, ui pass 45s, image pass 1m59s.

Two rulings worth recording. @architecture-guardian — the gate that filed this ticket — ruled explicitly that no ADR is required: nothing was decided here, and ADR-020-session-concurrency-control.md:130-137 already owns the underlying decision and carries no stale budget claim, so docs/adr/README.md needs no change either. @security-auditor proved from the schema that the race is bounded by uq_player_session_seat plus chk_player_seat_order CHECK BETWEEN 0 AND 5 — a database-level pigeonhole — not by the stale check, so the newly-documented behaviour is a latency artefact and not a vulnerability. It also corrected the worst-case cost upward: ~24 DB statements per contested join, not 8.

Findings filed rather than accepted

The commit was merged exactly as approved — amending files after sign-off would have invalidated all five approvals for the commit actually merged. Every MINOR/INFO/Warning went to the backlog instead:

  • EOP-112 — derive or guard the literal "eight" seat attempts in runtime-view.md:525 and SessionContentionIntegrationTest:43
  • EOP-113 — the 409 title "The lobby filled while you were joining" asserts a fullness that need not hold (a real API-contract change, out of scope for a docs ticket)

  • EOP-118 — housekeeping: ADR-006 citation siting, CHANGELOG/pom version mismatch, + 2 margin rationale

Scope

fields.summary: Game Screen UI: play a trick from the browser

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a player in an active EoP session

I want to see my hand of cards around a shared table, drag a card to the central area to play it, and be told who won each trick

So that I can participate in a full game of Elevation of Privilege from my browser without needing a physical deck

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: EOP-59 — Game Screen UI: play a trick from the browser
  • Target Persona: Any player (facilitator or participant) in a session that has moved from LOBBY to IN_PROGRESS
  • Value Proposition: Completes the browser-playable loop — the backend game engine (EOP-14, EOP-15) is fully built; this story surfaces it in the UI

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag Name: eop.features.game-screen — boolean, default false
  • Vite env var: VITE_GAME_SCREEN_ENABLED=true mirrors the backend flag for the front-end build
  • Deployment Behaviour: Merged to main with flag OFF. The LobbyScreen already shows a "The game has started" warning when session.status === 'IN_PROGRESS'; with the flag OFF that warning remains and no game screen is rendered.
  • Release Condition: Enable flag once all Acceptance Criteria pass and @product-owner approves release.

Screen Layout

The game screen is a virtual table view:

  • Central area — the trick zone: cards played in the current trick are displayed face-up here, one per player who has played so far. Labelled "Current trick".
  • Bottom of screen — the current player's own hand: cards face-up, player's display name above the hand, cards arranged horizontally.
  • Remaining seats — other players arranged around the table (top, left, right, depending on seat order relative to the current player): cards face-down (backs only), player's display name above their stack, card count shown (e.g. "7 cards").
  • Seat layout adapts to player count (3–6): positions are distributed evenly around the central area.

Card Interaction

  • Drag-and-drop (pointer and touch): a player drags a card from their hand and drops it onto the central trick area to play it.
  • Keyboard / click fallback (WCAG 2.2 AA): clicking a card selects it (highlighted border); a "Play selected card" button then appears and submits the play. This is the accessible equivalent — not a separate story.
  • Touch screens: drag-and-drop uses pointer events so it works on tablets and phones.
  • Out-of-turn state: when it is not the current player's turn, all cards in their hand are visually disabled (reduced opacity, aria-disabled="true", not draggable, not selectable). An aria-live region announces whose turn it is.

Trick Winner Announcement

  • After all players have played and the trick is resolved server-side, a banner / modal overlay appears: "Trick won by [display name]" with the winning card shown.
  • The announcement is dismissible by the trick winner (who clicks "Start next trick") or auto-dismissed after 5 seconds, whichever comes first.
  • The winner's action opens the next trick via POST /api/v1/tricks.
  • The announcement is announced to screen readers via role="alert".

Real-Time Updates

  • The game screen subscribes to {{GET /api/v1/sessions/ {id}/events}} (SSE doorbell, same pattern as LobbyScreen).
    * On each SSE event, the screen re-fetches trick state (GET /api/v1/tricks/current) and session state ({{GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}

    }}).

  • Other players' played cards appear in the central area in real time as SSE events arrive.

API Endpoints Used

Action Endpoint
Read own hand {{GET /api/v1/sessions/ {id}/hand}}|
|Get current trick state|GET /api/v1/tricks/current (or equivalent)|
|Play a card|POST /api/v1/tricks/{trickId}/plays}}|
|Resolve trick|{{POST /api/v1/tricks/{trickId}/resolve (facilitator)|
|Subscribe to events|{{GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}

/events}} (SSE)

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD)

Scenario 1: Player sees the game screen when the session is IN_PROGRESS (flag ON)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.game-screen is ON (VITE_GAME_SCREEN_ENABLED=true)
  • And the player is in a session with status IN_PROGRESS
  • When the App component evaluates the current view
  • Then the GameScreen component is rendered instead of the lobby warning
  • And the player's display name is shown above their hand
  • And other players' names are shown above their face-down card stacks

Scenario 2: Player plays a card by drag-and-drop on their turn

  • Given it is the current player's turn (they are the leading seat or the next in clockwise order)
  • And the player's cards are enabled (not aria-disabled)
  • When the player drags a card from their hand and drops it onto the central trick area
  • Then {{POST /api/v1/tricks/ {trickId}/plays}} is called with the correct cardId and playerToken
    * And the played card moves to the central area
    * And the card is removed from the player's hand

    h3. Scenario 3: Player plays a card by keyboard (WCAG fallback)

    * Given it is the current player's turn
    * When the player clicks a card (or focuses it and presses Enter/Space)
    * Then the card is highlighted with a visible selection indicator
    * And a "Play selected card" button becomes visible
    * When the player activates the "Play selected card" button
    * Then the same {{POST /api/v1/tricks/{trickId}

    /plays}} call is made

Scenario 4: Cards are disabled when it is not the player's turn

  • Given it is another player's turn
  • When the game screen renders
  • Then all cards in the current player's hand have aria-disabled="true"
  • And the cards are not draggable
  • And an aria-live region announces "[Player name]'s turn"

Scenario 5: Trick winner announcement

  • Given all players have played a card in the current trick
  • And the trick has been resolved server-side
  • When the SSE doorbell fires and the screen re-fetches trick state
  • Then a role="alert" banner appears: "Trick won by [winner display name]"
  • And the winning card is displayed in the banner
  • And the trick winner sees a "Start next trick" button
  • And the banner auto-dismisses after 5 seconds if not manually dismissed

Scenario 6: Default fallback (flag OFF)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.game-screen is OFF
  • Then the GameScreen component bean is absent from the application context
  • And a player whose session moves to IN_PROGRESS sees the existing lobby warning: "The game has started"
  • And no game screen route or component is reachable

Scenario 7: Touch screen drag-and-drop

  • Given the player is on a touch device
  • When the player long-presses a card and drags it to the central trick area
  • Then the card play is submitted identically to the pointer drag-and-drop path

Definition of Done

  • UI designs conform to GOV.UK Design System and WCAG 2.2 AA (keyboard navigation, aria-disabled, aria-live, role="alert", colour contrast).
  • Drag-and-drop implemented with pointer events (works on touch and mouse).
  • Keyboard / click-to-select fallback implemented in the same component.
  • Sub-second unit tests written for GameScreen, card selection state, and trick winner banner.
  • API contract verified: {{GET /api/v1/sessions/ {id}

renderedFields.description:
⚠️ Nice-to-Have — Low Priority

This story is explicitly marked nice-to-have. It must not block delivery of EOP-60 (the core game screen). Pick it up only after EOP-60 is live and stable.

User Story

As a player joining or already in an EoP session

I want to choose an avatar from a set of illustrations provided by the product owner

So that I am visually distinguishable from other players at the table without needing to type anything extra

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: EOP-59 — Game Screen UI: play a trick from the browser
  • Depends on: EOP-60 (game screen must exist before avatars are displayed there)
  • Target Persona: Any player who wants a richer visual identity at the table
  • Value Proposition: Adds personality and makes it easier to track who is who around the virtual table

Constraints

  • Avatar set is PO-supplied. The product owner will provide the image assets (format, dimensions, and count TBD at time of pickup). Do not design or source avatars — wait for the assets.
  • Selection point: avatar is chosen during the join / create flow (before entering the lobby), or on a dedicated "Edit profile" step. Exact placement to be confirmed with PO at pickup.
  • Storage: avatar choice is stored server-side against the player record. A new avatarId field is added to Player and returned in PlayerDto. A Liquibase changeset adds the nullable column.
  • Default: if no avatar is chosen, a deterministic fallback is shown (e.g. initials on a coloured background derived from the player's seat order). The fallback must not require a network call.
  • GOV.UK / WCAG 2.2 AA: each avatar option must have a descriptive alt text. The selection control must be keyboard-navigable (radio group or equivalent).

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag Name: eop.features.player-avatar-selection — boolean, default false
  • Deployment Behaviour: Merged to main with flag OFF. Avatar selection UI is hidden; all players show the initials fallback.
  • Release Condition: Enable flag once all Acceptance Criteria pass, PO has supplied and approved the avatar assets, and @product-owner approves release.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD)

Scenario 1: Player selects an avatar during join (flag ON)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.player-avatar-selection is ON
  • When a player creates or joins a session
  • Then an avatar selection step is presented showing the PO-supplied illustrations
  • And each avatar has a visible label and descriptive alt text
  • And the player can navigate and select an avatar by keyboard
  • When the player confirms their choice
  • Then the selected avatarId is persisted server-side
  • And the player's avatar is shown above their hand on the game screen (EOP-60)

Scenario 2: Avatar shown next to other players' card backs

  • Given a session is IN_PROGRESS and all players have chosen avatars
  • When the game screen renders
  • Then each player's avatar is displayed above their face-down card stack alongside their display name

Scenario 3: Initials fallback when no avatar is chosen

  • Given a player has not selected an avatar (or the flag is OFF)
  • When the game screen renders
  • Then the player's initials are shown on a coloured background in place of an avatar
  • And no network request is made to fetch an avatar image

Scenario 4: Default fallback (flag OFF)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.player-avatar-selection is OFF
  • Then the avatar selection step is absent from the join / create flow
  • And all players display the initials fallback
  • And the eop.features.player-avatar-selection bean is absent from the application context

Definition of Done

  • PO has supplied avatar assets before implementation begins.
  • avatarId nullable column added via Liquibase changeset with rollback.
  • PlayerDto updated to include avatarId (nullable).
  • Avatar selection UI is keyboard-navigable and WCAG 2.2 AA compliant.
  • Initials fallback renders without a network call.
  • Feature flag documented in application.yml and ADR-013.
  • Unit tests for avatar selection state and initials fallback.
  • All child Bug Sub-tasks resolved and verified green.

⚠️ Nice-to-Have — Lowest Priority

This story is explicitly marked nice-to-have and is the lowest-priority item in the game screen epic. It must not be picked up until EOP-60 (core game screen) and EOP-61 (PO-supplied avatar selection) are both live and stable. Details are intentionally deferred — do not refine this story until it is actively scheduled.

User Story

As a player joining an EoP session

I want to upload my own image as my avatar

So that I can use a personal photo or illustration to represent myself at the virtual table

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: EOP-59 — Game Screen UI: play a trick from the browser
  • Depends on: EOP-61 (avatar infrastructure — avatarId column, PlayerDto field, and selection UI — must exist first)
  • Target Persona: A player who wants a fully personalised identity at the table
  • Value Proposition: Maximum personalisation; reduces friction for teams who already have profile photos

Intentionally Deferred Details

The following must be agreed with the PO at the time this story is scheduled, not now:

  • Accepted file types (e.g. JPEG, PNG, WebP only)
  • Maximum file size
  • Image dimensions / cropping behaviour
  • Moderation policy (none, manual, automated)
  • Storage location (local filesystem, object store, CDN)
  • Whether uploaded avatars are session-scoped (discarded after session ends) or persistent per player identity

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag Name: eop.features.player-avatar-upload — boolean, default false
  • Deployment Behaviour: Merged to main with flag OFF. Upload UI is hidden; players fall back to the PO-supplied avatar set (EOP-61) or initials fallback.
  • Release Condition: Enable flag only after PO has agreed all deferred details above and all Acceptance Criteria pass.

Acceptance Criteria (Placeholder — to be refined at scheduling)

Scenario 1: Player uploads a custom avatar (flag ON)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.player-avatar-upload is ON
  • When a player creates or joins a session
  • Then an "Upload your own avatar" option is available alongside the PO-supplied set
  • And the upload control accepts only the agreed file types and enforces the agreed size limit
  • And the uploaded image is cropped / resized to the agreed dimensions
  • And the avatar is stored and returned in PlayerDto.avatarId (or equivalent)

Scenario 2: Default fallback (flag OFF)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.player-avatar-upload is OFF
  • Then the upload option is absent from the join / create flow
  • And the eop.features.player-avatar-upload bean is absent from the application context

Definition of Done (Placeholder — to be completed at scheduling)

  • All deferred details agreed with PO and recorded in this story before implementation begins.
  • File type and size validation at the API boundary (reject early, reject explicitly).
  • Uploaded image stored per agreed storage strategy.
  • WCAG 2.2 AA: upload control is keyboard-accessible with clear error messages.
  • Feature flag documented in application.yml and ADR-013.
  • Security review: no path traversal, no stored XSS via filename or EXIF, no unauthenticated upload endpoint.
  • All child Bug Sub-tasks resolved and verified green.

renderedFields.description:
Problem

Several gameplay issues found during manual testing of the trick-play flow:

  1. Opening leader rule — Hands.openingLeaderSeat() was finding the lowest Tampering card dealt, but the EoP rules say the player holding the three of Tampering leads. The 78-card seeded deck includes a two of Tampering, so the two-holder was incorrectly leading instead of the three-holder.
  1. Deal not triggered from UI — The facilitator navigating to GameScreen had no way to trigger the deal; the backend POST /deal endpoint existed but was never called from the front end.
  1. Follow-suit not enforced in UI — Players could attempt to play any card even when they held a card of the led suit. The server enforces this, but the UI gave no feedback and allowed the attempt.
  1. Auto-resolve not wired — After all players played, the trick was complete=true but nobody called POST .../resolve. Only the facilitator could resolve, and only via a button that was gated on iAmWinner.
  1. Seat comparison type coercion — JSON deserialisation sometimes produced seat values as strings (\"0\") rather than numbers, causing === comparisons to fail silently (wrong player shown as active, winner banner not shown).

Changes

  • Hands.java: openingLeaderSeat() now looks for rank == THREE && suit == TAMPERING instead of the lowest Tampering card
  • DealHandsUseCase.java: adds SLF4J logging of the opening leader seat
  • HandsTest.java, TrickPlayRepositoryAdapterIntegrationTest.java, TrickControllerIntegrationTest.java: tests updated to match the new rule
  • api.ts: adds dealDeck() function
  • GameScreen.tsx: deal-on-load (facilitator only, 409 = already dealt), follow-suit enforcement, auto-resolve useEffect (facilitator only), seat coercion with Number(), autoFocus on lobby forms
  • CreateSessionForm.tsx, JoinSessionForm.tsx: autoFocus on first input

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a player in an EoP threat modelling session

I want to see a final leaderboard when the last card is played, showing each player's score and captured threats by STRIDE category

So that I can understand who identified the most threats and reflect on the session's outcomes

As a facilitator

I want to start a new game with the same players after reviewing the results

So that the group can play another round without having to re-create the session

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: EOP-59 — Game Screen UI: play a trick from the browser
  • Target Persona: Facilitator + all players in a threat modelling workshop
  • Value Proposition: Closes the game loop — players get meaningful feedback on their performance and the facilitator can run multiple rounds in one session

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag Name: eop.features.game-over
  • Deployment Behavior: Code merged to main and continuously deployed with flag set to OFF.
  • Release Condition: Enable flag once all Acceptance Criteria pass and @product-owner approves release.

Scoring Rules

  • Every card played is a threat card worth 1 point to the player who played it (regardless of whether they win the trick).
  • The player who wins the trick earns an additional +1 point.
  • Example: 3-player trick — Player A plays Spoofing 7, Player B plays Tampering 5, Player C plays Repudiation 2. Player B wins the trick. Scores: A=1, B=2 (1 card + 1 trick win), C=1.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: Game Over screen shown to all players (Feature Enabled)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.game-over is ON
  • And all players have played all their cards (hands are empty)
  • When the last trick is resolved
  • Then all players' screens automatically transition to the Game Over screen
  • And the screen shows a leaderboard sorted by total score descending (highest first)
  • And players with equal scores share the same rank (e.g. two players on 12 points both show as rank 1)
  • And each leaderboard row shows: rank, player name, total score, and a count of captured cards per STRIDE category (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege)

Scenario 2: Facilitator sees "Start New Game" button

  • Given feature flag eop.features.game-over is ON
  • And the Game Over screen is displayed
  • When the current player is the facilitator
  • Then a "Start new game" button is visible on the Game Over screen
  • And non-facilitator players do not see this button

Scenario 3: Facilitator starts a new game

  • Given the facilitator clicks "Start new game"
  • When the server processes the request
  • Then all tricks are cleared and hands are re-dealt from the same 68-card deck
  • And the opening leader is determined by the seat holding the 3 of Tampering
  • And all players remain in their original seats with the same seat numbers
  • And all players' screens transition back to the Game Screen (trick-play view)

Scenario 4: Game history persisted

  • Given the last trick is resolved and the game ends
  • Then a record is written to the game_result table containing:
  • Session ID
  • Timestamp the game started (when the deck was first dealt)
  • Facilitator's display name
  • Each player's display name and final score
  • Timestamp the game finalised (when the last trick was resolved)

Scenario 5: Default Fallback (Feature Disabled)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.game-over is OFF
  • Then the existing game screen behaviour is unchanged (no Game Over screen, no leaderboard, no "Start new game" button)
  • And the eop.features.game-over bean is absent from the application context

Technical Notes

  • New game_result table via Liquibase changeset (new file under db/changelog/changes/)
  • Score calculation lives in the domain layer (org.maglez.eop.*) — zero Spring imports
  • Leaderboard data served via a new endpoint (contract-first: update docs/api/openapi.yml first)
  • UI: GOV.UK Design System table component for the leaderboard; WCAG 2.2 AA

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • UI designs conform to GOV.UK accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2 AA).
  • Sub-second unit tests written with high branch coverage (scoring logic, tie-breaking, leaderboard ordering).
  • API contract updated and verified with integration tests.
  • No security regressions or plaintext secrets introduced.
  • game_result Liquibase migration with rollback block.
  • Documentation updated in docs/ if applicable.
  • All child Bug Sub-tasks resolved and verified green.

User Story

As a player in an EoP threat modelling session

I want to see the real EoP card artwork when playing my hand

So that the game feels authentic and I can easily identify each threat card visually

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: EOP-59 — Game Screen UI: play a trick from the browser
  • Target Persona: All players in a threat modelling workshop
  • Value Proposition: Replaces generic coloured rectangles with the official Microsoft EoP card artwork, making the game immediately recognisable and improving the player experience

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag Name: eop.features.card-images
  • Deployment Behavior: Code merged to main and continuously deployed with flag set to OFF.
  • Release Condition: Enable flag once all Acceptance Criteria pass and @product-owner approves release.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: Player's hand shows real card images (Feature Enabled)

Summary

After the facilitator clicks "Start game", the UI calls {{POST /api/v1/sessions/

{sessionId}/start}} but never calls {{POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}

/deal}}. As a result, the game screen loads but immediately shows:

Could not load game — No hands have been dealt in session

Unknown macro: {sessionId}

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create a session as facilitator
  2. Have 2+ players join
  3. Click "Start game"
  4. Observe the error on the game screen

Expected behaviour

After start succeeds, the facilitator's client calls {{POST /api/v1/sessions/

{sessionId}

/deal}} so all players receive their hands before the game screen loads.

Root cause

LobbyScreen.handleStartGame calls startGame() but does not call dealHands(). The dealHands API function was missing from ui/src/api.ts.

Fix

  • Add dealHands(sessionId, playerToken) to ui/src/api.ts
  • Call await dealHands(sessionId, playerToken) in LobbyScreen.handleStartGame after startGame() succeeds

comments.body:
Resolved — the reported defect was already fixed; this ticket delivered the nomenclature alignment

The symptom this ticket reports is not present on `main`, and has not been since `35c3ed0` (EOP-70). That commit added both halves of the fix this ticket prescribes, in one go:

  • ui/src/api.ts gained the deal helper calling {{POST /api/v1/sessions/ {sessionId}

    /deal}}

  • LobbyScreen.handleStartGame gained the await call to it, immediately after startGame() succeeds

It was already covered by three tests in ui/src/components/LobbyScreen.test.tsx and ui/src/api.test.ts — success path, failure path and call count — all of which stub global fetch rather than spying on the module, so the ADR-045 boundary parsers are genuinely exercised.

The residual timing window is benign and tested: the SSE game-started event can mount GameScreen while the deal request is still in flight, but GameScreen absorbs the resulting 409 (HandNotDealtException) as a waiting state, and the subsequent hand-dealt event triggers a re-fetch that populates the hand. A lost race therefore degrades to "waiting", not to "Could not load game".

What this ticket did deliver

What EOP-70 did not do was agree on a name. docs/api/openapi.yml:475 declares operationId: dealHands, and both TrickController.dealHands and DealHandsUseCase carry it — three of four layers said dealHands and only the browser said dealCards. The divergence is exactly the kind that defeats grep-based archaeology, and it is what produced the wrong initial diagnosis on this very ticket.

Commit `e648cd7` — "[EOP-67] refactor: rename dealCards to dealHands to match operationId", merged to main as b6e8447 via PR #107. Eight files, +26 / −22:

  • Helper, import, call site and both Vitest suites renamed. Function body byte-identical — same route, same POST, same player-token header, still 204, still correctly parser-free per .opencode/rules/error-handling.md
  • Live prose updated in three documents: ADR-045 §4's parser roster, ADR-040's non-atomic start-then-deal limitation, and C4-Diagrams.md's parser-exemption paragraph
  • CHANGELOG.md gained a ### Changed bullet under [1.0.0-SNAPSHOT] — Unreleased
  • ADR-045's one historical mention deliberately keeps (then named dealCards — renamed by EOP-67) so a reader meeting the old name in git log has somewhere to land

No Java changed. No route, method, header, status code, response body or behaviour changed.

Verification

Gate Result
./mvnw clean verify BUILD SUCCESS — 1256 tests, 0 failures; SpotBugs 0 findings; JaCoCo all coverage checks met
cd ui && npm run verify typecheck clean, lint clean, 223 tests passing, production build ✓
CI on PR #107 build, ui, supply-chain, image — all green

All five Definition-of-Done gates returned VERDICT: APPROVE: @tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian. The architecture gate specifically upheld on the merits the decision not to amend the ADR-040 and ADR-045 status lines, on the grounds that a nomenclature alignment is not a re-decision.

Closing as Done.

Problem

The build CI job re-downloads all Maven dependencies from scratch on every run. Analysis of CI run #212 shows ./mvnw verify taking 1m 57s, almost entirely due to dependency downloads. Total pipeline time: 3m 51s.

Root Cause

No actions/cache@v4 step for ~/.m2/repository in the build job. The image job already uses GHA cache for Docker layers (39s build), but Maven deps are uncached.

Fix

Add a Maven cache step to the build job in .github/workflows/ci.yml:

- name: Cache Maven dependencies
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:     path: ~/.m2/repository
    key: ${{ runner.os }}-maven-${{ hashFiles('**/pom.xml') }}
    restore-keys: |
      ${{ runner.os }}-maven-

Expected Outcome

  • ./mvnw verify drops from ~2m to ~45–60s on cache hit
  • Total pipeline time drops from ~3m 51s to ~2m 30s
  • Cache invalidates automatically when pom.xml changes

renderedFields.description:
Problem

When the number of players does not divide evenly into the deck size (74 cards), some players receive more cards than others. For example, with 3 players: seats 0 and 1 get 25 cards, seat 2 gets 24. This is confusing and unfair.

Desired Behaviour

All players start with the same number of cards. Remainder cards are discarded (not dealt). With 3 players: each gets floor(74/3) = 24 cards, 2 cards are discarded.

Constraint

The opening-lead rule requires the lowest-ranked Tampering card to determine who leads first. The discard must not remove all Tampering cards from the dealt portion. The fix must ensure the lowest Tampering card in the shuffled deck is always in the kept portion.

Approach

  1. Compute handSize = floor(deckSize / playerCount)
  2. Compute keptSize = handSize * playerCount
  3. Find the index of the lowest-ranked Tampering card in the shuffled deck
  4. If that index is within keptSize, truncate the deck to keptSize and deal normally
  5. If that index is beyond keptSize (i.e., it would be discarded), swap it with the last card in the kept portion before truncating — this guarantees the Tampering card is always dealt

Impact

  • Hands.deal() — change distribution logic
  • Hands.openingLeaderSeat() — no change needed
  • HandsTest — update 4 existing distribution tests + add discard tests
  • ADR-023 — must be amended to document the new rule

Acceptance Criteria

  • All players receive exactly floor(deckSize / playerCount) cards
  • The lowest-ranked Tampering card is always dealt (never discarded)
  • ./mvnw verify passes
  • ADR-023 updated

Context

The physical Elevation of Privilege card game does not include Ace cards. The current implementation seeds all 78 cards (ranks 2–A for each of the 6 STRIDE suits), and the previous migration (2026-08-17--trim-deck-to-74-printed-cards.xml) removed 4 cards to reach 74. However, 6 Ace cards (one per suit, rank 14) remain in the deck and do not exist in the physical game.

What needs to change

  1. Database migration — add a new Liquibase changeset that deletes the 6 Ace rows from the card table (one per STRIDE suit). After this migration the deck holds 68 cards.
  1. `Rank` enum — remove the ACE constant (value 14, symbol "A"). KING becomes the highest rank.
  1. `Card.isOpenThreat()` — the Open Threat concept was tied to Aces. Since Aces no longer exist, remove this method and all references to it.
  1. Tests — update all tests that reference Rank.ACE, isOpenThreat(), or assert deck size of 74:
  • RankTest — update count (12 ranks), remove ACE-specific assertions
  • DeckFixture.fullDeck() — remove ACE exclusion logic; deck is now 68 cards
  • CardTest — remove isOpenThreat tests
  • HandTest, HandsTest, TrickTest, TrickPlayTest, ScoreSheetTest — replace Rank.ACE with Rank.KING or another valid rank
  • CardControllerIntegrationTest — update expected deck size and rank assertions
  • CardRepositoryAdapterIntegrationTest — remove isOpenThreat assertions
  • ResolveTrickUseCaseTest — replace Rank.ACE with a valid rank

Acceptance Criteria

  • ./mvnw verify passes with zero failures
  • Rank enum has 12 values (TWO through KING); Rank.ACE does not exist
  • Card.isOpenThreat() method is removed
  • A new Liquibase migration deletes the 6 Ace rows; deck total is 68 cards
  • DeckFixture.fullDeck() returns 68 cards
  • No test references Rank.ACE or isOpenThreat

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a developer testing the application locally

I want to run a single script that rebuilds both Docker images from the latest main code and restarts the running stack

So that I never accidentally test against a stale container that predates recent merges

Context & Business Value

CI builds and publishes images to GHCR on every push to main, but the local compose.app.yml defaults to eop-threat-medeling:local and eop-ui:local — tags that are only updated when a developer manually runs docker build. There is no mechanism that keeps those local tags in sync with main.

This gap caused a real incident: the running stack was built on Aug 17 07:25 (commit 9a90efd, EOP-68), while the database had all subsequent Liquibase migrations applied (including EOP-75's 68-card deck). The app code expected 78 cards; the database held 68. The deal failed silently, current_leader_seat was never written, seatToPlay came back undefined, and the opening player's drag was blocked by isMyTurn = false — the card snapped back with no error shown.

A one-command script eliminates this class of bug entirely for local testing.

This script is a temporary convenience. Once the project is wired up to AWS (Terraform + CD pipeline), every merge to main will deploy automatically and the local stack will no longer be the primary test target. At that point this script can be deleted.

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag Name: N/A — this is a developer tooling script, not a user-facing feature.
  • Deployment Behavior: Script lives at scripts/update-local.sh, committed to main. No application code changes.
  • Release Condition: Available immediately on merge.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: Happy path — stack is running, new code on main

  • Given the developer has pulled the latest main
  • And the local Docker stack is running (eop-app, eop-caddy, eop-postgres)
  • When the developer runs ./scripts/update-local.sh
  • Then both images are rebuilt (eop-threat-medeling:local and eop-ui:local) from the current working tree
  • And eop-app and eop-caddy are restarted with the new images (--force-recreate)
  • And eop-postgres is left untouched (data is preserved)
  • And the script exits non-zero if any step fails

Scenario 2: Script is self-documenting

  • Given a developer reads scripts/update-local.sh
  • Then a comment block at the top explains:
  • why the script exists (local :local tags are not auto-updated by CI)
  • that it rebuilds from the current working tree (not from GHCR)
  • that it will be obsolete once CD to AWS is in place

Scenario 3: Script is executable and discoverable

  • Given the script is committed to main
  • Then it has the executable bit set (chmod +x)
  • And it is referenced in README.md or CHANGELOG.md so developers know it exists

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • scripts/update-local.sh committed with executable bit, passes shellcheck
  • Comment block explains the gap and the AWS obsolescence condition
  • CHANGELOG.md updated under ## [Unreleased]
  • Script tested locally: ./scripts/update-local.sh rebuilds both images and restarts app + caddy without touching postgres
  • GET /api/v1/cards?size=1 returns totalElements:68 after running the script against the current main

Symptom

Dragging a card from the hand onto the central trick drop zone does not play the card. The card returns to the hand area and the game cannot be started.

Reported against the local Docker stack after scripts/update-local.sh, with VITE_GAME_SCREEN_ENABLED=true (EOP-78 merged, so the game screen mounts correctly).

Investigation so far

Ruled out:

  • Server side is correct. GetTrickStateUseCase falls back to handRepository.findCurrentLeaderSeat(sessionId) when no trick is open, and current_leader_seat is non-null after the deal — so seatToPlay is present at the opening lead and isMyTurn should be true for the leader.
  • {{POST /api/v1/sessions/ {id}

    /plays}} returns 201, which satisfies response.ok in api.ts.

  • The drag ghost carries pointerEvents: 'none' and cannot intercept the drop.
  • There are zero stopPropagation calls in GameScreen.tsx.
  • The drop zone is rendered unconditionally, so dropZoneRef.current is never null while the board is visible.
  • No CSS transform or scroll container that would skew getBoundingClientRect.

Root cause of the escape

ui/src/components/GameScreen.tsx registers onPointerMove / onPointerUp / onPointerCancel on <main>, and onPointerDown on the card, but the entire pointer-event play path has no test coverage. GameScreen.test.tsx contains a single drop-zone test that only asserts the zone renders. This is why the defect shipped.

Acceptance criteria

  • Dragging a card onto the trick drop zone submits the play and the card leaves the hand.
  • A regression test covers the full pointerdown → pointermove → pointerup-over-drop-zone path and asserts playCard is called.
  • A test covers pointerup outside the drop zone and asserts no play is submitted.
  • npm run verify and ./mvnw verify both green.

renderedFields.description:
Follow-up raised by @architecture-guardian during the EOP-79 review (MINOR-B). Deferred from EOP-79 deliberately: fixing it there would have meant rewriting the pointer state machine inside a narrow regression fix, and would have landed untested multi-touch behaviour.

Problem

DragState in ui/src/components/GameScreen.tsx stores cardId, startX, startY, currentX, currentY — but not pointerId, even though handlePointerDown has e.pointerId in hand when it calls setPointerCapture(e.pointerId).

Three handlers therefore gate on dragState truthiness alone and cannot tell which pointer they are serving:

  • handlePointerMove — gates on if (!dragState) return;
  • handlePointerUp — gates on if (!dragState) return;
  • handlePointerCancel — takes no event parameter at all, so it structurally cannot filter; it is {{() => { setDragState(null); }

    }}

All three are bound on the <main> container, so any event from any pointer beneath that container is served as though it belonged to the active drag. With a drag in flight, a second concurrent pointer can therefore move the ghost, submit a play, or abort the drag.

Note the count: three handlers, not two. The architecture-guardian's round-2 review named only handlePointerUp and handlePointerCancel and explicitly corrected itself in round 3 — handlePointerMove has the same hole.

Why this matters beyond multi-touch

ADR-038 declares multi-touch out of scope (ADR-038:50-51), so this is not a supported-gesture gap. But the EOP-79 amendment paragraph (a) now leans on the absence of pointerId filtering to justify a broad manual invariant ("no descendant of a drag surface may be natively draggable"), which every future author must remember and which nothing enforces. The architecture-guardian's point: the structural fix is narrower and stronger, and the manual invariant should be the backstop rather than the primary remedy.

Proposed change (~4 lines)

  1. Add pointerId: number to the DragState interface.
  2. Store e.pointerId in handlePointerDown.
  3. Compare e.pointerId !== dragState.pointerId and return early in handlePointerMove and handlePointerUp.
  4. Give handlePointerCancel an event parameter and apply the same comparison.

Acceptance criteria

  • DragState carries pointerId, and all three of handlePointerMove, handlePointerUp and handlePointerCancel ignore events from any other pointer.
  • A test proves a second pointer's pointercancel does not clear a drag started by the first.
  • A test proves a second pointer's pointerup over the drop zone does not submit a play for the first pointer's card.
  • ADR-038 amendment paragraph (a) is re-worded so the descendant-guarding invariant is stated as defence in depth, with the pointerId filter named as the primary structural remedy.
  • npm run verify and ./mvnw verify both green.

Context

  • EOP-79: https://maglez.atlassian.net/browse/EOP-79
  • PR #84: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/84
  • ADR-038 docs/adr/ADR-038-pointer-event-drag-and-drop.md, amendment paragraph (a) at lines 73-88

renderedFields.description:
Problem

ui/ has no enforced formatting standard, so any stray formatter run produces a large spurious diff that no quality gate catches.

Verified state:

  • Prettier is not a dependency at all — no prettier in ui/package.json dependencies or devDependencies
  • There is no .prettierrc, no prettier.config.*, and no .editorconfig in ui/
  • ui/eslint.config.js:23-27 declares only consistent-type-imports and no-unnecessary-condition on top of the recommended sets — no stylistic or quote rule anywhere

The consequence is already visible in the tree: ui/src/components/GameScreen.tsx:1 imports with single quotes while ui/src/components/CardCatalogue.tsx:1-2 uses double quotes, and npm run verify passes with both.

Why this matters — it caused a real incident

During the EOP-79 review (PR #84), a reviewer ran npx prettier -write src/components/GameScreen.tsx --dry-run. dry-run is not a valid Prettier flag, so Prettier warned Ignored unknown option --dry-run and treated the command as a plain -write.

Because no Prettier config exists, npx downloaded Prettier ad hoc and applied its defaults (double quotes, 80-column wrap) against a file written to a different convention. Nearly every line moved: 474 insertions / 281 deletions. Critically it was not whitespace-only — git diff -w --stat still reported 408/215, because quote style changed, and it inserted compiler-visible {{

{" "}

}} JSX children.

Two architectural consequences:

  1. Formatting churn is indistinguishable from authored change in any future diff or review. Had this been committed with git add -A, EOP-79's four-line semantic bug fix would have been buried inside a 755-line churn diff, and git blame on the file would have been destroyed.
  2. The repo's stated quality gate (npm run verify = typecheck && lint && test && build) cannot detect a whole class of unintended modification. All 158 tests passed on the reformatted file, which is precisely what made it dangerous rather than obviously broken.

Three separate DoD gate agents (@security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian) rejected EOP-79 round 4 on the resulting dirty tree, costing a full review round.

Proposed change

Either:

  • (a) Adopt Prettier as a pinned devDependency with a committed config (.prettierrc) matching the existing dominant convention (single quotes), and wire prettier --check into the verify script so drift fails the gate; or
  • (b) Add explicit stylistic rules to ui/eslint.config.js so eslint . enforces quote style and formatting.

Option (a) is likely preferable because it also fixes the npx-downloads-defaults hazard: with a committed config, an accidental prettier --write conforms to the repo's own style instead of rewriting the file.

Note that whichever is chosen, a one-off normalisation commit will be needed, and it must be its own commit ([EOP-NNN] style: …) so it never mixes with semantic change.

Documentation obligation

ADR-009 fixes the front-end stack (React + TypeScript + Vite, GOV.UK Design System) but does not settle formatting authority. This choice deserves recording — either an amendment to ADR-009 or a new ADR — because it establishes which tool is authoritative and that the gate enforces it.

Acceptance criteria

  • A formatting standard is enforced by npm run verify, so a drifted file fails the gate rather than passing silently
  • If Prettier is adopted, it is a pinned devDependency with a committed config — not resolved ad hoc by npx
  • The existing ui/ sources are normalised in a dedicated commit containing no semantic change
  • npm run verify and ./mvnw verify both green
  • The formatting-authority decision is recorded in an ADR (amendment to ADR-009 or a new ADR), and docs/adr/README.md updated to match

Provenance

Raised as MINOR-C by @architecture-guardian during the EOP-79 re-check on commit d2bc95c, explicitly as non-gating for EOP-79 and pre-existing rather than introduced by it.
