Five places state that a per-trick score assembler would cost seventy-nine round trips at three players. That figure is 1 + 3 x 26 — a 78-card-era number, stale since EOP-69 trimmed the deck to 74, and untouched by EOP-75 (74 -> 68). Because it was never a 74-card figure, it fell outside EOP-93's sweep, which was scoped to 74-card references. Raised by @architecture-guardian while approving EOP-93 (PR #87).

The correct arithmetic at 68 cards

A three-player deal is 23 / 23 / 22 cards, so a hand runs to 23 tricks. A per-trick assembler costing three reads per trick plus one is therefore 1 + 3 x 23 = 70 round trips, not 79.

Sites to correct

File Line Current text
docs/adr/ADR-031-the-score-is-read-through-its-own-route.md 103 "game reaches twenty-six tricks, so mapping it over the history would cost seventy-nine round trips"
docs/adr/README.md 41 "at three players is four round trips instead of seventy-nine"
docs/architecture/runtime-view.md 843 "would have cost three reads per trick: seventy-nine in a twenty-six-trick hand"
src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/persistence/TrickPlayRepositoryAdapter.java 310 "would cost seventy-nine round trips at three players"
src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/migration/SeatAndSequenceBoundsTest.java 241 "a three-player deal is 26 tricks"

Line numbers are indicative — locate by phrase, not by number (the lesson EOP-93 learned the hard way).

Also in scope: an internal contradiction EOP-93 widened

ADR-031:103 says "twenty-six tricks" while :257 now says "23 tricks" — EOP-93 corrected the latter and left the former. The contradiction pre-existed (25 vs 26) but is now three tricks wide, and :257 refers to "the read count" that the same document declines to reconcile. Fix both together so the ADR is internally consistent.

Acceptance criteria

  1. All five sites state a figure derived from the 68-card deck, or say "the read count" without a figure if the derivation cannot be pinned down.
  2. ADR-031:103 and :257 agree on the trick count.
  3. Where a number is stated, the derivation is stated with it (1 + 3 x 23), so the next deck change makes the staleness visible rather than silent.
  4. ./mvnw verify stays green.

Why the guard did not catch this

DeckArithmeticClaimsTest (added by EOP-93) cannot see it: "seventy-nine" is neither a superseded deck size nor a universal-quantifier claim over table sizes. One of the five sites is production javadoc in TrickPlayRepositoryAdapter. This is a concrete instance of the limitation now recorded at docs/adr/ADR-006-build-quality-gates.md:44 — the matchers are phrase lists, so a green build is not proof that documentation is correct. Consider whether this story's defect class is worth adding to the guard, and if not, say why in the PR.

comments.body:
All four acceptance criteria met. PR #88 has all five Definition-of-Done sign-offs and is ready for human merge approval.

PR: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/88 — branch eop-96-rederive-score-read-round-trips, five commits on bd90766, 8 files, +311/-19.

The arithmetic

79 = 1 + 3 x 26 and 26 = ceil(78 / 3) — a 78-card-era figure that survived EOP-69 (78→74) and EOP-75 (74→68). It escaped EOP-93's sweep because it is derived from the deck size rather than being the deck size. At 68 cards the three-player deal is 23/23/22, so a hand runs to 23 tricks and the cost is 1 + 3 x 23 = 70.

Nine sites, not the five in the ticket

The four named sites plus the ADR-031 self-contradiction, and four more found by sweeping for derived rather than stated figures: SeatAndSequenceBoundsTest's trick sequence 26 (now 1/23/999 — the old value was a legal 78-card game length, so it proved nothing about the absence of an upper bound), the migration 005 <comment>, and two changelog entries. Where a figure was load-bearing it was kept with its derivation stated; where it was incidental historical colour it was dropped, exercising criterion 1's "no figure" branch.

Guard question: yes, worth adding — invariant 3

DeckArithmeticClaimsTest gained a third invariant deriving both figures from CURRENT_DECK_SIZE. It is sentence-scoped, strips Jira keys, and fires only where a sentence prices a read.

The review caught this story committing its own defect

@architecture-guardian rejected the first version and proved it by simulating the next deck trim against the shipped predicate: 1 of 4 sites caught. Two causes. spell() had no word for 70, and an unspellable number fails to match silently — so the guard would have gone quiet while reporting success, with the changelog and the test's own javadoc both promising it was trim-proof. And line scoping was invalidated by this very fix's rewrap, which left "= seventy" ending one line and "round trips" beginning the next — the primary site moved out of reach, and sentencesOf's own javadoc had already argued that "a line-scoped matcher would miss exactly the paragraph-length claims that go stale".

Fixed in fb26bf5: case 70, plus a precondition asserting every cost is spellable before a trim makes it superseded, so the build fails on the trimming commit rather than after it; sentence scoping; the markdown-table-row skip removed (the read anchor already acquitted the lines it was written for, while the skip blinded the guard to docs/adr/README.md — itself one of the nine sites). Re-run: 4 of 4. Both false written claims were corrected rather than softened.

Liquibase

The migration <comment> was corrected in place. ChangeSet.generateCheckSum() in liquibase-core 5.0.3 digests only getChanges() and getSqlVisitors(), never getComments() — verified by decompilation and independently reproduced by @security-auditor. The green build deliberately does not corroborate this: every test context reads the same new file into a fresh schema, so a comment-inclusive checksum would recompute identically and pass. An earlier draft of the changelog claimed that replay as empirical confirmation; that overstatement was retracted in 221a2d5.

Verification

./mvnw verify → EXIT=0, BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 1231, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, coverage met, checkstyle and spotbugs clean. Reproduced independently by @architecture-guardian.

Follow-ups filed

EOP-99 (invariant 2 misses markdown and the spelled deck size inside Java — including production GetScoreUseCase javadoc; also carries the ADR-006 amendment this story omitted), EOP-100 (scope the merged-changeset rule to checksum-affecting elements and prove it in a test), EOP-101 (checksum negative-control test against a pre-existing DATABASECHANGELOG), EOP-102 (ADR-002 says the bootstrap used Java 26), EOP-103 (shouldCarryAmendmentDates passes vacuously for an undated status line).

docs/architecture/ contains only C4-Diagrams.md and runtime-view.md. The arc42 static building-block view has no file in this repository and never has. Raised by @architecture-guardian as its own standing gap while approving EOP-93 (PR #87) — explicitly not to be attached to a documentation-sweep story.

Resolution options — implementer must choose one

Option A — Create the file. Author docs/architecture/building-blocks.md with a static module breakdown of the current architecture. More valuable, more work.

Option B — Correct the references. Remove or correct the reference in AGENTS.md's Documentation Protocol and in the @architecture-guardian agent brief (.opencode/agents/architecture-guardian.md) to name only the two documents that actually exist. Lower effort. If Option B is chosen, verify there are no other references to building-blocks.md elsewhere in the repository (other agent briefs, ADRs, docs cross-links) and correct them in the same commit.

Both options are valid. The choice is part of the work — do not assume creation is mandated.

Scope (if Option A)

Author docs/architecture/building-blocks.md: the static module breakdown of org.maglez.eop.*.

  • The Clean Architecture rings as a Mermaid flowchart TD, showing dependencies pointing inward only: Entities -> Use Cases -> Interface Adapters -> Frameworks & Drivers.
  • Per-layer module inventory with each module's responsibility and its allowed dependencies:
  • org.maglez.eop.entity — domain entities and domain exceptions, zero framework imports (no Spring, no Jakarta)
  • org.maglez.eop.usecase — application use cases and the port interfaces they depend on
  • org.maglez.eop.adapter.* — web (controllers, GlobalExceptionHandler, DTOs), persistence (repository adapters), security (SecureRandomDeckShuffler)
  • org.maglez.eop.config — @ConfigurationProperties classes (interface adapter layer)
  • Where DTOs sit and why entities never cross a boundary.
  • The documentation-integrity guards in org.maglez.eop.docs and what each holds (they are part of the static picture now that prose is a build gate — see ADR-006 as amended 2026-08-18).

Acceptance criteria

  1. Either docs/architecture/building-blocks.md exists and is listed wherever the architecture documents are indexed, or all references to it in AGENTS.md and agent briefs are corrected to reflect the two documents that exist.
  2. No dangling references to building-blocks.md remain anywhere in the repository.
  3. If Option A: every layer named above appears with its responsibility and its permitted dependency direction, and the Mermaid diagram renders on GitHub.
  4. No stale deck arithmetic is introduced — DeckArithmeticClaimsTest walks all of docs/*/.md, so this file is inside a build gate from the moment it is committed.
  5. ./mvnw verify stays green.

Assignment

@architecture-guardian owns this. It identified the gap in its own remit rather than in any diff.

comments.body:
Nominated as the canonical ticket for the missing `docs/architecture/building-blocks.md`. EOP-47 and EOP-116 are now linked to this one as duplicates.

Found during the EOP-41/EOP-49 gate round (PR #105). @architecture-guardian raised the missing arc42 static view as a finding, and a search before filing a new ticket turned up three open tickets for the identical gap, none referencing another:

  • EOP-47 (2026-08-12, from the EOP-14 Slice A review)
  • EOP-97 (2026-08-18, raised by @architecture-guardian while approving EOP-93/PR #87) — this one
  • EOP-116 (2026-08-20, from the EOP-58 gate round)

Its own verdict on that: "Three tickets for one gap is the backlog equivalent of the drift this PR exists to fix." Filing a fourth would have made it worse, so nothing new was created; EOP-47 and EOP-116 should be closed as duplicates of this ticket once someone with authority to close them agrees.

One correction to this ticket's scope, established by command rather than assumption. ls docs/architecture/ returns exactly two files, C4-Diagrams.md and runtime-view.md. So this is not an "audit the file" or "author the file" task with a settled answer — the file does not exist, while AGENTS.md and the @architecture-guardian operating protocol both name it as though it does. An agent instructed to read a file that is not there is the actual defect, and it has two defensible remedies:

  1. Create the document, or
  2. Remove every reference to it and record in an ADR that C4 Level 3 is deliberately the only static view.

If creating it, resist duplicating `C4-Diagrams.md`. A building-blocks view that restates the container diagram in prose becomes a second place to drift — precisely the failure EOP-41 and EOP-49 spent a story correcting, and the same file is already carrying that load: because C4 Level 3 has absorbed the static-view role, C4-Diagrams.md has grown past a thousand lines and now contradicts itself about the trick-play surface (:81-84 versus :1081-1089), filed separately as EOP-128. Prefer moving content out of C4-Diagrams.md over copying it, leaving a pointer at the origin.

Acceptance criteria (superseding whichever of the three tickets' criteria conflict)

  • Either docs/architecture/building-blocks.md exists with content not duplicated from C4-Diagrams.md, or every reference to it is removed and an ADR records C4 Level 3 as the static view.
  • EOP-47 and EOP-116 are closed as duplicates of this ticket.
  • If content moves out of C4-Diagrams.md, the origin keeps a pointer rather than a copy.
  • Any line citation in new content is re-derived from source, never adjusted by an offset.
  • ./mvnw verify green — the prose gates walk all of docs/*/.md, so a new file there is inside their reach.
  • docs/adr/README.md updated if an ADR is added or amended.

ADR-023 lines 1180-1206 (on main) are the composite-foreign-key deferral and the fk_trick_winner_play decision. The seat/sequence bounds these sources claim to implement are recorded elsewhere in the ADR — at roughly :1323-1326, the passage beginning "@security-auditor measured player.seat_order = -7 …". So the citation pointed at the wrong subject even before any line drift. EOP-93's edits then moved the target a further eight lines.

Constraint — only one of the four is fixable

Two of the sites are inside 005-seat-and-sequence-bounds.xml, a merged Liquibase changeset. .opencode/rules/database.md golden rule 1 forbids modifying a merged changeset: Liquibase identifies changesets by id + author + filepath, and editing one causes checksum failures on every environment it has already run against. Do not edit that file.

That leaves SeatAndSequenceBoundsTest.java:39 as the tractable half. Decide and record in the PR how to handle the changeset comments — the likely answer is a note in ADR-023 itself acknowledging that the changeset's comments cite a superseded line range and cannot be corrected in place, so the ADR carries the correction rather than the changeset.

Acceptance criteria

  1. SeatAndSequenceBoundsTest.java:39 cites ADR-023 by a quoted phrase that is unique and grep-locatable, pointing at the passage that actually records the seat/sequence bounds — not at the composite-FK deferral.
  2. The chosen phrase is verified to resolve by grep against the current ADR. Note EOP-93's lesson: a phrase spanning a hard-wrapped newline will not match a single-line grep, so pick a fragment that sits on one line.
  3. The immovable changeset citations are addressed by documentation rather than edited, with the reasoning recorded in the PR.
  4. ./mvnw verify stays green.

Raised by @architecture-guardian while reviewing EOP-96 (PR #88). Non-blocking for that story; this is the gap it left open and recorded.

The gap

DeckArithmeticClaimsTest invariant 2 (shouldNotStateASupersededDeckSizeInJavaProse) walks javaPaths() only, so nothing guards a stale deck size in markdown. EOP-96's corrected sentences in ADR-031, docs/adr/README.md and docs/architecture/runtime-view.md now name 68 cards and 23 tricks with no test standing behind them — the same shape of miss EOP-96 was raised to fix, one layer out.

Worse, and inside invariant 2's own declared scope: spell() has no case 68, and statesTheNumber returns false silently when the digits regex misses and the spelling is null. So every site stating the deck size as a word is unguarded. Seven live ones:

  • src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/usecase/GetScoreUseCase.java:13 — "deck: sixty-eight cards, whatever the game." Production code, no digits, so it goes stale and unguarded on the next trim
  • src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/entity/DeckFixture.java:12,59,69
  • src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/security/SecureRandomDeckShufflerTest.java:23
  • src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/web/TrickControllerIntegrationTest.java:964
  • src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/persistence/CardRepositoryAdapterIntegrationTest.java:72

EOP-96 added a spellability precondition, but it maps over costs only, so a future author can satisfy it in full and leave invariant 2 blind. This is the same silent-blindness class EOP-96 was rejected for on its first pass.

Scope

  1. Add case 68 -> "sixty-eight" to spell().
  2. Widen EOP-96's spellability precondition to cover deck sizes as well as their costs.
  3. Extend invariant 2 from javaPaths() to prosePaths(). Prefer an anchor over an exemption: EOP-96 learned that its READ_COST anchor did all the work a markdown-table-row skip could not, and the skip cost it a real site.
  4. Add the ADR-006 Amendments entry EOP-96 omitted. ADR-006 states that a change to what mvn verify gates on is recorded there; its negative-consequences list is headed "These are the ones that must not be omitted" and already carries the structurally identical twin bullet "ui/** is outside invariant D. It is clean today and unguarded tomorrow." ADR-006:35 also still credits DeckArithmeticClaimsTest to EOP-93 alone. Record the new invariant, its markdown-and-spelled-form blindness, and item 5.
  5. Record the cross-row merge hazard. sentencesOf splits only on [.!?]\s+, so a markdown table row whose last cell lacks a terminal full stop merges with the next row. This already happens 5x in the real docs/adr/README.md (85 lines produce 125 sentences; the longest merged sentence is 1850 chars and spans 12 rows). None carries a READ_COST anchor today, so the hazard is latent, not absent — a two-row merge can offend while neither row offends alone. Record it where the class's other limits live.
  6. Optional: narrow the trailing-hyphen exclusion in statesTheNumberStrictly so "the seventy-round-trip alternative was rejected" and "seventy-plus round trips" stop escaping. A lookahead excluding only a following unit word — (?!-(?:one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine)) — keeps the seventy-nine exclusion that the current blanket hyphen rule provides.

Acceptance criteria

  1. spell() knows every supported deck size and every cost derived from one, asserted rather than remembered.
  2. A superseded deck size in markdown fails the build, in digits and spelled.
  3. The ADR-006 Amendments entry exists and records the gap as closed, not open.
  4. The cross-row merge limit is recorded in the test's own javadoc.
  5. ./mvnw verify stays green, with no false positive on ADR-023's amended historical deal tables or on CHANGELOG.md's qualified historical entries.

Line numbers are indicative — locate by phrase, not by number.

renderedFields.description:
Raised during EOP-96's DoD review. Non-blocking for PR #88.

EOP-96 corrected a factually wrong trick count inside the <comment> of a merged Liquibase changeset (src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/005-seat-and-sequence-bounds.xml, changeset 002-add-trick-sequence-check). .opencode/rules/database.md golden rule 1 says "Never modify a merged changeset", with checksum failure as its stated rationale — a rationale that provably does not apply to comment text.

Evidence

javap -p -c on ChangeSet.class from the resolved liquibase-core 5.0.3 shows generateCheckSum delegating wholly to lambda$generateCheckSum$0, whose digest input is only getChanges() + ":" then getSqlVisitors() + ";", fed to CheckSum.compute. getComments() is invoked in exactly three places in the class — setStopTime() twice and getSerializableFieldValue(String) — none in or after that lambda. Independently reproduced by @security-auditor.

What was rejected

@db-designer proposed rewording the rule to "Never modify a merged changeset's structural elements … Elements that do not affect checksums (such as <comment> text) may be corrected in place when factual errors are discovered, but such edits should be rare and well-justified."

@architecture-guardian rejected that drafting for three reasons: it pins the rule to one Liquibase version's implementation while stating it timelessly (true of 5.0.3, not guaranteed of 5.1 — the blunt rule is safe under version drift, the reworded one silently becomes false the day the digest widens); "may be corrected in place … rare and well-justified" converts an absolute into an unenforceable judgement call in a file that loads into every agent's context on every dispatch, where agents will read the permission as a licence and the qualifier as satisfied by their own reasoning; and it demotes "always add a new changeset" to a special case.

Scope

  1. Keep "Never modify a merged changeset" as the headline imperative in .opencode/rules/database.md.
  2. Add one bounded sentence: <comment> text is outside the checksum as verified against the pinned `liquibase-core` version; correcting a factual error in it is permitted; and the correction must be recorded in the changelog file's own header comment. That last clause codifies the practice EOP-96 established.
  3. State that structural elements (<sql>, <preConditions>, <rollback>, attributes) remain absolutely immutable.
  4. Add a test asserting ChangeSet.generateCheckSum() is comment-blind for the resolved Liquibase version, so the version-dependent half of the claim fails the build on upgrade instead of rotting silently in prose.
  5. Add a short dated Amendments entry to docs/adr/ADR-008-database-migration-liquibase.md. A grep of that ADR for checksum|immutab|modify returns 0 — the rule lives only in the rules file, and "a rules file is instruction, not a decision record", so the reasoning must survive where decisions live.

Acceptance criteria

  • The headline prohibition still reads as an absolute; the exception is one bounded sentence naming the pinned version.
  • A test fails if a future Liquibase upgrade makes the checksum comment-inclusive.
  • ADR-008 carries a dated Amendments entry.
  • ./mvnw verify stays green.

Line numbers are indicative — locate by phrase, not by number.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @architecture-guardian during EOP-96's Definition of Done review. Non-blocking for PR #88.

The gap

grep -rln "Testcontainers|PostgreSQLContainer" src/test/java returns nothing. Every @SpringBootTest context builds a fresh H2 schema from an empty database, so the suite cannot detect a Liquibase checksum break at all.

EOP-96 edited the <comment> of a merged changeset in 005-seat-and-sequence-bounds.xml in place. That was justified by decompiling ChangeSet.generateCheckSum(), and the changelog states plainly that the green build cannot corroborate it: every context reads the same new file into a fresh schema, so a comment-inclusive checksum would recompute identically and pass just as cleanly. Falsifying the claim needs the old file and then the new one against one persistent database, which nothing in the suite does.

Scope

Add a test that:

  1. Applies a pre-EOP-96 revision of 005-seat-and-sequence-bounds.xml to a persistent H2 file datasource — not mem:.
  2. Records MD5SUM for 002-add-trick-sequence-check from DATABASECHANGELOG.
  3. Re-runs Liquibase with the current file against that same database.
  4. Asserts no ValidationFailedException and an unchanged MD5SUM.

This converts EOP-96's decompilation argument into a build-enforced fact, and closes the standing gap that no test replays these migrations against a pre-existing DATABASECHANGELOG.

The checksum algorithm is engine-independent, so H2 is sufficient for this specific claim — a PostgreSQL 17 replay is a larger, separate question.

Consider whether the fixture holds the old changeset text as a test resource or reconstructs it from git; a test resource is more honest about what is being asserted and does not couple the test to history.

Notes

  • Line numbers are indicative — locate by phrase, not by number.
  • Acceptance: ./mvnw verify stays green, and the new test demonstrably fails if the changeset's <sql> is altered.

docs/adr/ADR-002-spring-boot-bootstrap.md:8 states that the original pom.xml used "only JUnit 5 with Java 26". The project is Java 21 LTS, maven-enforcer-plugin requires JDK >= 21, and Java 26 did not exist when this project was bootstrapped.

Filed as a Task because this project has no Bug issue type; it is a defect in a documentation record.

Noticed during EOP-96 while sweeping for stale numbers. Deliberately left out of that story's scope: different defect class, different file, and folding it in would have put an unrelated edit under an EOP-96 To Do prefix.

Scope

  • Establish the real value from git log on the original pom.xml rather than assuming 21. This is a historical record of what the bootstrap actually used, so the correct fix is the value that was true then, not the value that is true now.
  • Likely a transcription of the ADR number or a stray year, but verify rather than guess.
  • ADR-002:3 already carries a framework version superseded annotation, so the file has an Amendments section ready to receive the correction.

Why no test caught it

Every documentation-integrity invariant in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ is keyed to deck arithmetic, so a wrong tool version in prose is invisible to all of them. This is a concrete instance of the limitation recorded at ADR-006:44: the guards are phrase lists, and a green build is not proof the documentation is correct. Whether a version-checking invariant is worth adding is a judgement call for this ticket — the cheaper answer may be that it is not, and that should then be said explicitly rather than left implied.

Acceptance criteria

  1. ADR-002 states the Java version the bootstrap actually used, evidenced from git history.
  2. The correction is recorded in that file's Amendments section with a date.
  3. ./mvnw verify stays green.

Line numbers are indicative — locate by phrase, not by number.

Defect (filed as a Task — project EOP has no Bug issue type). Raised by @architecture-guardian during the EOP-96 sign-off. Non-blocking for PR #88.

The defect

AdrIndexConsistencyTest.shouldCarryAmendmentDates reads the dates out of an ADR's status line and then does:

if (dates.isEmpty())

{ continue; }

So an ADR whose status line carries no date is skipped rather than flagged. The test reports success for the documents it never examined.

ADR-031 is a live instance. Its index row has no date:

sed -n '41p' docs/adr/README.md | grep -oE '20[0-9]

{2}-[0-9]{2}

-[0-9]

{2}

' # empty

EOP-96 amended that ADR's body — correcting a round-trip figure derived from a two-trims-old deck size — and the index recorded nothing, with no test objecting. Had the status line been dated, the test would have forced the index to record when.

Why this matters more than its size suggests

This is the same silent-blindness family as the defect EOP-96 was rejected for on its first pass: a guard that cannot see a case reports no offence, and a green build vouches for prose nobody checked. skip-when-absent is the shape to distrust. The house practice is the opposite — see ADR-006:47, and the two anti-vacuity preconditions in DeckArithmeticClaimsTest which assert their own applicability rather than quietly passing when it lapses.

Scope

  1. Replace the silent continue with something that fails, or is explicitly and visibly exempt. Two candidate shapes: require a date on every status line whose leading word is amended; or assert that the set of skipped ADRs equals an expected list, so a new undated amendment breaks the build.
  2. Record the adjacent limit in the test's own javadoc: it pins status lines only, so an index cell's prose can drift arbitrarily far from its ADR without any test noticing. That is exactly how the ADR-031 row came to state a superseded round-trip figure for two deck trims.
  3. Decide, and write down, whether ADR-031's status line should now carry a date. This is a judgement call, not a defect: @architecture-guardian rated leaving it undated defensible, because the in-body amendment note exists and is dated. If the rule from (1) requires a date, this becomes a consequence of that rule rather than a separate decision.

Acceptance criteria

  • An ADR with an undated amended status line either fails the build or appears in an explicit, asserted exemption list — no silent skip remains.
  • The test's javadoc records the status-lines-only reach, naming the ADR-031 row as the concrete case that drifted.
  • A deliberate temporary edit demonstrates the new assertion actually fires; the demonstration is described in the PR, not committed.
  • ./mvnw verify stays green.

Line numbers are indicative — locate by phrase, not by number.

renderedFields.description:
Raised during the EOP-35 review rounds and deliberately excluded from that story. Every item below is pre-existing or explicitly accepted as non-blocking by a Definition-of-Done gate; none was introduced by EOP-35.

@architecture-guardian asked for one ticket rather than three, because items 1–4 are a single defect class: ADR structural and factual drift that no build gate can see.

1. ADR-008 references profiles that have never existed

docs/adr/ADR-008-database-migration-liquibase.md names dev, test and staging profiles at :47, :56, :67, :70, :98. Per .opencode/rules/configuration.md and ADR-012 there are exactly two profiles — the default profile and prod — and there have only ever been two.

There is a partial retraction note at :49, but the surrounding prose still states the false thing. Rewrite the prose; do not stack a second retraction note on top of the first.

2. ADR-013 has two ## Amendments headings

docs/adr/ADR-013-feature-flags-spring-conditional.md:89 and :310. Merge under one heading, preserving amendment order and dates.

3. ADR-042 uses the wrong section heading

docs/adr/ADR-042-game-over-flag-on.md:192 uses ## Relations where the house convention — prescribed by docs/adr/README.md step 3 and followed by 34 of 39 ADRs — is ## Related. Rename. No test enforces either spelling, which is why it drifted.

4. The amendment-visibility hole — the most valuable item here

AdrIndexConsistencyTest.shouldCarryAmendmentDates derives the dates it demands from the ADR's own `*Status:` line* and skips entirely when that line carries none:

final List<String> dates = datesIn(status);
if (dates.isEmpty()) { continue; }

So an amendment that declines to touch the Status line is invisible to the test and to the index by construction. This is not hypothetical — EOP-35 produced a live instance of each outcome:

  • ADR-008's 2026-08-19 amendment is visible in docs/adr/README.md only because its Status line was extended by hand in the same commit.
  • ADR-006's 2026-08-19 amendment (the sixth gate class) is invisible in the index today — its Status line is a bare *Status:* Accepted, the amendment added no date, so the assertion never fires. ADR-043:312-316 records this explicitly.

Extend `shouldCarryAmendmentDates` to scan for `*Amendment, YYYY-MM-DD{{ headings and require the ADR's }}*Status:{{ line and its }}docs/adr/README.md` row to carry the most recent one.** Then bring ADR-006's Status line and index row into line.

Per ADR-006's own rule at :37 — "That is a change to what `mvn verify` gates on, and this ADR is where such changes are recorded" — record the gate change in ADR-006.

5. Hardening items on LiquibaseContextGatingAbsentTest (all accepted as non-blocking in EOP-35)

src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/config/LiquibaseContextGatingAbsentTest.java

  • `:136` weak anti-vacuity threshold. hasSizeGreaterThan(1) passes with 10 files present even if 8 of the 9 changesets were deleted. Both @tester-unit-and-quality and @security-auditor independently graded this MINOR and non-blocking — it catches every path to vacuity, and because these are presence assertions a depopulated tree cannot produce a false negative. Tighten only if it can be done without failing on every legitimate new migration.
  • `:167-169` relaxed-binding spellings escape the property assertion. @security-auditor verified by harness that label_filter:, LABEL-FILTER:, LABELFILTER: and CONTEXTS: bind to the real property but escape the startsWith check. All four set a non-empty value, so they fail closed with respect to the fail-open finding. Fix: normalise the key with toLowerCase() / replace('_','-') before comparison.
  • `:82, 94, 103, 112` the control under-claims its own breadth. The Javadoc and @DisplayName}}s say "changeset-side", but {{@security-auditor traced the XSD and found gating attributes are declared on five distinct carriers: changeSet, the root databaseChangeLog group, include, includeAll, property and modifySql. Because the scan is line-based over all .xml it catches all of them. Under-claiming is the safe direction, but a maintainer trusting the narrow wording might "optimise" the scan to <changeSet> blocks and silently lose four carriers. *This matters because the master changelog uses `includeAll` — a `context` there would gate every changeset in the file.
  • `:190` unasserted coupling. The .xml filter is coupled to db.changelog-master.xml's endsWithFilter=".xml". They agree today, so a .yaml changelog is invisible to both and never runs (fail-closed by coincidence); change endsWithFilter and the scan goes blind to a format that now executes. Nothing asserts they stay in step.
  • `:44-61` Javadoc asterisk misalignment. A 2-space {{ * }} indent where the rest of the class uses 1-space. Checkstyle does not enforce Javadoc indentation. Note the two gates disagreed: `@code-reviewer` raised it as a cosmetic warning, `@architecture-guardian` explicitly declined it ("Leave it; I do not want it"). Neither blocked. Decide once here.
  • `:91` `LABELS_ATTRIBUTE` naming. The constant also matches labelFilter, a runtime property name rather than a changeset attribute. Rename, or add an inline note at the declaration.

Explicitly NOT in scope

The `contexts: {}` blind spot and the environment-override bypass are not defects to fix. Both are properties of Spring's YAML flattener and of runtime overrides respectively; @security-auditor independently confirmed "No choice of accessor fixes this." They are honestly conceded in ADR-043's Consequences and must stay conceded rather than be "fixed".

  • ADR-006 records the gate change, per its own rule.
  • No ADR references a dev, test or staging profile.
  • ADR-043's statement that ADR-006's amendment is invisible in the index is updated once that is no longer true — it is a dated observation, not a permanent claim.

renderedFields.description:
Defect

The hand-maintained TypeScript DTO layer in ui/src/api.ts has drifted from the server's enums. This is not a spec-vs-code mismatch that could be argued either way — the Java entities are the source of truth, docs/api/openapi.yml agrees with them, and the front end disagrees with both.

PlayerDto.role — ui/src/api.ts:97

readonly role: 'FACILITATOR' | 'PLAYER';

src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/entity/PlayerRole.java declares FACILITATOR, PARTICIPANT (:14, :16). docs/api/openapi.yml's PlayerRole enum lists FACILITATOR, PARTICIPANT.

So 'PLAYER' is a value the server never emits, and 'PARTICIPANT' — which it emits for every non-facilitator player — is absent from the union.

SessionStateDto.status — ui/src/api.ts:104

readonly status: 'LOBBY' | 'IN_PROGRESS' | 'ENDED';

src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/entity/SessionStatus.java declares LOBBY, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, ABANDONED. docs/api/openapi.yml's SessionStatus enum agrees.

So 'ENDED' is never emitted, and both 'COMPLETED' and 'ABANDONED' are missing.

Why this is worse than it looks

TypeScript unions are erased at runtime, so nothing throws. The server's real value flows into a variable typed as something else, and every comparison against it silently evaluates false:

  • any role === 'PLAYER' branch is dead code
  • any status === 'ENDED' branch is dead code
  • a session that reaches COMPLETED or ABANDONED matches no case, so end-of-game and expiry handling has no typed path to hit

The compiler cannot help, because the values arrive from fetch through a type assertion rather than a parse. This is the classic failure mode of a hand-maintained contract mirror, and it has already failed.

How it was found

Raised as a MAJOR by @tester-api during the EOP-40 Definition-of-Done review, sampling three DTO interfaces against docs/api/openapi.yml. TrickPlayDto was clean; the two above were not. It was then confirmed against the Java enums rather than stopping at the OpenAPI document, because a spec and a client can drift together.

EOP-40 documented the risk class — ADR-009's amendment now records that the DTO layer is "hand-maintained rather than generated from docs/api/openapi.yml, so the anchor holds only as long as someone keeps the two in step" — but deliberately changed no code, being a documentation-truth story.

Acceptance criteria

  1. ui/src/api.ts unions for PlayerDto.role and SessionStateDto.status match the Java enums exactly — FACILITATOR | PARTICIPANT and LOBBY | IN_PROGRESS | COMPLETED | ABANDONED.
  2. Every call site that branched on a removed value ('PLAYER', 'ENDED') is corrected rather than merely made to compile. Search ui/src/ for both strings; the branching lives in ui/src/components/.
  3. COMPLETED and ABANDONED have defined UI behaviour, or an explicit decision is recorded that they fall through to a default. A session can reach ABANDONED via the expiry sweep (GameSessionJpaRepository:196,209), so this is reachable in production, not hypothetical.
  4. ConnectionStatus is typed as bare string in ui/src/api.ts while the contract declares an enum (CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED) — tighten it in the same pass or state why not.
  5. A Vitest case asserts each union member is accepted and a non-member rejected, so the next drift fails a test rather than a review.
  6. Consider whether the mirror should be generated from docs/api/openapi.yml rather than hand-written. That is the root cause and worth a decision — if generation is rejected, record why in ADR-009 or ADR-004, since ADR-009's amendment now names this as an unenforced manual invariant.

Evidence

  • ui/src/api.ts:97, :104
  • src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/entity/PlayerRole.java:14,16
  • src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/entity/SessionStatus.java:17,19 plus its COMPLETED/ABANDONED members
  • docs/api/openapi.yml — SessionStatus and PlayerRole schemas
  • src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/persistence/GameSessionJpaRepository.java:196,209 — ABANDONED is set by the expiry sweep, so it reaches clients

comments.body:
Fixed on eop-105-ui-enum-drift, PR https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/92 (commit b4f64cc).

All six acceptance criteria answered

AC-1 met. PLAYER_ROLES = ['FACILITATOR', 'PARTICIPANT'] and SESSION_STATUSES = ['LOBBY', 'IN_PROGRESS', 'COMPLETED', 'ABANDONED'], as as const arrays with derived unions rather than inline unions — keeping the members at runtime is what makes them checkable.

AC-2 reported as not met on its premise, rather than ticked. The AC asserted the dead branching lives in ui/src/components/. It does not, and never did. There is no role === 'PLAYER' and no status === 'ENDED' anywhere in ui/src. Every production role comparison tests 'FACILITATOR', which was valid on both sides of the drift. All 'PLAYER' occurrences were test fixtures, now corrected. Three review gates confirmed this independently. The ticket's "any role === 'PLAYER' branch is dead code" describes a branch that never existed — worth annotating so the claim does not outlive the story.

AC-3 met, and the ticket's premise on `ABANDONED` was weaker than filed. COMPLETED was a genuine dead end and now exits the lobby via onSessionEnd(). ABANDONED deliberately gets no branch: SweepExpiredSessionsUseCase → abandonAndDelete sets the status and deletes the row in the same transaction, so no client can observe it — the next fetch is a 404, already handled. It is listed for contract fidelity only. Separately, SessionStatus's javadoc claimed "No code reaches this state yet", which was false; it now scopes the unobservability to the one path that writes it today and admits a second writer would make it observable with no test failing.

AC-4 met — ConnectionStatus tightened to 'CONNECTED' | 'DISCONNECTED', and LeaderboardDto.sessionStatus tightened from bare string in the same pass.

AC-5 met — Vitest asserts every declared member accepted and non-members rejected, including the two that had drifted.

AC-6 met: codegen rejected, with the reasoning and its limits recorded. ADR-009 carries a three-option decision table; the mirror is small and a generator would be a stack decision needing its own ADR. Enforcement is instead EnumMirrorParityTest, a new Java documentation-integrity test comparing the Java enums, the enum: lists in docs/api/openapi.yml and the as const arrays in ui/src/api.ts — four mirrors × two directions = 8 cases. It is Java rather than Vitest because ui/ deliberately has no @types/node, so a browser test cannot read files off disk.

Two things found that were not in the ticket

`StrideCategory` was a fourth mirror in the same condition — a bare union whose own comment asserted parity while nothing checked it, with SUIT_LABELS keyed exhaustively off it, so a drifted member would have taken the label map with it while tsc stayed green. It had not yet drifted, which is exactly why it was worth pinning. Found by a review agent during this story's own gate round, not by the build — the registration hole documented as a possibility fired within one review cycle.

Two known limitations, stated plainly: nothing detects a fifth unregistered mirror, and the guard reads only the export const NAME = [...] as const; idiom, so registering a bare-union mirror means rewriting the declaration first.

Verification

npm run verify in ui/ → exit 0, 178 tests. ./mvnw verify → exit 0, 1244 tests, SpotBugs 0, JaCoCo 96.9% instruction / 88.6% branch against 80/70.

Mutation-tested rather than merely green. Reintroducing ['FACILITATOR', 'PLAYER'] failed exactly one of the eight parity cases with a diagnostic naming the file — so the guard discriminates rather than failing broadly. @tester-unit-and-quality then ran five further mutations independently; none survived.

Definition of Done

All five gates approved. It took four rounds: @architecture-guardian rejected three times, and each rejection found something real — twice including prose that asserted a rule the code contradicted, which is the defect class this story exists to close.

@security-auditor answered the obvious question directly: enum drift on a role field in a game called Elevation of Privilege is not a privilege escalation, on two independent grounds — the client branch was never wrong, and the server recomputes the role from the opaque token before applying canStartPlay().

Follow-ups filed

  • EOP-108 — the boundary asserts rather than parses, and the new guards have no production callers. The root cause, deferred deliberately because it needs an error-contract decision first.
  • EOP-109 — three DTO fields still bare string where the contract declares an enum.
  • EOP-110 — six CVEs in the ui/ dev toolchain, one critical; production tree reports 0.

renderedFields.description:
The suspicion

ui/vite.config.ts:22 sets the dev server port to 5371. Vite's default is 5173. 5371 looks like a digit transposition of the default rather than a chosen number, and no ADR, comment or changelog entry gives a reason for it.

The header comment in that file explains at length why API_TARGET is a constant rather than an env var, and why the proxy mirrors Caddy's single-origin behaviour — but says nothing about the port, which is what you would expect if the value was never deliberate.

Why EOP-40 documented it rather than changed it

EOP-40 was a documentation-truth story. ADR-009 claimed :5173 and three documentation sites repeated it; the code says 5371, and code is authoritative for what actually happens. So EOP-40 corrected the prose to :5371 and recorded the suspicion in ADR-009's ### Why the front-end port is :5371 rather than quietly changing the port under cover of a docs ticket.

@architecture-guardian reviewed that call and endorsed it emphatically, adding the reasoning that matters here: do not record `:5371` as a deliberate decision. An ADR asserting intent behind a probable typo would manufacture exactly the false-but-authoritative prose EOP-40 exists to delete, and it would then be load-bearing — the next person to notice the transposition would be blocked by a fabricated rationale.

Scope — five files, not a one-liner

The port is dev-server only. ui/Caddyfile and compose.app.yml are unaffected, because in the container topology Caddy serves the built bundle and there is no Vite dev server. But the value is now cited in prose in several places, all of which move together:

  1. ui/vite.config.ts:22 — server.port
  2. AGENTS.md — the Front-end bullet's Build clause, which names :5371 and contrasts it with Vite's default
  3. docs/devops/local-development.md — two sites: the quick-start comment and the two-terminal workflow line
  4. docs/devops/local-development.md — the paragraph added by EOP-40 stating that ui/vite.config.ts is the only source of truth for the port
  5. docs/adr/ADR-009-frontend-react-typescript.md — the ### Why the front-end port is :5371 note, which becomes obsolete and should be folded into a dated amendment rather than deleted

Leave `ADR-009`'s original Development-workflow line alone. It says :5173 and is preserved historical text under the house amendment convention — it is not a stale reference to fix.

Acceptance criteria

  1. A decision is recorded either way. If the port moves to 5173, say so; if it stays at 5371, that is now a deliberate choice and needs a one-line reason, at which point ADR-009's note is amended to state it rather than speculate.
  2. If it moves: all four documentation sites above are updated in the same commit, and ADR-009's ### Why the front-end port is :5371 is superseded by a dated amendment rather than silently removed.
  3. npm run dev in ui/ is actually run, and /api and /health are confirmed to still proxy to :8080 on the new port.
  4. Nothing in ui/Caddyfile, ui/Dockerfile or compose.app.yml changes — confirm by inspection, since the container path does not use the dev server.
  5. Check whether any developer tooling, editor config, browser bookmark or .env.example entry hardcodes the old port before switching.

Prior art

Raised as a follow-up by EOP-40 and endorsed by @architecture-guardian during that story's Definition-of-Done review. See docs/adr/ADR-009-frontend-react-typescript.md, section ### Why the front-end port is :5371.

comments.body:
Decision: the port moves back to 5173

The ticket asked whether 5371 is deliberate or a transposition. Git history answers the first half, and the author answered the second.

The premise in ADR-009 was wrong — but so was the port

ADR-009's ### Why the front-end port is :5371 says the value is "very likely a typo in the original commit". git log – ui/vite.config.ts shows that is false on both halves:

Commit Subject Port
7efd900 EOP-9 Done feat: serve a React front end behind Caddy on one origin created the file with `5173` — Vite's default, correct
496d7b5 EOP-63 To Do chore: set Vite dev server port to 5371 2026-08-17, +1/-1, sole change `5173` → `5371`
aab329f EOP-110 Done chore: clear six CVEs… touched only the import line

So the original commit was correct, and a later dedicated commit — whose subject line names the new value — introduced 5371. That sentence in ADR-009 has to be corrected whichever way the port goes.

Author's answer closes it

Asked whether the 2026-08-17 change dodged a port clash: "I got the port number wrong. I had no reason for changing the port number."

That is the one thing no amount of repository archaeology could establish, and it removes the only argument for keeping 5371. A non-default port with no reason behind it is pure carrying cost: every doc site has to explain the deviation, and the explanation is "someone mistyped it". Reverting to 5173 deletes the exception instead of documenting it.

Note this is the opposite of inventing a rationale. @architecture-guardian's objection on EOP-40 was to an ADR asserting intent behind a probable typo; recording an author-confirmed mistake is the honest alternative, and it means ADR-009 no longer needs a ### Why the port is … section at all.

Scope

  • ui/vite.config.ts — server.port → 5173
  • Four documentation sites updated in the same commit (AC#2): AGENTS.md, docs/devops/local-development.md, and two live claims in ADR-009
  • ADR-009's ### Why the front-end port is :5371 is superseded by a dated amendment, not deleted (AC#2)
  • ADR-009's original Development-workflow line stays untouched — preserved historical text, per the ticket

AC#4 and AC#5 already verified

A repo-wide search for 5371 finds it in no operational file. Confirmed absent from ui/Caddyfile, ui/Dockerfile, compose.app.yml, docker-compose.yml, .env, .env.example, .envrc, scripts/, .githooks/ and .github/. There is no .vscode/ or .idea/ directory in the repository. Nothing operational changes — only vite.config.ts and prose. CHANGELOG.md's two mentions stay as-is: they are records of past changes, not live references.

Follow-up filed separately

496d7b5 is prefixed EOP-63 To Do , but EOP-63 is "Add EoP card images to docs/EoP_Microsoft_Docs/cards/". That violates .opencode/rules/git-commits.md and is the direct cause of this ticket existing: with no port ticket to record against, the rationale (that there wasn't one) was never captured. Raised as its own issue.

Done — merged to main as f7bb35a (PR #96).

Decision: the port moved back to Vite's default :5173. The ticket's premise — that :5371 might be a transposition slip in the original commit — was disproved by git, and then resolved by the author. git log – ui/vite.config.ts returned three commits before this work: 7efd900 created the file at port: 5173, the correct default; 496d7b5 (2026-08-17, carrying an unrelated ticket's prefix) changed it to 5371 in a dedicated +1/-1 commit whose subject names the new value; aab329f touched only the import line. So the ADR's claim was false on both halves: the original commit was right, and a later deliberate edit introduced 5371. Asked directly, the author confirmed he "got the port number wrong" and "had no reason for changing" it.

Given that, reverting deletes the exception rather than documenting it — a non-default port with no reason behind it is pure carrying cost, four documentation sites each explaining a deviation whose explanation is "someone mistyped it". This also satisfies the objection @architecture-guardian raised while reviewing the earlier documentation-truth story (do not record :5371 as a deliberate decision), though the choice between reverting and recording was not one it expressed a preference on.

Acceptance criteria

  • AC#1 — decision recorded: the ADR-009 status line, a new dated amendment, and CHANGELOG.md.
  • AC#2 — all four documentation sites updated in the same commit (59c22b0), and the "Why the front-end port is :5371" section superseded by a dated blockquote placed above its original body, not removed. Same treatment at the development-workflow amendment and the amendment-table row.
  • AC#3 — npm run dev actually run against Spring Boot on :8080. Vite 7.3.6 bound IPv6 loopback :5173 (nothing on 5371); /health through :5173 returned 200 text/plain "OK", and /api/v1/cards returned 200 application/json 4685 bytes byte-identical (cmp -s) to the direct :8080 response. Independently reproduced by @tester-api.
  • AC#4 — ui/Caddyfile, ui/Dockerfile and compose.app.yml untouched, confirmed by git diff --name-only and by inspection: none of the three ever referenced the dev port, since Caddy serves the built bundle and the dev server never runs in a container.
  • AC#5 — no tooling, editor config or .env.example hardcodes the old port. No .vscode/ or .idea/ exists. Every surviving 5371 mention is a deliberate historical record (the ADR's superseded passages, two dated CHANGELOG entries, and the new explanatory comment in vite.config.ts). AGENTS.md and docs/devops/local-development.md contain zero.

renderedFields.description:
Origin

Five items surfaced by @security-auditor across two Definition-of-Done reviews on EOP-40, plus one from @tester-api. None was introduced by EOP-40 — that story changed only Markdown. All were raised as explicitly non-blocking follow-ups and are collected here so they stop being rediscovered on every review of a front-end change.

Each item was verified against the live configuration, not inferred from a diff.

1. No cross-origin isolation headers — ui/Caddyfile:97-107

Caddy sets a good header block: CSP (default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'none'), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, HSTS, Permissions-Policy, -Server removed, admin off, a 16 KB request-body cap on /api/*, and — a genuinely thorough touch — the whole block re-applied to Caddy-generated 4xx/5xx via handle_errors.

Missing: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy, Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy. Also no require-trusted-types-for/trusted-types, and the CSP is origin-based rather than nonce-based. All defense-in-depth on an app that loads no third-party script. X-Frame-Options is absent but correctly superseded by frame-ancestors 'none'.

2. Visiting by IP literal bypasses the entire header block — ui/Caddyfile:47-52

HTTP routing is gated on host: localhost. RFC 6066 forbids IP literals in SNI, so a request to https://<ip>/ completes the TLS handshake via default_sni localhost but the Host does not match — returning an empty 200 with Server: Caddy and none of the headers in item 1. The Caddyfile documents this against itself and notes the demo is localhost-only. Worth closing if the stack is ever exposed.

3. Production source maps served from the web root

ui/vite.config.ts:30 sets sourcemap: true, and ui/Dockerfile:52 copies /build/dist to /srv, so .map files are served by file_server. Anyone fetching them gets the original TypeScript. Either stop emitting them for production builds, or exclude *.map from the served root. (Noted as sound in passing: ui/Dockerfile:58 runs USER web, so the container is not root.)

4. playerToken in sessionStorage — ui/src/App.tsx:50,80

The session credential is persisted to sessionStorage under eop_session and replayed as a custom request header at ~11 call sites in ui/src/api.ts. Any script achieving execution can read it directly — the exposure an HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict cookie exists to remove.

This is a deliberate ADR-015 decision, because the SSE stream is fetch-based precisely so it can carry a custom header, which EventSource cannot. It is mitigated by the CSP in item 1 plus Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, and by the fact that no token is ever placed in a URL — all call sites pass it in headers on relative paths, so it cannot leak via Referer, history or the Caddy access log.

So this is a re-examination, not a straightforward fix. If the header approach stands, record why in ADR-015 in terms of the XSS exposure it accepts; if it does not, the SSE transport has to change with it.

5. .opencode/agents/ui-builder.md has no security section

The brief for the only agent that writes React covers accessibility, typography, forms and technical quality — and says nothing about XSS, token storage, the CSP, or the auth-header convention. It instructs nothing unsafe today, and JSX's default escaping means the absence of guidance still yields safe rendering in the common case. But it gives that agent no reason to prefer a cookie over the sessionStorage pattern it will find in App.tsx and copy.

6. The forms guidance does not mention form-action 'none' — .opencode/agents/ui-builder.md

The brief instructs GOV.UK forms, and the GOV.UK Design System's canonical examples are server-rendered <form action="..." method="post">. ui/Caddyfile sets form-action 'none'. An agent following the brief literally can produce a form that works under npm run dev (Vite sets no CSP) and is silently blocked behind Caddy.

Both shipped forms already do the right thing — JoinSessionForm.tsx and CreateSessionForm.tsx both use an onSubmit handler calling preventDefault() with no action attribute — so nothing is broken now.

The risk is the repair, not the break. An agent that hits Refused to send form data because it violates ... form-action 'none' and has no instruction saying the directive is deliberate may relax it in ui/Caddyfile, turning an availability bug into a weakened exfiltration control. One line in the brief closes it.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Items 1-3 are each either fixed or explicitly declined with a recorded reason. They are independent; do not let the hardest gate the easiest.
  2. Item 4 gets a decision recorded in ADR-015, whichever way it goes, stated in terms of the exposure accepted.
  3. Items 5 and 6 are closed together — a short Security section in .opencode/agents/ui-builder.md covering token handling, the CSP constraints the front end runs under, never dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and the preventDefault() form convention with the reason.
  4. If the CSP changes, docs/adr/ADR-017-frontend-delivery-topology.md moves with it.
  5. Anything touching ui/Caddyfile is verified by actually starting the stack and checking response headers, not by reading the config.

comments.body:
Delivered on branch eop-107-frontend-security-hardening — PR https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/97 (2 commits, 8 files, +387/−6).

Item 1 — cross-origin isolation headers: FIXED. Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp added to both the site header block and the handle_errors block in ui/Caddyfile, so the success path and the error path stay header-for-header identical. require-corp is safe because there is no cross-origin subresource: the only external URL in the front end is the footer Creative Commons link, which is a navigation, and the GOV.UK CSS and fonts are copied into the bundle and served from /assets. Verified in the built artefact and on the wire. Trusted Types declined (needs a policy in application code and its failure mode is visible only in a real browser, which nothing in the pipeline runs) and nonce-based CSP declined (a static file_server cannot rewrite index.html per request, and Vite emits only external content-hashed files so default-src 'self' already refuses inline script). Both declines are recorded in ADR-035 with revisit triggers.

Item 2 — IP-literal header bypass: FIXED for every address a local browser can use; residual recorded. Site address widened to localhost:8080, 127.0.0.1:8080, [::1]:8080. https://127.0.0.1/ previously returned an empty 200 with Server: Caddy and none of the headers; it now returns 200 with all eight, as does https://[::1]/. An arbitrary unmatched Host still gets the bare empty 200 — recorded in ADR-035 as not closed, with the two ways out (a real certificate, or on-demand TLS behind an ask endpoint) named and rejected as disproportionate for a loopback-only demo. Worth noting for the record: what closed this was HTTP Host routing, not certificate issuance. Caddy did mint 127.0.0.1 and [::1] leaves, but RFC 6066 forbids an IP literal in SNI, so the localhost leaf is still the one presented and the browser name-mismatch warning is unchanged.

Item 3 — production source maps: FIXED in two layers. build.sourcemap: false in ui/vite.config.ts, so nothing is emitted (find /srv -name '*.map' in the built image returns nothing); plus @sourcemap path *.map → error 404 at the edge, because the SPA try_files fallback would otherwise answer a .map request with index.html and a 200, hiding a regression instead of reporting it. error rather than respond so handle_errors re-applies the headers and the 404 is byte-identical to any other.

Item 4 — `playerToken` in `sessionStorage`: re-examined and UPHELD, with the exposure now stated in ADR-015. The finding is correct and is not disputed: a script executing in this origin reads eop_session and holds a player's full authority for the life of the tab, which an HttpOnly cookie would take off the table. It stands because per-tab scope is the mechanism the demo actually uses for several seats in one browser, because the custom header is what keeps CSRF out of the threat model entirely, and because the SSE transport is built on fetch precisely so it can set that header — so moving to a cookie is a transport change, not a storage change. The amendment states plainly that the listed mitigations narrow the routes and do not prevent exfiltration by a script that already runs, and names three revisit triggers.

Items 5 and 6 — `.opencode/agents/ui-builder.md`: FIXED. New ### 5. Security section covering token handling (never localStorage, never in a URL or a log line, and exactly two modules touch it — App.tsx reads it out of storage behind its isStoredSession guard, api.ts attaches it to a request), never dangerouslySetInnerHTML, the CSP quoted in full with its practical consequences, the form-action 'none' convention (onSubmit + preventDefault(), never action, with the npm run dev false-negative spelled out), and an explicit prohibition on relaxing a CSP directive in ui/Caddyfile to make a component work.

Acceptance criteria. (1) Items 1–3 were judged independently and each is fixed. (2) Item 4's decision is recorded in ADR-015 in terms of the exposure accepted. (3) Items 5+6 closed together. (4) The CSP is byte-identical to main — diff on the directive returns nothing — so criterion 4's condition never fired; ADR-017 was amended anyway, because three new headers and a new refusal in the handler it describes would otherwise leave it silently incomplete. (5) Every header claim was measured against a running stack whose config was confirmed byte-identical to the committed file by md5sum inside the container, not read off the config.

Also amended: ADR-035 (three header-table rows, three dated narrowing pointers to prose the change falsified, and a new Amendments section), ADR-017, ADR-015, docs/adr/README.md (the ADR-035 index row said "five security response headers"; it now says eight), and CHANGELOG.md.

Definition of Done: all five gates approved — @tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian. @architecture-guardian first rejected on documentation synchrony (a stale index row and prose still asserting the pre-change position) and re-approved against commit f551627 after six remediation edits. ./mvnw verify and npm run verify both exit 0.

Merged to main as 77c4968 (PR #97, squash-free merge commit; branch deleted). CI green on all three jobs before merge — build 1m43s, ui 25s, image 1m18s (run 32362020895). Local container stack has been taken down.

renderedFields.description:
Context

Raised by all five DoD gates during EOP-105. EOP-105 corrected which enum members ui/src/api.ts declares and added a build-time parity gate (EnumMirrorParityTest), but deliberately did not touch the root cause the ticket itself named.

The defect

Every fetch helper in ui/src/api.ts ends:

return (await response.json()) as SomeDto;

That is a type assertion, never a parse. TypeScript unions are erased at runtime, so a payload carrying role: "ROOT" or status: "WHATEVER" flows into React state unchallenged and every comparison against it silently evaluates false.

EOP-105 added four runtime-preserved mirrors with type guards — isPlayerRole, isSessionStatus, isConnectionStatus, isStrideCategory — but they have zero production call sites. They are exercised only by ui/src/api.test.ts. @security-auditor graded this MEDIUM/MAJOR: "the server→browser trust boundary is byte-for-byte as unvalidated after this change as before it."

Why it was deferred rather than blocked

@security-auditor judged the deferral defensible on three grounds, each verified rather than assumed:

  1. Every client-side comparison fails closed. Each production comparison is a positive test for a specific member (role === 'FACILITATOR', status === 'LOBBY', === 'IN_PROGRESS', === 'COMPLETED'), so an unknown value degrades to no privilege granted, no transition fired, least-privileged state.
  2. Nothing on the client is authoritative. No authentication exists (ADR-015) and the sole privilege is enforced in the domain entity (GameSession.start → PlayerRole.canStartPlay()), with the role derived server-side from the opaque token and never submitted.
  3. A parse buys little against the actual threat. ui/Caddyfile serves bundle and API from one origin (ADR-017), so a server able to inject a bogus enum can already serve arbitrary JavaScript.

Why it still needs doing

Exported-but-unused guards read as protection to the next maintainer, and the guards are the correct seam for a parse. Scope is contained: the boundary points touching these enums.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Decide and record whether validation is adopted per-DTO by hand, via a schema library (Zod/Valibot), or by generating validators from docs/api/openapi.yml. A library is a stack decision needing its own ADR, not an amendment.
  2. Define the error contract for a validation failure before writing code — throw? ApiError? degrade to a partial render? This is the substantive decision and it touches .opencode/rules/error-handling.md, which is why it did not belong bolted onto an enum-parity story.
  3. Adopt the existing is* guards at the boundary rather than duplicating them, or delete them if the chosen mechanism supersedes them. Do not leave both.
  4. A Vitest case per boundary asserting a payload with an out-of-contract enum value is rejected rather than admitted.
  5. If adopted, re-evaluate ADR-009's codegen rejection — its third revisit trigger is precisely "runtime validation of responses is adopted (a parse rather than an assertion)", at which point a generated schema and a generated type become one artefact and codegen buys two things instead of one.

Evidence

ui/src/api.ts — as SomeDto at every helper; the four guards defined and unused. ADR-009's EOP-105 amendment records the deferral and the revisit trigger.

Delivered — PR 93(https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/93) open for human approval. Branch eop-108-ui-parse-response-dtos, commit 8f8dcb6, off main @ 211ca12.

Acceptance criteria

AC Discharged by
1. Decide and record the mechanism New [ADR-045](docs/adr/ADR-045-frontend-response-validation.md) — hand-written per-DTO parsers inside ui/src/api.ts. A schema library (Zod/Valibot) was rejected because ui/ has exactly three production dependencies and EOP-110 already tracks six dev-toolchain CVEs, so adding production supply-chain surface for ~11 shapes is disproportionate; codegen was deferred to ADR-009 as a stack decision. A re-open trigger is stated: "shape count roughly doubles or nested/recursive shapes appear"
2. Define the error contract before writing code, and reflect it in .opencode/rules/error-handling.md ContractViolationError extends ApiError with status = 502, thrown from the parser. Decided in ADR-045 §3 with both alternatives recorded as rejected. error-handling.md gains a ## Client side — the browser's own boundary section
3. Adopt the existing is* guards rather than duplicating them, or delete them — not both Adopted. All four guards are consumed through a single requireEnum(source, key, path, guard, members) seam that takes the guard and its as const array, precisely so no member list is re-inlined (EnumMirrorParityTest only sees the arrays). No second validation mechanism exists — @architecture-guardian verified this four ways
4. A Vitest case per boundary asserting an out-of-contract enum is rejected Ten rejection cases via it.each over a boundaries table, plus ten happy-path cases and twenty-two focused cases
5. Re-evaluate ADR-009's codegen rejection Its third revisit trigger — "runtime validation of responses is adopted (a parse rather than an assertion)" — fired. ADR-009 amended with a dated section: rejection upheld but on explicitly narrower grounds, since its original "three-enum, roughly twenty-line surface" argument is spent (api.ts went 525 → 883 lines). One new trigger registered

What changed

All ten JSON-returning helpers now parse instead of asserting. Twelve module-private parse* functions plus eleven shared validation primitives. The parsers are deliberately un-exported: that turns "api.ts is the only place a response is parsed" from a convention into a compiler-enforced property, and stops a vi.spyOn(api, …) test being mistaken for evidence that the boundary works.

startNewGame, dealCards (204) and subscribeToSession correctly get no parser — the SSE stream is a doorbell whose data: frames carry no DTO, and the re-fetch it triggers is parsed.

Strictness is bounded on purpose, and the bound must be quoted whenever this change is described: object-ness, required-field presence and typeof, arrays actually arrays, enum membership — but no format validation, no UUID regex, no ISO-8601, no ranges. The DTOs are structurally and enumerably validated; "validated at the boundary" unqualified over-claims.

This is not a security improvement and must not be cited as one. All three grounds on which this ticket recorded the EOP-105 deferral as defensible still hold. It closes a maintenance hazard — four exported guards that read as protection while protecting nothing — and converts silent misbehaviour into a loud failure.

Three items of unplanned scope

  1. `CardDto.suit` narrowed from bare string to StrideCategory. This closes the first of EOP-109's three items — commented on that ticket separately.
  2. `problemMessage` hardened — it read the error body as ProblemDetail and would render [object Object] into the error summary for {"detail": {…}}. Now type-checks detail/title and degrades to statusText. Deliberately not a DTO parser and must never throw.
  3. `requireNumberRecord` does not delegate to `requireNumber` — deliberate duplication, because its map keys are server-chosen and therefore payload. @security-auditor demonstrated a key like <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> being reflected into a message that renders in a GOV.UK ErrorSummary (escaped by React, not exploitable, but contrary to the never-name-the-payload rule). It now reports only the field, and builds its result with Object.create(null).

Verification

cd ui && npm run verify   → exit 0 — 9 test files, 220 tests (was 178, so +42)
./mvnw verify             → exit 0 — 1244 tests, BUILD SUCCESS
                            JaCoCo 96.9% instruction / 88.6% branch (vs 80/70)

The three component test files that stub global fetch pass unchanged — itself the evidence their fixtures were already contract-complete, since an incomplete one would now throw. No component or component test was modified.

Definition of Done — all five gates approved

  • @tester-unit-and-quality — APPROVE. Confirmed all ten boundaries covered and the toEqual(validBody) happy-path assertion is a real constraint. Identified three surviving mutants in the exactOptionalPropertyTypes conditional-spread absent arms; closed by eight further cases asserting Object.hasOwn(...) === false.
  • @tester-api — APPROVE. Field-by-field agreement against docs/api/openapi.yml and every Java DTO. Critically: no required field can legitimately arrive `null` or absent, so the parsers reject no valid response — the regression direction that mattered most. Confirmed TrickDto.ledSuit is the only outstanding bare-string contract enum.
  • @security-auditor — APPROVE. Verified the not-a-security-improvement framing is stated plainly and over-claimed nowhere; fail-closed at all ten boundaries and improved at two (no bogus admission reaches sessionStorage; no lifecycle transition fires on a rejected payload); prototype pollution structurally impossible; no production dependency added; EOP-110 posture unchanged. Its MINORs are fixed in this PR.
  • @code-reviewer — APPROVE. All twelve parsers read every declared field, all nested path strings correct and indexed, zero any, no surviving DTO assertion. Endorsed the un-export decision.
  • @architecture-guardian — APPROVE on the second round. It rejected the first round on two MAJORs, both legitimate and both remediated rather than downgraded: (1) docs/architecture/C4-Diagrams.md claimed api.ts owns "every wire concern" and then listed four, omitting validation, and runtime-view.md's running enumeration of refreshSession exits was stale — fixed, including a new section distinguishing three `onSessionEnd()` triggers from four distinguishable outcomes, now enumerated in full because an unenumerated count is uncheckable; (2) ADR-009 falsely claimed only a generator could close the field-coverage hazard — it cannot, since this repo already runs four text-reading comparison gates and a fifth would close it without a dependency, so the claim is deleted from both sites and the option set restated as three wide.

Known limitation carried forward

Because a parser reconstructs rather than passing the payload through, a field added to a DTO interface but not to its parser is silently dropped and arrives undefined while still typechecking — strictly worse than the as cast it replaced. EnumMirrorParityTest compares enum member lists, not field sets, so nothing detects it and enforcement is review only. Pinned as documented behaviour by a drops a field the server sends but no parser reads test, and registered as the one trigger that should reopen ADR-009's codegen rejection with the presumption reversed. ADR-009 now specifies concretely the text-comparison build gate that would close it without a generator.

Definition of Done — five-gate sign-off complete

Resolved. Implementation landed in PR #93 (merge 6fd0b42, commit 8f8dcb6) and is on main. Follow-ups already landed on top: 1ad2d01/fa65505 (EOP-109, rank exclusion rationale), f551627 (EOP-107, front-end edge hardening).

Acceptance criteria

AC Result
Record whether validation is hand-written per-DTO vs schema library vs generated from docs/api/openapi.yml PASS — recorded as a four-way decision table in docs/adr/ADR-045-frontend-response-validation.md §1. Outcome: hand-written per-DTO parsers
Define the error contract before writing code PASS — ContractViolationError extends ApiError (ui/src/api.ts:114-119) with super(502, message). Both rationales stated in place: extending is load-bearing because every component already catches instanceof ApiError and renders .message through ErrorSummary, so a standalone class would be missed by every existing catch and surface as a blank screen; and 502 is fixed rather than response.status because the server said 200
Adopt the existing is* guards rather than duplicating, or delete them PASS — the four EOP-105 guards went from zero production call sites to real ones via a requireEnum(source, field, path, guard, MEMBERS) seam (:178-190): isStrideCategory at :307, isPlayerRole at :423, isConnectionStatus at :424, isSessionStatus at :433 and :647. @code-reviewer confirmed no parser re-inlines an enum member list — which matters because EnumMirrorParityTest pins only the arrays, so an inline duplicate would be invisible to it
A Vitest case per boundary asserting an out-of-contract enum is rejected PASS — all 10 JSON-returning helpers have one (ui/src/api.test.ts:520, 530, 540, 551, 561, 571, 581, 591, 603, 614, plus a ledSuit variant at :628). No parsed helper is missing a case
Re-evaluate ADR-009's codegen rejection PASS, explicitly recorded rather than implied — ADR-009:478 carries a dated heading: "Amendment — EOP-108 (2026-08-19): codegen re-evaluated because the parse landed, and still declined". ADR-009:491-493 concedes the codegen case is now "the strongest form yet available", and :541-547 records that EOP-108 ruled its own best argument ("the work is already done") inadmissible as self-reinforcing

The test-quality trap was avoided

.opencode/rules/error-handling.md:22 warns that a test using vi.spyOn(api, …) bypasses the parsers entirely and is not evidence they work. @tester-unit-and-quality measured it: zero vi.spyOn calls in api.test.ts (the one textual occurrence, at :420, is a comment quoting the rule), against 12 vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …) sites. Every rejection case exercises the real code path.

Security posture — the vector I had demonstrated pre-merge is closed at source

@security-auditor read all 918 lines of ui/src/api.ts and audited every violation() call site individually. requireNumberRecord (:249-264) deliberately does not delegate to requireNumber, precisely because requireNumber's message would carry the key it was handed; it reports only the field ("expected every value to be a finite number"). So the attack it demonstrated pre-merge — a payload key <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> in capturedBySuit reflected into the GOV.UK ErrorSummary — is closed at the source rather than mitigated downstream.

Fail-closed, with no status collision. The fixed 502 matches none of the 403/404/409 special-case branches in App.tsx, LobbyScreen, GameOverScreen or GameScreen, so every path falls through to setError(message). @security-auditor noted this is a genuine design property, not luck: echoing response.status instead would have let a bogus 409 body clear GameScreen to a plausible waiting state.

No over-claiming. Every hit for trusted|secured|security control|fully validated across ADR-045, the rule file, AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md is a disclaimer, not a claim — ADR-045:44 ("not a security fix… closes a maintenance hazard"), :80, :202, CHANGELOG.md:33. The mandated "structurally and enumerably validated" phrasing is used throughout.

Build evidence

  • ./mvnw clean verify → exit 0, BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 1256, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
  • ui/ npm run verify → exit 0, Test Files 9 passed (9), Tests 223 passed (223), production build succeeded

Gate verdicts — all five APPROVE

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE
@architecture-guardian APPROVE

Highest-value negative result

@code-reviewer ran the silent-drop check field-by-field across all 12 DTO interfaces against their parsers — the gap the rules name as review-enforced because a field added to an interface but not its parser still typechecks and arrives undefined. Zero instances found. Also: zero any, zero residual as SomeDto on a response body, no exported parse*, and no component casting a payload. App.tsx's isStoredSession correctly scoped as the sessionStorage boundary, not an exception.

Accepted-but-open

  • `capturedBySuit` under-constraint. requireNumberRecord (:637) validates that all values are finite numbers but does not enforce the six STRIDE keys docs/api/openapi.yml:1740-1746 marks required. No live payload is affected — LeaderboardDto.java:61-64 iterates StrideCategory.values() and inserts zero for every missing category — and no false-rejection risk exists; the risk is the reverse. Graded LOW by both @tester-api and @tester-unit-and-quality. Fixture ui/src/api.test.ts:465 uses two of six keys and is described as "contract-complete", which is inaccurate for that field.
  • `startNewGame` has no test at all — correctly parser-free, but structurally identical dealCards has both a happy and an error path. Filed as EOP-124.
  • ADR-045:60 argues a spent ground. The Zod/Valibot rejection row still cites EOP-110's six CVEs in the present tense; ADR-009:767-774 records that ground as "now discharged… it must not be cited again". The conclusion is unaffected. Filed as EOP-123 — the EOP-40 defect class recurring inside this ticket's own artefact.
