renderedFields.description:
Context

Found during EOP-105 by @tester-api and confirmed by @architecture-guardian. EOP-105 tightened two such fields (PlayerDto.connectionStatus and LeaderboardDto.sessionStatus, both string → a derived union) and left three.

The three fields

Field Declared Contract says
Card.rank string $ref: Rank
CardDto.suit string $ref: StrideCategory
CardDto.rank string $ref: Rank

`CardDto.suit` is the one that matters, and a ticket scoped as "Rank only" would be wrong. Unlike Rank, it is not a case of having nothing client-side to compare against: STRIDE_CATEGORIES exists as a registered mirror under EnumMirrorParityTest, its sibling Card.suit in the same file is properly typed against it, and CardDto.suit simply is not using it. This is recorded in both of the gate's exclusion lists (EnumMirrorParityTest.mirrors() javadoc and ADR-009's "the guard only sees one declaration idiom" section) precisely so this ticket cannot be mis-scoped.

Two lower-priority relatives

  • TrickDto.ledSuit?: string — contract is allOf: [$ref: StrideCategory].
  • LeaderboardRowDto.capturedBySuit: Readonly<Record<string, number>> — the contract declares an object with all six STRIDE categories as required integer properties. Structurally compatible but admits arbitrary keys.

Severity: MINOR, because drift here fails safe

Verified by @architecture-guardian rather than assumed: cardImagePath returns null for an unknown suit, and every consumer either null-checks or falls back (SUIT_COLOURS[…] ?? '#0b0c0c', SUIT_LABELS[…] ?? card.suit[0]). An unexpected value degrades to a missing image — not a crash, and not a silent wrong-comparison path. That is why this is a follow-up rather than part of EOP-105.

Acceptance criteria

  1. CardDto.suit and TrickDto.ledSuit retyped to StrideCategory (optional for ledSuit). No new mirror needed — STRIDE_CATEGORIES already exists and is gated.
  2. For Rank, decide rather than default. It has no TypeScript mirror because the client only ever displays the rank, never compares it, so a mirror may not earn its maintenance. If one is added, note it needs EnumMirrorParityTest.openApiEnumValues taught to read a YAML flow sequence — Rank's enum: is written inline on one line and ENUM_KEY ({{^ {6}

    enum:\s*$}}) cannot match it. If rejected, say so in ADR-009's exclusion list and leave Rank out.

  3. Any new mirror gets a row in EnumMirrorParityTest.mirrors() in the same commit — the registration hole is that nothing detects an omission, and it has already fired once (StrideCategory, caught by a review agent rather than by the build).
  4. Consider tightening capturedBySuit to Readonly<Record<StrideCategory, number>>.
  5. Update the exclusion lists in EnumMirrorParityTest.mirrors() javadoc and ADR-009 so they describe the position after this ticket, not before it.

Evidence

ui/src/api.ts (the three fields, plus Card.suit as the correctly-typed sibling); docs/api/openapi.yml StrideCategory and Rank schemas; ADR-009's idiom known-limitation section.

comments.body:
Scope reduced by EOP-108 — this ticket is now one field, not three.

EOP-108 (PR #93) narrowed `CardDto.suit` from bare string to StrideCategory and gave it a runtime parse via requireEnum(..., isStrideCategory, STRIDE_CATEGORIES). That was not scope creep for its own sake: EOP-108 was replacing every response assertion with a parse, and parsing every enum around suit while leaving that one field asserted would have been incoherent when isStrideCategory already existed and was already being consumed two lines away.

What remains. @tester-api audited every enum-typed field in docs/api/openapi.yml against what ui/src/api.ts now reads, and reported that `TrickDto.ledSuit` is the only outstanding bare-`string` contract enum:

  • docs/api/openapi.yml declares it allOf: $ref: '#/components/schemas/StrideCategory', so it is the STRIDE enum on the wire.
  • ui/src/api.ts reads it with optionalString, and TrickDto.ledSuit is still typed string. There is an inline comment at the field naming this ticket.
  • It is genuinely optional server-side — TrickDto is @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) and ledSuit is null until the first card of a trick is played — so any narrowing must keep it optional and must go through optionalString's replacement rather than requireEnum, which has no optional variant today. That is the one design decision this ticket still carries.
  • Every other enum-typed contract field is already narrowed and parsed: CardDto.suit and Card.suit (isStrideCategory), PlayerDto.role (isPlayerRole), PlayerDto.connectionStatus (isConnectionStatus), SessionStateDto.status and LeaderboardDto.sessionStatus (isSessionStatus). CardDto.rank is type: string in the contract rather than an enum schema, so bare string is correct there and it is not part of this ticket.

Please re-check the third item before starting. This ticket was filed as "three DTO fields still bare string where the contract declares an enum". One is now closed and one is identified above; if the third was CardDto.rank, it is not a defect. Worth confirming against the ticket's original evidence rather than assuming the count.

Two things EOP-108 leaves in place for you. The mechanism is decided — [ADR-045|docs/adr/ADR-045-frontend-response-validation.md], hand-written per-DTO parsers, bounded to structure and enum membership — so no new ADR is needed for a field narrowing that follows it. And .opencode/rules/error-handling.md now requires that the four is* guards be consumed, never re-inlined, because EnumMirrorParityTest only holds the as const arrays in three-way agreement with the Java enums and the OpenAPI enum: lists; a hand-written member list inside a parser would be invisible to that gate. Narrowing ledSuit therefore means routing it through the existing isStrideCategory seam, plus one Vitest rejection case proving an out-of-contract ledSuit is rejected rather than admitted.

Delivered — PR 94(https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/94), all five Definition-of-Done gates approved. Awaiting human approval to merge.

Scope, as it actually turned out

The ticket was filed as three bare-string fields. EOP-108 closed CardDto.suit first, so this story delivered one field: TrickDto.ledSuit.

The third item in the original list — CardDto.rank — was not in scope, but not for the reason the scope-reducing comment on this ticket gave. That comment said the contract declares rank as type: string rather than $ref-ing Rank, and therefore that bare string was faithful to the contract. That was false, and this ticket's own instruction to "re-check the third item before starting rather than assuming the count" was the right warning: docs/api/openapi.yml L995-996 is rank: / $ref: '#/components/schemas/Rank', there is exactly one rank: field, and there is no separate CardDto schema — both TypeScript interfaces map onto the one Card schema. Card.rank/CardDto.rank typed string is drift. It is accepted, fail-safe, recorded drift, which is a different thing from fidelity, and the difference is now stated correctly in six places rather than mis-stated.

What shipped

TrickDto.ledSuit is now readonly ledSuit?: StrideCategory, parsed by a new module-private optionalEnum(source, key, path, guard, members) that delegates to requireEnum once a value is present.

A helper rather than an inline check, because the field is genuinely optional on the wire — TrickDto is @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) and ledSuit is null until the first card of a trick is played — and requireEnum has no optional variant. The guard is passed in rather than the member list re-inlined, per .opencode/rules/error-handling.md, so isStrideCategory and STRIDE_CATEGORIES stay the single seam and remain visible to EnumMirrorParityTest. Net effect: optionality now weakens presence, never membership.

Two Vitest cases, both stubbing global fetch rather than vi.spyOn, so they exercise the real parser: an out-of-contract ledSuit rejects with TrickDto.ledSuit: expected one of SPOOFING, …, and ledSuit: null is still admitted as absent (Object.hasOwn false). Both would have passed vacuously under optionalString.

The three acceptance criteria that were decisions, not code

  • AC-2 — `Rank` mirror: REJECTED, not deferred. The client never compares or orders a rank: the contract supplies rankValue: integer described "Numeric rank used for comparison", the trick arithmetic that consumes it runs server-side, and the card face renders from rankSymbol. card.rank reaches exactly one consumer, cardImagePath(suit, rank), which returns string | null and whose every call site null-checks — so drift degrades to a missing card image, the same fail-safe shape suit had before EOP-108. Registering the mirror would additionally require teaching EnumMirrorParityTest.openApiEnumValues to read a YAML flow sequence. Exit condition recorded: revisit if rank ever becomes something the front end orders.
  • AC-3 — no new `mirrors()` row was needed, so it is satisfied vacuously. Stated explicitly in the code, the ADR and the changelog, because "no row needed" and "row forgotten" are indistinguishable in a diff — which is exactly how StrideCategory went unregistered until a review agent caught it during EOP-105.
  • AC-4 — `capturedBySuit` tightening: DECLINED. requireNumberRecord deliberately never inspects keys, because keys are server-chosen and ADR-045 §2 forbids reflecting them into a violation message. A Readonly<Record<StrideCategory, number>> index type would therefore be an unenforced compile-time claim — the exact defect class EOP-108 existed to remove. It would also be actively harmful: Record<K, V> over a finite union asserts total presence, so GameOverScreen.tsx's ?? 0 guard would look redundant to a future cleanup.

AC-5 — the exclusion lists in EnumMirrorParityTest.mirrors() and ADR-009 now describe the position after this ticket. No new ADR: ADR-045 already decided the mechanism, and a field narrowing that follows an existing decision is not a new one.

Gate outcomes — five approvals, four rejections survived

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE (after 2 rejections)
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE
@architecture-guardian APPROVE (after 1 rejection)

Both @tester-api rejections were factual and both were accepted in full: first the false type: string claim above, then a seventh site where the same over-claim survived in different words ("the last bare-string contract enum", which ledSuit was not). @architecture-guardian then rejected a correction for stating a non-operative cause — it had said a test-file rank list was invisible to the gate because of an idiom regex, when the operative reason is that typeScriptArrayValues reads only ui/src/api.ts and never opens the file at all.

The surviving lesson, recorded in CHANGELOG.md: a claim of this shape has to be swept for by *meaning, not by matching the phrasing of the first instance found.* Three of the four rejections were the same defect recurring in new words.

Verification

./mvnw verify — 1244 tests, 0 failures, checkstyle clean, SpotBugs 0, JaCoCo all coverage checks met, BUILD SUCCESS. All four documentation-integrity tests ran (AdrIndexConsistencyTest 5, DeckArithmeticClaimsTest 5, EnumMirrorParityTest 8, TrickPlayExceptionOriginTest 3).

cd ui && npm run verify — typecheck, ESLint, 223 Vitest tests across 9 files, production build, all clean.

Carried as reviewer-approved accepted-but-open

  • docs/adr/ADR-045-…:160-161 — one further unscoped "Rank has no mirror" sentence, under-qualified rather than false; @architecture-guardian named the exact one-clause edit and explicitly declined to block on it.
  • docs/adr/ADR-009-…:405 — the capturedBySuit decline stated as live text outside its authoritative home (ADR-045 §4); scoped "not required for this story" by the reviewer that raised it.
  • CHANGELOG.md entry length — measured at 935 words and found the shortest of the four entries in its section, so the house style rather than this entry is the issue.
  • mirrors() still has no omission detector, and nothing detects a $ref-ed contract enum typed bare string. Building the second gate was assessed and rejected as a code generator in all but name that would immediately fail on Card.rank and so need its own hand-written exclusion registry — the identical hole.

Five commits on eop-109-ui-narrow-ledsuit: 703169a (code + tests + docs), then 1ad2d01, 069b70e, fa65505, 29556c0 correcting review findings.

renderedFields.description:
Context

Found by @security-auditor during EOP-105's gate round, graded MEDIUM and explicitly not charged to that story: ui/package.json and ui/package-lock.json are untouched by it (git diff origin/main...HEAD – ui/package.json ui/package-lock.json was empty), so blocking there would have been wrong scope.

Findings

npm audit in ui/ reports 6 vulnerabilities:

Severity Package Issue
critical vitest (<=3.2.5) UI-server arbitrary file read/execute
high vite (<=6.4.2) Path traversal in optimized-deps .map handling; server.fs.deny bypass
high nanoid (<3.3.18) —
moderate @vitest/mocker, esbuild, vite-node esbuild dev-server request reflection

Why this is not a production exposure

npm audit --omit=dev reports 0 vulnerabilities — none of these reach the shipped bundle. All are build/test-time, and the advisories require a running, reachable dev server; ui/vite.config.ts binds :5371 locally. The exposure is a developer machine and CI, not a deployed container.

That is a reason to schedule it, not to dismiss it: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs npm run verify on every push, so the vulnerable dev-server code executes in CI against branch content.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Bump vitest, vite, nanoid and the transitive esbuild past the advisory ranges. Note vite and vitest versions are coupled — expect to move both together, and check @vitejs/plugin-react compatibility.
  2. npm audit in ui/ reports 0 critical and 0 high. Record any residual moderate with a reason.
  3. npm run verify in ui/ stays green — typecheck, ESLint, Vitest (178 cases at time of filing) and the production build.
  4. ./mvnw verify stays green. This is not a formality: EnumMirrorParityTest reads ui/src/api.ts as text, so a codemod applied by a major-version upgrade tool can turn the Java build red. Watch in particular for anything rewriting the export const NAME = [...] as const; declarations — typeScriptArrayValues recognises only that idiom.
  5. ui/package-lock.json committed with the change. engines.node >= 22 must remain satisfiable and CI must still build on 22.

Evidence

npm audit and npm audit --omit=dev in ui/; ui/package-lock.json; ui/vite.config.ts (dev server on :5371); .github/workflows/ci.yml (ui job).

Done — delivered in PR #95, merged to main as 19f75bd (commit aab329f).

Acceptance criteria

AC Result
1. Bump vitest, vite, nanoid, transitive esbuild past the advisory ranges ✅ vite ^5.4.9 → ^7.3.6, vitest ^2.1.3 → ^3.2.7. nanoid and esbuild cleared transitively — see below
2. npm audit 0 critical / 0 high, residual moderates recorded ✅ 0 vulnerabilities of any severity. No residual to record
3. npm run verify green ✅ exit 0 — Test Files 9 passed (9), Tests 223 passed (223), 0 skipped, 0 todo
4. ./mvnw verify green ✅ exit 0 — Tests run: 1244, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 across 95 classes. EnumMirrorParityTest 8/8
5. Lockfile committed; engines.node satisfiable; CI builds on 22 ✅ lockfile committed; floor raised to >=22.12; CI `ui` job passed on Node 22

All six advisories cleared

vitest 3.2.7 (CRITICAL), vite 7.3.6 (HIGH), nanoid 3.3.18 (HIGH), esbuild 0.28.2, @vitest/mocker 3.2.7, vite-node 3.2.4 — verified in the installed tree, not just package.json. @security-auditor added a negative control: the pre-change manifests audited against the same live database in the same minute return 6 vulnerabilities (3 moderate, 2 high, 1 critical). So 6-before / 0-after is a real delta, not an offline no-op.

Three were cleared transitively rather than by a direct pin — nanoid only via vite → postcss ^8.5.6 → nanoid@3.3.18, so a direct dependency would have been a fiction; esbuild as vite 7's own dependency. No overrides, no resolutions, no new install scripts, universal integrity hashes, single registry host.

AC 1's coupling warning was correct, and resolved without a plugin major

@vitejs/plugin-react's declared floor rose ^4.3.2 → ^4.7.0 even though the installed 4.7.0 did not move: ^4.3.2 peers only vite ^4.2 || ^5, so leaving it declared a combination the plugin forbids under vite 7. Major 4 was kept — 4.7.0 already peers vite 7. @vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.0 was rejected as out of scope (it drags in a rolldown + React-Compiler migration).

npm's own suggested majors were declined

npm suggested vitest 4.1.11 + vite 8.2.1. Declined: every advisory range sits strictly below the installed 7.3.6 / 3.2.7 pair, so the majors close nothing extra — they are an artefact of npm audit fix computing from the old declared ranges. The cost would have been a 91-site vi.spyOn(api, …) refactor across five helpers in GameScreen.test.tsx (the ticket's own estimate was understated by >2×). Bundling that into a CVE fix would make the security change un-reviewable as a security change.

⚠️ Recorded honestly in ADR-009: the vitest-4 breakage is upstream guidance, not reproduced here. The ADR instructs confirming it against a real vitest 4 run before sizing the refactor, and striking the constraint if the pattern survives — so it cannot outlive its premise.

AC 4's warning about codemods

No file under ui/src/ was touched, so the as const enum mirrors were never at risk. Proven rather than assumed: git diff on ui/src/api.ts is empty and EnumMirrorParityTest passes 8/8.

Exposure was narrower than filed

npm audit -omit=dev was 0 before the change too, so nothing ever reached the shipped bundle. @security-auditor narrowed it further: the CRITICAL is unreachable in this repo at all (it needs a listening Vitest UI server; @vitest/ui is not installed and no script passes -ui), and two of the three vite advisories are Windows-only while the project runs darwin locally and ubuntu-latest in CI. What CI genuinely exposed was the install step, not the six advisories.

Scope additions

  • ADR-009 amended a fifth time (2026-08-20) with the docs/adr/README.md status row moved in step, as AdrIndexConsistencyTest requires. No new ADR — the constraint qualifies a choice ADR-009 already owns and is enforced mechanically by the ^3.2.7 caret. ADR-046 left unconsumed.
  • Five prose surfaces corrected. Four quoted the old versions/floor (AGENTS.md ×2, SETUP.md, docs/devops/local-development.md, ui/Dockerfile's stale dependency count). Separately, five places over-claimed that Node 22.0–22.11 fails npm install with EBADENGINE — with engine-strict unset and no .npmrc, npm warns and installs anyway. engine-strict=true was deliberately not added: it evaluates every package's engines, so it could hard-fail an install over an unrelated transitive declaration. That deserves its own ticket.
  • The EOP-40 CHANGELOG entry was deliberately not retro-edited.
  • Discharges a blocker on another decision: ADR-009's EOP-108 amendment rejected OpenAPI codegen partly because EOP-110 was open against this supply chain. A future codegen re-evaluation now inherits two live grounds, not four.

One new build warning, cosmetic and deliberately unsuppressed

esbuild 0.28 reports govuk-frontend's IE8–11 @media screen\0 hack in its minified CSS. Proved new (built main in a throwaway worktree: zero occurrences) and harmless (identical 140 selectors / 452 @media / 15 screen queries; sole delta @media ( → @media(, accounting for all 620 bytes of reduction). Not suppressed: the only lever silences the whole class and would hide a future CSS error that is genuinely ours.

Definition of Done — five of five

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE — proved vitest 2→3 dropped nothing by querying the installed module's collection globs (identical to v2) and running --reporter=verbose over all 223 cases
@tester-api APPROVE — scope claim verified by empty diffs on src/, docs/api/openapi.yml, ui/src/api.ts; full API integration suite enumerated green
@security-auditor APPROVE — the negative control, the lockfile supply-chain review and the per-advisory reachability analysis
@code-reviewer APPROVE — no blockers; confirmed the EBADENGINE mechanism, the 6 production packages and the vitest/config type augmentation from the installed package
@architecture-guardian APPROVE — reviewed its own stage-1 prose and found two MAJOR defects in it, both fixed

CI on PR #95: build, ui and image all pass — the image job additionally proves the container builds on node:22-alpine with the new toolchain.

Every figure above was re-run by me rather than inherited from a subagent. Two subagent claims were rejected: a fabricated "residual moderate esbuild false positive" (contradicted by its own 0-vulnerability output) and a NIT alleging the Node base image was bumped (the ui/Dockerfile edit is comment-only; FROM node:22-alpine is unchanged).

renderedFields.description:
Found while resolving EOP-106.

The defect

Commit 496d7b5 (2026-08-17) has the subject:

[EOP-63] chore: set Vite dev server port to 5371

Its sole change is ui/vite.config.ts, +1/-1, port: 5173 -> port: 5371.

EOP-63 is "Add EoP card images to docs/EoP_Microsoft_Docs/cards/" — 96 PNG card images. It has nothing to do with the Vite dev server, and it is still in To Do, so the commit was not even a partial delivery of it.

This violates .opencode/rules/git-commits.md, which requires every commit message to start with the uppercase Jira key of the ticket the work belongs to.

Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

The mis-prefix is not merely untidy — it is the mechanical cause of the problem EOP-106 had to spend a whole story unpicking.

Because no ticket described the port change, there was nowhere to record why the port moved. The value 5371 then propagated into four documents, and ADR-009 eventually grew a section guessing at a motive for it ("very likely a typo in the original commit") that turned out to be wrong on both halves. EOP-106 established the truth only by asking the author directly, who confirmed he had simply got the number wrong.

So the chain was: wrong Jira key -> no ticket -> no rationale -> a documented guess -> false-but-authoritative prose in an ADR -> a story to undo it.

What cannot be fixed

496d7b5 is merged into main and its message cannot be rewritten without a force-push that would rewrite shared history. This ticket is not a request to amend it. The historical record is preserved, and the EOP-106 amendment to ADR-009 documents the discrepancy so a future reader who greps for the port's history is not misled by the key.

What could be fixed

The question this ticket exists to answer is whether the convention should be enforced rather than merely documented, given that documentation did not prevent this instance.

Options to consider:

  1. A `commit-msg` git hook in .githooks/ rejecting any message not matching ^[EOP-\d+] (feat|fix|chore|docs|refactor|test|perf): }}. Cheap and immediate, but local-only and bypassable with {{--no-verify, and it cannot tell whether the key is the right one.
  2. A CI check on pull requests validating every commit message in the branch against the same pattern. Not bypassable, but still cannot validate key relevance.
  3. Validating the key exists and is not Done by querying Jira from CI. This is the only option that would have caught this case, since the pattern itself was satisfied — EOP-63 To Do is well-formed, just wrong. Costs a Jira credential in CI.
  4. Accept the convention as review-enforced and close this as won't-do, on the grounds that a reviewer reading a diff of ui/vite.config.ts under a card-images ticket should have caught it.

Option 3 is the only one that addresses the actual failure, and it is also the most expensive. Option 1 or 2 would catch malformed keys but not misapplied ones, so adopting either while claiming the class is closed would be worse than adopting nothing.

A decision either way should be recorded; if enforcement is added it needs an ADR, since it changes what the build gates on.

Acceptance criteria

  • A decision is recorded on which of the four options above is adopted, including "none, review-enforced" as a legitimate outcome with a stated reason.
  • If a hook or CI check is added, it is tested against both a well-formed and a malformed message, and the bypass path (--no-verify, or a direct push if branch protection allows one) is documented rather than left implied.
  • .opencode/rules/git-commits.md is amended to say how the rule is enforced, so the next reader knows whether the build will catch a mistake or only a human will.
  • 496d7b5 is not rewritten.

References

  • Commit 496d7b5 — git show --stat 496d7b5
  • .opencode/rules/git-commits.md
  • EOP-106 — the story that unpicked the consequences; its ADR-009 amendment carries the three-commit history
  • EOP-63 (id 10435) — the unrelated ticket whose key was used

Raised by @architecture-guardian (MINOR) and @security-auditor (F1, F2) during the EOP-58 DoD gate round. Not a defect today — both statements are true — but the same class of drift EOP-58 existed to fix.

EOP-58 changed JoinSessionUseCase.MAXIMUM_SEAT_ATTEMPTS from the literal 8 to GameSession.MAXIMUM_PLAYERS + 2. Two sites still assert the literal:

  • docs/architecture/runtime-view.md:525 — opt all eight attempts lost their race
  • src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/web/SessionContentionIntegrationTest.java:43 — "Seat contention needs every one of the eight attempts to lose its race"

And the Javadoc of the newly-derived constant explains itself with literals: JoinSessionUseCase.java:36-39 says "at most five times" and "keeping the budget above six".

Why it is only MINOR. JoinSessionUseCaseTest.java:50 holds SEAT_ATTEMPTS = 8 and line 328 asserts repository.seatPlayerCalls() equals it against observed behaviour, so changing GameSession.MAXIMUM_PLAYERS turns the build red and puts a human back in front of the budget. The prose is reachable from a forced stop rather than orphaned.

A second consequence, from @security-auditor F1. Deriving the budget also makes worst-case work per join request a derived quantity: roughly 3 DB statements per attempt (SELECT + compare-and-set UPDATE + INSERT), so ~24 statements at a budget of 8. The pinning test asserts only budget > capacity, which any increase to MAXIMUM_PLAYERS satisfies, so nothing in the build would flag a table size of 20 taking the worst case to ~66 statements. + 2 is not intrinsically the right margin for an arbitrary table size.

Suggested scope

  • Reword or derive the two prose sites (a Mermaid label cannot compute, so runtime-view.md:525 may need "every attempt" — note @architecture-guardian judged that less informative, since the number is the point of the opt guard)
  • Consider replacing "five"/"six" in JoinSessionUseCase.java:36-39 with references to GameSession#MAXIMUM_PLAYERS
  • Add one clause to the constant's Javadoc recording that the budget bounds work per request, so whoever changes the table size sees the cost
  • One plausible mechanism is a sixth org.maglez.eop.docs gate in the style of DeckArithmeticClaimsTest, holding the prose number against the computed budget

Constraint

ADR-006's anti-vacuity rule applies to any new guard: it must be able to fail, and if it ever cannot, delete it rather than leave it green.

Raised by @code-reviewer (🟡 Warning) and @security-auditor (F4) during the EOP-58 DoD gate round. Deliberately left out of EOP-58, which was scoped to documentation and Javadoc — this is a change to a user-facing API string that tests and the OpenAPI contract both pin.

The inconsistency

GlobalExceptionHandler.java:870 sets the 409 title:

problem.setTitle("The lobby filled while you were joining");

That asserts fullness as the cause. The Javadoc paragraph EOP-58 added directly above it says the exception is reachable without the lobby being full: under concurrent joins each attempt can pass a fullness check against a snapshot that was already stale, then lose on the uq_player_session_seat constraint, exhausting the attempt budget while seats remain. Five players all joining simultaneously can produce this 409 at a lobby that never reached six.

The detail field is accurate and already says the right thing:

"Another player took the seat on every attempt. Read the session and try again."

So the reconciliation EOP-58 performed on the two Javadocs stops short of the string a caller actually sees. @security-auditor classed this as under-disclosure — conservative, not a leak — so it is a correctness-of-prose issue rather than a security one.

Why it is not a one-line fix

The exact string is asserted and documented in at least two places, so changing it is an API-contract change:

  • src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/web/SessionContentionIntegrationTest.java:83 — jsonPath("$.title").value("The lobby filled while you were joining")
  • docs/api/openapi.yml — the Conflict response component at :1880 (referenced from the join path at :245-246) describes the seat-contention case

Suggested scope

Pick a title that holds in both the quiet-lobby and the concurrent case — e.g. "Another player took every seat you tried" — then update the integration test assertion and the openapi.yml description in the same commit. Alternatively, if the title is kept, qualify the CHANGELOG claim that "the reader who finds one is not misled by the other" to exclude the HTTP response title.

Note the genuinely-full case already leaves through handleSessionFull, so this title is only ever emitted on the contention path.

Raised by @tester-api (MINOR + NIT) during the EOP-58 DoD gate round. Pre-existing; EOP-58 fixed the documentation to match the code, which was the correct direction for a docs ticket.

The question

{{POST /api/v1/sessions/

{joinCode}/players}} creates a Player row and mints an identity token, but answers 200. .opencode/rules/api-design.md specifies 201 for create operations. SessionController.java:151-160 returns a bare SessionAdmissionDto with no @ResponseStatus, so Spring defaults to 200; docs/api/openapi.yml:185-229 and four integration-test helpers all agree on 200, so the contract is at least internally consistent.

Decide deliberately whether to align the implementation with the rule or to record the 200 as an accepted exception. Arguments for 200: the join is idempotent-ish from the caller's view and returns no Location header for the created player, which 201 would ordinarily carry. Arguments for 201: the rule, and createSession on the same controller does return ResponseEntity.created(location).

If the answer is 201, the change touches SessionController plus docs/api/openapi.yml plus SessionContentionIntegrationTest:110, SessionControllerIntegrationTest:120, EndSessionControllerIntegrationTest:199, GameOverControllerIntegrationTest:346, and docs/architecture/runtime-view.md:536 (which EOP-58 has just corrected to 200). If the answer is 200, the exception belongs in an ADR or in api-design.md so the next reviewer does not re-raise it.

h2. Second, smaller finding (NIT)

The 200 contract is pinned only as a side-effect inside setup helpers — e.g. SessionControllerIntegrationTest.java:116-124 asserts status().isOk() while joining in order to proceed. The assertion does execute and would catch a regression, but a helper refactor that dropped it would silently unpin the contract. A named test — {{@DisplayName("POST /{joinCode}

/players returns 200 OK")}} — would make the intent visible. Worth doing whichever way the status question is resolved.

Raised by @security-auditor (F3, pre-existing) during the EOP-58 DoD gate round, while checking a log statement against the observability rules. Not introduced by that story, and the auditor was explicit that it should be owned by a ticket of its own.

The gap

.opencode/rules/observability.md requires structured JSON output via logback-spring.xml for production profiles and an MDC correlation ID (X-Correlation-Id request header → MDC) on every log line. Neither exists:

  • no logging: key in src/main/resources/application.yml or application-prod.yml (the only match is a comment at application.yml:124)
  • no logback-spring.xml anywhere under src/main/resources
  • grep -rln "MDC|X-Correlation-Id" over src/main/java and src/main/resources returns nothing
  • no logstash/ecs-logging encoder in pom.xml

So the root level is Spring Boot's default INFO and output is plain text with no correlation identifier.

A consequence worth knowing

Because the root level is INFO, every LOG.debug in the codebase currently emits nothing in production. That happens to strengthen the reasoning in GlobalExceptionHandler.handleSeatAlreadyTaken — its debug-level, no-stack-trace logging cannot be used as a log-flooding amplifier because it does not log at all — but it also means the debug diagnostics that were deliberately written for operational awareness are unavailable when they are needed. Any fix should decide the intended production level for org.maglez.eop explicitly rather than inheriting a default.

Suggested scope

  • Add logback-spring.xml with a JSON encoder active under the prod profile and human-readable output otherwise (note there are exactly two profiles — default and prod; do not introduce a third)
  • Add a servlet filter or interceptor that reads X-Correlation-Id, generates one when absent, puts it in MDC and clears it in a finally
  • Include the correlation ID in the JSON encoder pattern
  • Set explicit levels for org.maglez.eop in both profiles
  • Do not log PII, secrets, request bodies or identity tokens — the existing handlers are already careful about this and the filter must not undo it
  • A test asserting the MDC value is present and cleared after the request completes

Cross-check against .opencode/rules/observability.md for the per-layer level expectations, and against ADR-026 (use-case observability) before choosing levels.

renderedFields.description:
Three small findings from the EOP-58 DoD gate round, none of which justified holding that ticket and none of which should be silently dropped. Grouped because each is a one- or two-line change.

1. The ADR-006 justification is sited only in the CHANGELOG (@architecture-guardian, MINOR)

EOP-58 chose a test assertion over a runtime guard for the MAXIMUM_SEAT_ATTEMPTS > GameSession.MAXIMUM_PLAYERS invariant, because a guard over two compile-time constants is a branch no input can exercise — the anti-vacuity lesson in ADR-006. That reasoning is correct and correctly applied, but it lives only at CHANGELOG.md:20. The reader tempted to "harden" this by adding if (MAXIMUM_SEAT_ATTEMPTS <= GameSession.MAXIMUM_PLAYERS) throw ... is standing in JoinSessionUseCase.java:31-52 or JoinSessionUseCaseTest.java:331-338, where ADR-006 is not mentioned. Move or copy one clause into the test Javadoc.

2. CHANGELOG and pom.xml disagree on the version string (@code-reviewer, pre-existing)

CHANGELOG.md heads its unreleased section ## [1.0.0-SNAPSHOT]; pom.xml says 1.0-SNAPSHOT. .opencode/rules/versioning.md makes pom.xml the single source of truth and mandates MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, so pom.xml is the one that is wrong — but the two must move in the same commit, per the same rule. Decide which form is intended and align both.

3. The + 2 margin has no independent justification (@code-reviewer, 🔵 Suggestion)

JoinSessionUseCase.java:54 reads GameSession.MAXIMUM_PLAYERS + 2. The cited precedent, SseSessionEventPublisher.MAX_SUBSCRIBERS_PER_SESSION = 2 * GameSession.MAXIMUM_PLAYERS, encodes a ratio with a domain reason (one stale connection per player while reconnecting). + 2 is a slack constant with no such reason, so the expression carries the appearance of a derived relationship where only the > part is meaningful. Either give the margin a stated reason in the Javadoc or note explicitly that it is arbitrary slack above a floor. Overlaps with EOP-112, which covers the same constant from the drift angle — consider doing them together.

Problem

docs/adr/ADR-011-graphify-knowledge-graph.md (Status: Accepted) was written when the repository held 88 lines of Java across 4 files, and every quantity in it dates from that moment. None has been revisited since. The graph rebuilt at commit bc2b089 measures 3531 nodes / 10874 edges / 248 communities; the ADR describes a graph of 151 nodes, 542 edges and 9 communities. That is not drift, it is a different artefact.

This was found while refreshing the Blueprint's Graphify screenshot under EOP-000 (commit 72b5b32) and deliberately left out of scope there, because the fix requires a decision rather than a find-and-replace — see Options below.

Stale claims, with line numbers as of 72b5b32

Line Claim Measured at bc2b089
12 "88 lines of Java across 4 files" far larger; the domain code the graph was installed ahead of now exists
22 "the 27,989 ignored files alongside the 68 committed ones", "24,194 under tools/graphify", "3,652 under .opencode" 38777 ignored, 569 included of 639 candidates
23 "52 of 94 tracked files are Markdown, and the graph contains 8 distinct `source_file` values, none of them Markdown"; "all eleven ADRs" 7 source values (src 2854, git history 441, ui 169, none 33, tools 25, test 7, .opencode 2); 45 ADRs exist
42 "The nine communities carry meaningful names" 248 communities, of which only the first nine are named — the rest are bare Community N. The claim is now true of a small prefix and false of the whole
43 "coverage reached 26/26 describable nodes" 3531 nodes, descriptions: 0/3531 real; the last export emitted 89 unanswered prompt batches
47 "Of 542 edges, 96% are ON_BRANCH, PARENT_OF and MODIFIES. Only 21 edges describe code structure: method (10), contains (9), imports (2). Six of the eight…" 10874 edges; ontology now code 3083, Commit 420, Branch 21, rationale 7 — the git-metadata-dominated conclusion is very likely inverted now and must be re-measured, not re-asserted
48 "query_graph(\"health endpoint\", depth=2) returns 138 of 151 nodes" the ratio needs re-running; the noise-domination conclusion may or may not survive

Two of these carry weight beyond arithmetic. Line 47 is the evidence for the Negative consequence "the graph is mostly git metadata", and line 48 for "retrieval is currently noise-dominated" — so if the ratios have inverted, two of the ADR's recorded consequences are wrong in substance and not merely in their numbers. Line 23 is the evidence for rejecting inputs.corpus; that rejection may still be right, but it is currently argued from a file census that no longer holds.

Options (pick one; this is the decision the ticket exists to make)

  1. Re-pin with dated figures. Amend with a ## Amendments section per house convention, every number stated as of a named commit. Honest, but it is exactly what Blueprint §5.3 stopped doing after pinned counts went 100+ commits stale — it buys another year at most.
  2. De-pin: delete the quantities, keep the reasoning. Point at graphify summary / .graphify/GRAPH_REPORT.md as the authority, the way Blueprint §5.3 already does, and keep only the numbers a decision actually turned on. Preferred unless a reviewer objects — but note it cannot be applied blindly, because the two consequences above are conclusions drawn from ratios, so those must be re-measured and re-stated (or withdrawn) rather than simply unquoted.

Either way, per house convention the original text is superseded in place by a dated note rather than rewritten, so a reader landing mid-document cannot read a stale claim without seeing the correction.

Acceptance criteria

  • AC1 — Every quantity listed above is either corrected against a re-measured graph or removed in favour of pointing at the live authority, with the choice recorded.
  • AC2 — The two ratio-derived consequences (lines 47 and 48, "mostly git metadata" and "noise-dominated retrieval") are re-measured and re-stated or withdrawn. A conclusion may not be left standing on a ratio nobody re-ran.
  • AC3 — The inputs.corpus rejection (line 23) is re-argued from the current file census, or its rejection is confirmed on grounds that do not depend on one.
  • AC4 — Original text is superseded in place by a dated amendment, not silently rewritten.
  • AC5 — If the ADR's status line gains an amendment date, docs/adr/README.md's ADR-011 row is updated in the same commit — AdrIndexConsistencyTest requires every ISO date in a status line to appear in the index row, so omitting it turns the build red.
  • AC6 — ./mvnw verify green, including all five documentation-integrity gates.

Notes

  • ADR-011 lives under docs/, so unlike the Blueprint it is inside the scan root of the documentation-integrity tests — but none of them reads a graph statistic, so nothing here is machine-checkable. Enforcement is review.
  • Rebuild command is ./tools/graphify/node_modules/.bin/graphify update . --description-lang en --label-lang en (CLI pinned repo-locally at 0.17.1); both language flags must always be passed.
  • Do not treat "descriptions are 0/3531" as a regression to fix. ADR-011 itself decided descriptions are not maintained here, and that decision is unaffected by this ticket.

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a developer picking up this codebase

I want to find accurate, complete Javadoc on every public class, method, constructor, and field

So that I can understand the design intent, contracts, and security rationale without having to read the implementation

Context & Business Value

  • Target Persona: Incoming developer / technical handover recipient
  • Value Proposition: The codebase already has Javadoc on virtually every file, but there is no build gate enforcing completeness or accuracy. A new developer cannot trust that a missing @param or @return is intentional. One comment (IdentityTokenHash) is known to be factually wrong and is a false safety certificate. This story closes both gaps before handover.

Scope

Part A — Fix the known inaccurate comment in IdentityTokenHash

IdentityTokenHash Javadoc claims: "Comparison happens as an indexed database lookup rather than in Java, so there is no meaningful timing side channel in this type."

This is factually wrong. The real path is ResolvePlayerUseCase → GameSession.playerByTokenHash → players.stream().filter(p -> p.isIdentifiedBy(hash)) → String.equals — a short-circuiting byte-wise comparison, in Java, in memory. PlayerJpaRepository's own Javadoc says the opposite: "There is no method that finds a player by credential digest."

Fix: Correct the comment to reflect the actual comparison path, and switch the comparison to MessageDigest.isEqual so the claim becomes true rather than merely retracted. This resolves item 1 of EOP-31.

Part B — Add maven-javadoc-plugin with strict enforcement

Add maven-javadoc-plugin to pom.xml bound to the verify phase with:

  • failOnError=true
  • failOnWarnings=true
  • Full doclint enabled (all groups: accessibility, html, missing, reference, syntax) — this catches missing @param, @return, @throws tags as well as absent class-level comments

Two-phase delivery approach (important):

  1. First, run ./mvnw javadoc:javadoc locally (without binding to verify) to surface all gaps.
  2. Fix every warning/error across all ~157 source files.
  3. Only then bind the plugin to verify so CI goes green on the first attempt.

Do not merge a commit that binds the plugin to verify while warnings remain — the build must be green before the gate is wired in.

Part C — Verify the build stays green

./mvnw verify must pass with the plugin active, including all existing unit and integration tests.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: Build fails on missing Javadoc

  • Given maven-javadoc-plugin is bound to the verify phase with failOnWarnings=true
  • And a public class, method, constructor, or field has no /** Javadoc block
  • When ./mvnw verify is run
  • Then the build fails with a Javadoc warning identifying the missing comment

Scenario 2: Build fails on malformed Javadoc (missing tags)

  • Given a public method has a /** block but is missing a @param, @return, or @throws tag for a declared parameter, return type, or checked exception
  • When ./mvnw verify is run
  • Then the build fails with a doclint warning identifying the specific gap

Scenario 3: IdentityTokenHash comment is accurate

  • Given the corrected IdentityTokenHash Javadoc
  • When a developer reads it
  • Then it accurately describes the in-memory MessageDigest.isEqual comparison path, with no claim of a database-indexed lookup

Scenario 4: MessageDigest.isEqual is used for token hash comparison

  • Given IdentityTokenHash.isIdentifiedBy (or equivalent comparison method)
  • When two hashes are compared
  • Then MessageDigest.isEqual is used, making the constant-time claim true

Scenario 5: Full build passes

  • Given all Javadoc gaps are fixed and the plugin is bound to verify
  • When ./mvnw verify is run
  • Then the build is green with zero Javadoc warnings or errors

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • maven-javadoc-plugin added to pom.xml, bound to verify, with failOnError=true, failOnWarnings=true, and full doclint enabled.
  • All public classes, methods, constructors, and fields in src/main/java have complete, accurate Javadoc.
  • IdentityTokenHash comment corrected; comparison uses MessageDigest.isEqual.
  • EOP-31 item 1 is resolved and noted in EOP-31.
  • ./mvnw verify passes green with the plugin active.
  • No security regressions introduced.
  • CHANGELOG.md updated under ## [Unreleased].

Notes for the Tech Lead

  • Run ./mvnw javadoc:javadoc first (without binding to verify) to get the full list of gaps before touching CI.
  • src/test/java is excluded from Javadoc enforcement by default — test classes do not need @param/@return tags.
  • The IdentityTokenHash fix (Part A) is small and can be committed first under this ticket key before tackling the bulk Javadoc sweep.
  • This story resolves EOP-31 item 1 (the IdentityTokenHash false safety certificate). Update EOP-31 accordingly once merged.

Related

  • EOP-31 — item 1 (IdentityTokenHash inaccurate Javadoc) is in scope here and should be closed once this story merges.

*Delivered. PR open for human approval: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/103*

Branch EOP-120-javadoc-enforcement, eight commits on main (a89760c).

All five Definition-of-Done gates approved

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE
@tester-api APPROVE
@security-auditor APPROVE
@code-reviewer APPROVE
@architecture-guardian APPROVE

It took six rounds, with four rejections. Every rejection was correct, and each is worth recording because they were all the same defect class this story exists to remove — prose asserting a mechanism the artefact does not contain:

  1. The false lookup claim survived at a fourth site — an XML comment directly above the addUniqueConstraint in 003-session-lifecycle.xml, in a stronger form than the original. My commit message had asserted a repo-wide grep confirmed no fourth site; it did not.
  2. I claimed debug=true fixed the Unable to compute stale date failure and cited a reproduction as verification. A five-attempt controlled experiment with the flag removed falsified it. Retracted at all four sites; the failure is now recorded as observed and unexplained.
  3. My "corrected" Maven plugin inventory named liquibase-maven-plugin as a peer plugin (it is not declared, though it is parent-managed at 5.0.3 without a lifecycle binding), and claimed maven-enforcer-plugin resolved from remote metadata (it was already parent-managed at 3.6.3 by spring-boot-dependencies). Both were guesses stated with the precision of measurements. Fixed by parsing the effective pom.
  4. The commit that fixed the prose garbled the prose — a search/replace applied twice, doubling clauses in .opencode/rules/build-quality.md, a file injected into every agent's context.

Acceptance criteria

Criterion Evidence
Build fails on missing Javadoc Checkstyle MissingJavadocType / MissingJavadocMethod at scope=public, minLineCount=-1, allowMissingPropertyJavadoc=false; JavadocMethod with both allowMissing*Tags=false. failOnViolation=true at the validate phase
Build fails on malformed Javadoc maven-javadoc-plugin 3.11.2, javadoc-no-fork at verify, failOnError, failOnWarnings, doclint=all,-missing. A deliberately broken {{ {@link}}} was injected and failed the build|
|IdentityTokenHash comment accurate|False paragraph replaced; verified against this JDK's MessageDigest source|
|MessageDigest.isEqual used|IdentityTokenHash.java:135, guarded by a source-text test so a silent revert to the generated equals fails|
|Full build green|./mvnw clean verify exit 0|

h2. Verification

./mvnw clean verify → exit 0. 1256 tests, 0 failures/errors/skips. 0 Checkstyle violations. javadoc:3.11.2:javadoc-no-fork on the cold path (No previous run data found, generating javadoc.). SpotBugs BugInstance size is 0. JaCoCo All coverage checks have been met, 141 classes. enforcer:3.6.3 with three rules passed.

h2. What the measurement actually showed

The useful finding is that there was almost no documentation debt. Tightening Checkstyle to full strictness surfaced exactly one violation across 157 files, plus four genuine public-API gaps and two hard doclint errors. The existing Javadoc was already complete with @param/@return tags — the lax settings had been hiding nearly nothing.

h2. Known limitations, recorded rather than smoothed over

* A comment-only edit to a `.java` file can now turn `./mvnw verify` red.
* A warm target/ may log Skipping javadoc generation…, and that is not proof the goal re-analysed your edit: the staleness record holds 117 paths, 92 jars, zero .java. CI is always cold, so merges are gated on full analysis; use clean verify locally after comment-only changes.
* One Unable to compute stale date failure remains observed and unexplained. clean is the workaround.
* Both Checkstyle Javadoc modules are scope=public, so an undocumented protected member on a public non-final class is uncaught. No live instance today; recorded in ADR-006 as a future amendment.
* maven-javadoc-plugin is not covered by tools/supply-chain/. The whole Maven layer is uncovered: fourteen bound entries against thirty-one managed, so bumping the Boot parent moves about thirty plugin versions in one line.

h2. Recorded durably

ADR-006 gains a 2026-08-20 (EOP-120) amendment for the sixth gate — and states plainly that its own "Plugins pinned to specific versions" line was inexact when written and remains inexact, since five of six declared plugins carry a version here. ADR-015 gains an amendment for constant-time comparison and the standing prohibition on keying a hash-based collection on IdentityTokenHash or Player. .opencode/rules/build-quality.md gains a sixth gate bullet; .opencode/rules/clean-architecture.md gains the {@code}not{{{@link}

}} rule for inner layers naming outer types.

Out of scope, with follow-up filed

src/test/java is not covered, and no package-info.java exists across the eight class-holding packages. EOP-121 is filed for those plus a MissingJavadocPackage module.

Item 1 of EOP-31 is closed by this work and noted on that ticket.

Closing evidence — all three parts delivered and merged

Status changed To Do → Done. The work was already delivered and merged before this transition; only the ticket had gone stale. Merged via PR #103, merge commit c1ef080, branch EOP-120-javadoc-enforcement.

See also the earlier comment of 2026-08-20 21:35, which records the five-gate DoD round in full. This comment adds independent re-verification of the merged result, plus two corrections to statements made in an earlier draft of it (below).

Part A — IdentityTokenHash corrected, comparison made constant-time

IdentityTokenHash.java:135 is now return MessageDigest.isEqual(asciiBytes(), candidate.asciiBytes());, replacing the short-circuiting String.equals a record would generate. The Javadoc now states that comparison happens in Java, in memory, and not as a database lookup (line 22), and points at Player#isIdentifiedBy (line 24). Locked against silent regression by IdentityTokenHashTest.java:168, which asserts the source text contains the MessageDigest.isEqual(...) call.

The real path the old comment misdescribed is GameSession.java:251 — players.stream().filter(player -> player.isIdentifiedBy(tokenHash)).findFirst().

Part B — javadoc gate added, with one deliberate deviation

maven-javadoc-plugin 3.11.2, bound to verify as execution verify-javadoc, goal javadoc-no-fork (plain javadoc forks a generate-sources lifecycle and re-runs earlier phases), with failOnError=true, failOnWarnings=true, show=public.

Deviation from the brief: the story asked for full doclint with all five groups including missing. Delivered config is doclint=all,-missing — a two-tool split in which Checkstyle owns missing and the javadoc plugin owns malformed (accessibility, html, reference, syntax).

Why, recorded in ADR-006 and CHANGELOG.md:

  • doclint's missing group ignores javadoc's -public flag and demands a comment on every private field — roughly 50 findings across the domain exception classes, none of them public API.
  • The apparent scoping fix doclint=all/protected is rejected outright: error: Access qualifiers not permitted for -Xdoclint arguments.

The missing half therefore landed in checkstyle.xml:74-95: new MissingJavadocType; MissingJavadocMethod with minLineCount 10 → -1 and allowMissingPropertyJavadoc → false; JavadocMethod with allowMissingParamTags and allowMissingReturnTag both → false; all at scope=public.

The tightening surfaced one Checkstyle violation, four genuine public-API gaps (ScoredPlay#components, two record-component @param tags on LeaderboardResult, one @param on TrickRepository#openTrick) and two hard doclint errors. The useful finding is that there was almost no documentation debt — the lax settings had been hiding nearly nothing.

Part C — build green on the cold path

./mvnw clean verify → exit 0. javadoc:3.11.2:javadoc-no-fork (verify-javadoc) ran with no "Skipping javadoc generation" line, so the gate genuinely analysed rather than hitting the documented warm-target/ false green. Tests run: 1256, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0. SpotBugs check and JaCoCo check-coverage both ran. BUILD SUCCESS.

AC1 / AC2 — proven empirically, not merely reasoned about

Verified by injecting deliberate violations into Main.java, then reverting:

  • Missing Javadoc and missing tags → ./mvnw checkstyle:check exit 1, with exactly three errors: MissingJavadocMethod: Missing a Javadoc comment., JavadocMethod: @return tag should be present and have description., JavadocMethod: Expected @param tag for 'undocumented'.
  • Malformed reference → an unresolvable {{ {@link}}} gave ./mvnw javadoc:javadoc-no-fork exit 1 with error: reference not found. This confirms the plugin half is load-bearing rather than decorative, which matters precisely because Checkstyle does all the missing work.

    After reverting, git status --porcelain is empty and both goals return exit 0.

    Note on AC wording: AC1 and AC2 are satisfied in outcome, but by a different mechanism than their text names. They attribute the build failure to a maven-javadoc-plugin doclint warning; it is in fact Checkstyle that fails the build. The required outcome holds; the attribution does not. Documented in ADR-006.

    h3. Two corrections to an earlier draft of this comment

    Both were claims stated more confidently than the evidence supported — the same defect class this story exists to remove, so they are corrected in place rather than quietly dropped:

    # I wrote that the false lookup claim existed at three sites. It was four. The fourth was an XML comment directly above the addUniqueConstraint in db/changelog/changes/003-session-lifecycle.xml, stating the claim in a stronger form than the original — which is why PR #103 touches that changelog at all.
    # I wrote that two gates initially rejected. The actual record is six rounds with four rejections, all four correct. One of them falsified a claim I had made that debug=true fixed the Unable to compute stale date failure; a five-attempt controlled experiment with the flag removed disproved it, and the failure now stands recorded as observed and unexplained, with clean as the workaround.

    h3. Documentation

    ADR-006 gains a 2026-08-20 (EOP-120) amendment for the sixth gate, and states plainly that its own "Plugins pinned to specific versions" line was inexact when written. ADR-015 gains an amendment for constant-time comparison and the standing prohibition on keying a hash-based collection on IdentityTokenHash or Player. .opencode/rules/build-quality.md gains a sixth gate bullet; .opencode/rules/clean-architecture.md gains the {@code}not{{{@link}

    }} rule for inner layers naming outer types. CHANGELOG.md updated under ## [Unreleased].

Known limitations, recorded rather than smoothed over

  • A comment-only edit to a .java file can now turn ./mvnw verify red.
  • A warm target/ may log Skipping javadoc generation…, and that is not proof the goal re-analysed your edit: the staleness record holds 117 paths, 92 of them jars, and zero .java. CI is always cold, so merges are gated on full analysis; use clean verify locally after comment-only changes.
  • Both Checkstyle Javadoc modules are scope=public, so an undocumented protected member on a public non-final class is uncaught. No live instance today.
  • maven-javadoc-plugin is not covered by tools/supply-chain/, which audits the OpenCode npm plugins only. The whole Maven layer is uncovered.

Out of scope, with follow-up filed

src/test/java is not covered, and no package-info.java exists across the eight class-holding packages. EOP-121 is filed for those plus a MissingJavadocPackage module.

EOP-31 item 1 is closed by this work and noted on that ticket; its items 2–7 remain open, so EOP-31 stays in To Do.

renderedFields.description:
Context

EOP-120 made Javadoc a build gate on every public member — MissingJavadocType, MissingJavadocMethod and JavadocMethod in checkstyle.xml, all pinned to scope=public, plus maven-javadoc-plugin 3.11.2 owning malformed markup via doclint=all,-missing.

Packages were deliberately left out, because a package is not a public member and it sat outside EOP-120's acceptance criteria. ADR-006's 2026-08-20 (EOP-120) amendment names this as the deferred proposal.

Measured today: find src/main/java -name 'package-info.java' returns zero files, across eight class-holding packages:

  • org.maglez
  • org.maglez.eop.config
  • org.maglez.eop.entity
  • org.maglez.eop.usecase
  • org.maglez.eop.adapter.persistence
  • org.maglez.eop.adapter.scheduling
  • org.maglez.eop.adapter.security
  • org.maglez.eop.adapter.web

Why it is worth doing

EOP-120 was motivated by handover — the project may pass to another engineer. Per-member Javadoc tells a reader what a method does; it does not tell them why a layer exists or what may depend on what. A package overview is where the Clean Architecture story lands for someone reading the source rather than docs/: that entity/ has zero framework imports, that usecase/ holds ports the adapters implement, that config/ wires use cases so Spring imports stay out of the inner layers.

Scope

  1. Add a package-info.java to each of the eight packages, each carrying a short layer overview and its dependency direction.
  2. Add MissingJavadocPackage to checkstyle.xml so a ninth package cannot be added without one.
  3. Amend ADR-006's EOP-120 block (do not add a new amendment date unless the work lands on a different day) to record that the deferred proposal was taken up.
  4. Update .opencode/rules/build-quality.md's Checkstyle bullet to name package Javadoc alongside type and method Javadoc.

Admission test

ADR-006's EOP-35 block sets the precedent for an "admission test" — a test that fails if the configuration this ticket adds is ever silently removed. Follow it: a test in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ asserting checkstyle.xml carries a MissingJavadocPackage module, in the style of LiquibaseContextGatingAbsentTest.

Note the known limitation of that family, recorded in build-quality.md: their coverage is a hand-written list, so nothing detects a ninth package added without a row. MissingJavadocPackage is what closes that, which is why the module matters more than the eight files.

Acceptance criteria

Scenario: every package carries an overview
  Given a class-holding package under src/main/java
  Then it contains a package-info.java with a Javadoc comment

Scenario: the build refuses a package without an overview
  Given checkstyle.xml carries MissingJavadocPackage
  When a new package is added with no package-info.java
  Then ./mvnw verify fails

Scenario: the gate cannot be silently removed
  Given the admission test in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/
  When MissingJavadocPackage is deleted from checkstyle.xml
  Then that test fails

Scenario: the build is green
  When ./mvnw clean verify runs
  Then it exits 0 with zero Checkstyle violations

Definition of Done

  • Eight package-info.java files, each stating the layer's purpose and dependency direction
  • MissingJavadocPackage in checkstyle.xml
  • Admission test present and failing if the module is removed
  • ADR-006's EOP-120 block records the proposal as taken up
  • .opencode/rules/build-quality.md Checkstyle bullet updated
  • ./mvnw clean verify exits 0 with zero Checkstyle violations
  • CHANGELOG.md updated under ## [Unreleased]

Notes

Low priority: this is a readability and onboarding improvement, not a correctness or security matter. It is cheap and self-contained — eight small files plus one Checkstyle module — and needs no Java change.

Related: EOP-120, ADR-006 (as amended 2026-08-20).

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @architecture-guardian (finding F-1, MEDIUM) during the EOP-35 / EOP-40 / EOP-108 Definition-of-Done gate round. Approved-but-open: it did not block those tickets, but it is a recurrence of the exact defect class EOP-35 was raised to eliminate.

Problem

.opencode/rules/build-quality.md:6 asserts that Liquibase is "parent-managed at 5.0.3 in the effective pluginManagement, with no lifecycle binding, so it never runs", and cites "ADR-006 as amended 2026-08-20 (EOP-120)" as its authority.

The cited home does not contain the cited claim. grep -n 'liquibase|Liquibase' docs/adr/ADR-006-build-quality-gates.md returns only lines 53, 57 and 59, and the single 5.0.3 mention there (ADR-006:59) states a different proposition — that liquibase-core 5.0.3 reads contextFilter first (ChangeSet.java:432-434), an attribute-precedence fact about the library, not a statement about the Maven pluginManagement layer.

So a version literal sits in a hot-path rule file — injected into every agent's context every session — with no dated, supersedable home. That is precisely the finding that produced EOP-35 and ADR-043.

Four of the five version literals on that line do have a proper home (maven-javadoc-plugin 3.11.2, Boot-owned 3.12.0, maven-enforcer-plugin 3.6.3, spring-boot-maven-plugin 4.1.0 are all covered at ADR-006:100). Only the liquibase one is homeless.

Acceptance criteria

  • Either (a) the pluginManagement / 5.0.3 / no-lifecycle-binding proposition is added to docs/adr/ADR-006-build-quality-gates.md as a dated amendment, with the ADR's *Status: line updated accordingly; *or (b) the version literal is dropped from .opencode/rules/build-quality.md:6 and the fact stated without it.
  • If (a): docs/adr/README.md's ADR-006 row is updated so AdrIndexConsistencyTest still passes — note shouldCarryAmendmentDates requires every ISO date in the status line to appear in the index cell.
  • No version literal remains anywhere in .opencode/rules/ without a dated supersedable home.
  • ./mvnw verify green.

Notes

Do not resolve this by weakening the claim into vagueness — the fact is true and useful; it needs a home, not deletion, unless option (b) is chosen deliberately.

comments.body:
Resolved via option (b) — literal dropped, not homed. PR #104, three commits, all five DoD gates approved.

Disposition

Option (b) was chosen deliberately, as the ticket permits. AC 2 is therefore not applicable — docs/adr/ADR-006-build-quality-gates.md was not amended, its *Status:* line is untouched, docs/adr/README.md is untouched, and git diff main...HEAD – docs/ returns zero lines. @architecture-guardian ruled independently that option (a) would have been the wrong disposition and that it would have rejected it: an ADR records a decision this project made, and "the Boot parent happens to resolve liquibase to 5.0.3" is not a decision we took — no alternatives weighed, no consequence accepted — so it would have produced a decision record with no decision in it, while mis-signalling that the value is under our control.

The ticket's prohibition was honoured — no proposition was weakened. All four operative claims survive, and two gained precision:

Proposition Before After
liquibase is not one of the declared plugins ✓ ✓
liquibase-core executes during tests as an application dependency ✓ ✓
we declare no liquibase-maven-plugin ✓ ✓
the parent nonetheless manages one "it is parent-managed" "the Boot parent does carry one" — source named
nothing binds it, so it never runs "no lifecycle binding" "no <executions> and no <configuration>, so nothing binds it to a phase" — mechanism named
the version is 5.0.3 stated dropped, with the reason and the recovery command given

The new text also carries a standing instruction — "do not helpfully restore a literal" — at the exact site a future author would restore it, matching the prose-enforcement precedent database.md uses for the frozen NNN- sequence.

Grounds, ranked

@architecture-guardian required these be ranked rather than listed as equals, because one of them proves too much if cited alone:

  1. Guidance weight — decisive. Every operative proposition is true at any version, so the number was inert. A reader who knows 5.0.3 can do nothing they could not do without it.
  2. Not ours to pin — supporting only. It comes from the Boot parent's liquibase.version. But this cannot be the discriminator: the Boot-owned 3.12.0 on the same line is equally not ours to pin, yet correctly stays homed at ADR-006:100, because it is quoted contrastively to state we deliberately sit behind the parent at 3.11.2 — strip it and that proposition becomes unstatable. Guidance weight is the discriminator, not ownership. Anyone citing this precedent must lead with ground 1.
  3. Conflation risk. Of fifteen tracked 5.0.3 text sites, twelve concern liquibase-core — including ADR-006:59, the ADR's only mention, which states an unrelated contextFilter-precedence fact. Option (a) would have dropped a plugin assertion into the middle of that cluster, forty lines away.

AC 1 — met

grep -n '5\.0\.3' .opencode/rules/build-quality.md returns nothing.

AC 3 — met, with the full sweep

Site Literal Home
build-quality.md:6 3.11.2, 3.12.0, 3.6.3, 4.1.0 ADR-006:100/:102
build-quality.md:6 5.0.3 removed
build-quality.md:5 JDK ≥ 21 enforcer rule — mechanically enforced, not a pin
performance-testing.md:7 influxdb:1.8 docker-compose.yml:9 — now cited inline
versioning.md:1 SemVer 2.0.0 ADR-007:13/:37 — a spec version, immutable by definition
versioning.md:2 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT illustrative; corresponds to no real version, so nothing to diverge from

On the one judgement call: @architecture-guardian ruled decisively that docker-compose.yml:9 is an acceptable "dated supersedable home" — it is not a copy of the truth, it is the pin, executable, with version control supplying dating and commits supplying supersession. Demanding an ADR would create a second copy a compose bump silently falsifies, reinstating EOP-35's defect one file over. Reading AC 3 as "every literal needs an ADR" would absurdly force one for 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT.

performance-testing.md was also tightened: 1.8 appeared twice on main (lines 7 and 89), stated free-standing and attributed to nothing. It now appears once, at its citation.

AC 4 — met

./mvnw verify → Tests run: 1256, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS. Verified on the cold path too (./mvnw clean verify, full javadoc analysis). CI green on the exact SHA — run 32418426157, conclusion: success. All five documentation-integrity gates pass; none scans the three changed paths, and no test reads .opencode/rules/ at all (the single grep hit is a Javadoc mention at SessionLifecycleOffValueIntegrationTest.java:34).

DoD gate round — 5/5 approved

@tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian all returned VERDICT: APPROVE. Every one independently re-ran ./mvnw verify. Two gates rejected material and were remediated rather than argued with:

  • @code-reviewer challenged the entry's 31/14 effective-pom figures, reporting 34/17 with duplicates. I measured rather than conceding: direct <plugin> children are 31 and 14 with zero duplicates. Its 34/17 counted .//artifactId descendants, which pick up coordinates nested in <configuration>/<dependencies> blocks — hence the identical +3 offset in both sections and the phantom duplicates. It re-measured and withdrew both warnings. Corroborated four ways: my parse, @security-auditor's, @architecture-guardian's, and pom.xml's own EOP-120 figures.
  • @architecture-guardian found the CHANGELOG entry's own census was wrong — it said thirteen sites and claimed every one was liquibase-core, when the true figures are fifteen and twelve, with three plugin claims (pom.xml:164, CHANGELOG.md:59, CHANGELOG.md:20). Correct on all three sub-claims; fixed in commit three, which also records the trap that caused it: git grep emits Binary file … matches as a line, so three tracked PDFs under docs/EoP_Microsoft_Docs/ inflated the denominator while two CHANGELOG.md lines fell out of it. It also found the "doubled the stale-literal surface" claim false — see below — and both findings are now discharged.

Two findings deferred, both filed rather than dropped

  • EOP-126 — pom.xml:164 still carries a standing liquibase-maven-plugin 5.0.3 claim, same value, same parent property, same absence of any test. Found independently by @security-auditor and @architecture-guardian. It means this change's surface for the coordinate went from two sites to one, not zero to two averted, and the CHANGELOG entry was corrected to say so — shipping an overstating entry on a ticket about overstated claims would have been self-defeating. Deferred because it is outside AC 3's .opencode/rules/ scope, is co-located with the parent declaration that produces the value rather than sitting in a file injected into every agent's context every session, and does not contradict the new rule text; @architecture-guardian agreed, calling it un-tested rather than homeless.
  • EOP-127 — docker-compose.yml:9 homes InfluxDB's value, but ADR-016 records no rationale for the 1.x line, which matters because 2.x changed the write API and that write path is exactly what ADR-016 records as broken.

No new automated guard, with reasoning rather than omission

@architecture-guardian killed the obvious candidate explicitly: a RuleFileVersionLiteralHomeTest scanning .opencode/rules/.md for version-shaped strings and requiring each to appear in an authority file *would have PASSED F-1 — 5.0.3 was present at ADR-006:59 and eleven other authoritative sites. The defect was an unhomed proposition, and no digit matcher can distinguish liquibase-maven-plugin 5.0.3 from liquibase-core 5.0.3. A gate reporting "all literals homed" on the very tree containing this defect would be worse than no gate. The only structurally expressible neighbour — a dangling-ADR-citation check — would not have caught it either, since "ADR-006 as amended 2026-08-20" is a structurally valid citation. Enforcement stays with review plus the in-place inoculation.

State

PR #104 → main, three commits (fade9a2, 4273083, 4342a89), CI green, 5/5 gates approved. Awaiting human merge — not self-merged.

Closed — PR #104 merged by a human, all four ACs independently re-verified against origin/main, CI green.

Transitioned to Done. The work itself landed on 2026-08-20; this comment records the verification that justified closing the ticket rather than any new change. No file was modified and no gate was dispatched in this session — see the honesty note at the end.

Merge is real and human-approved

PR #104 EOP-122 Done docs: drop the homeless liquibase version literal from build-quality.md, head EOP-122-liquibase-version-literal-home @ 4342a89 → base main @ c1ef080. State closed, merged: true, merged at 2026-08-20T21:57:15Z by `miguel-gonzalez-gca-gov-uk` — a human, consistent with the previous comment's "awaiting human merge — not self-merged". Three commits, three changed files, +5 / −3: .opencode/rules/build-quality.md, .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md, CHANGELOG.md. Zero lines under docs/, as option (b) requires.

AC re-verification

Verified against origin/main via git grep / git show rather than by checking out main, because unrelated EOP-86 / EOP-87 work is in flight on the current branch.

AC Result Evidence
1 — literal dropped met git grep -nE '5\.0\.3' origin/main – .opencode/rules/ → no match
2 — ADR index n/a option (b): ADR-006 and docs/adr/README.md untouched, so AdrIndexConsistencyTest is not implicated
3 — no unhomed literal in .opencode/rules/ met at current `main` HEAD full sweep below
4 — build green met CI run `32421960111` (run 298) on merge commit d4deccf → conclusion: success

AC 4 is stronger than the branch-SHA run cited previously. The earlier comment recorded run 32418426157 on the branch tip; the run above is on the merge commit, so main itself is proven green, as is every subsequent main run through 32523482668 on f1baad6.

AC 3 was re-checked at today's `main` HEAD, not at the merge point — the check that actually matters, since four PRs landed after #104 (#105 EOP-41/[EOP-49|https://maglez.atlassian.net/browse/EOP-49], #106 EOP-31, #107 EOP-67, #108 MODEL_F) and any of them could have reintroduced a literal. None did. A sweep for [0-9]\.[0-9](\.[0-9]+)? across .opencode/rules/*.md returns exactly five lines, all accounted for:

  • build-quality.md:6 — 3.11.2, 3.12.0, 3.6.3, 4.1.0, all homed at ADR-006:100
  • performance-testing.md:7 — influxdb:1.8, homed at docker-compose.yml and now cited inline
  • performance-testing.md:33 — 0.001 / 0.1%, SLO thresholds rather than versions
  • versioning.md:1 — SemVer 2.0.0, a spec version, homed at ADR-007:13/:37
  • versioning.md:2 — 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT → v1.2.0, illustrative and asserting nothing

The duplicate InfluxDB 1.8 that stood free-standing at old line 89 is confirmed gone, so that version is now stated once, at its citation — the secondary tightening claimed in the previous comment holds.

The replacement text does what it claims

origin/main:.opencode/rules/build-quality.md:6 retains all four operative propositions and names both the source and the mechanism: "…though the Boot parent *does* carry one in the effective `pluginManagement`, as a bare entry with coordinates and a version but no `<executions>` and no `<configuration>`, so nothing binds it to a phase and it never runs. That version is deliberately not quoted here… Read it off `./mvnw help:effective-pom` when you need it, and *do not helpfully restore a literal*." No proposition was weakened, and the recovery command means nothing was lost that a reader cannot reconstruct on demand.

The CHANGELOG.md entry landed under ## [Unreleased] carrying the corrected fifteen-sites / twelve-liquibase-core census, the ranked grounds, the git grep binary-file trap, and the explicit disclosure that pom.xml:164 survives — so the entry states the surface went from two sites to one rather than overstating the fix. @architecture-guardian's rejection is discharged in the shipped artefact, not just in the reply to it.

One observation, outside AC 3's scope and deliberately not actioned: the EOP-120 entry now at CHANGELOG.md:71 still contains a "parent-managed at 5.0.3 without a lifecycle binding" phrase. It is left alone because it is a dated record of what was measured on a date — exactly the distinction the EOP-122 entry itself draws between a dated record and a standing claim. Editing it would falsify history to satisfy a grep.

Deferred findings confirmed filed, not dropped

Both exist, both are To Do, both are linked to this ticket as Relates: EOP-126 (pom.xml:164 carries a standing liquibase-maven-plugin 5.0.3 claim with no test) and EOP-127 (ADR-016 records no rationale for the InfluxDB 1.x line). Closing this ticket therefore does not retire either.

Honesty note on the Definition-of-Done gate

The 5/5 approvals belong to the prior session's record (comment above), not to this one. I authored no artefact here and dispatched no gate agent, so presenting those verdicts as mine would be a fabrication of exactly the kind the DoD rules forbid. What this session contributes is independent confirmation of the externally checkable facts a gate round cannot substitute for: that the PR was merged by a named human, that CI passed on the merge commit, that all four ACs still hold at today's main, and that the two deferred findings were really filed. Those are verification of a merged change, not a sixth approval.

Local branch EOP-122-liquibase-version-literal-home deleted.

Problem

docs/adr/ADR-045-frontend-response-validation.md:60 — the row rejecting Zod/Valibot in the decision table — argues in the present tense:

"EOP-110 is already open against six CVEs in the ui/ dev toolchain — appetite for new supply-chain surface is at its lowest."

But it has no test whatsoever in ui/src/api.test.ts — not a happy path (204 resolves void), not an error path (non-ok throws ApiError).

A regression in startNewGame's error handling would go undetected by the unit suite.

  • Both cases stub global fetch via the existing helper rather than using vi.spyOn(api, …) — a spy bypasses the module under test and is not evidence it works.
  • Mirror the shape of the existing dealCards cases so the two structurally identical helpers are tested consistently.
  • npm run verify in ui/ green; ./mvnw verify green.
