Raised by @architecture-guardian (finding F-3, LOW, recommended) during the EOP-35 / EOP-40 / EOP-108 Definition-of-Done gate round.

Problem

EOP-35 removed a liquibase-core 5.0.3 pin from .opencode/rules/database.md because a hot-path rule file has no *Status:, no Date: and no supersession mechanism, so a version claim in one can never be retired. *It fixed the instance and established no invariant — and the defect has already recurred (see the sibling ticket on build-quality.md:6, filed from finding F-1 in the same round).

No build gate reads .opencode/rules/ at all. All five documentation-integrity guards in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ are scoped to docs/*, src/*, docs/api/openapi.yml and ui/src/api.ts.

Measured during the gate round:

Metric At the EOP-35 finding Now
.opencode/rules/database.md 63 L / ~4,600 B 70 L / 6,408 B
its context bullet 1,858 B 1,340 B (−28%)
bullet share of its file 40.4% 20.9%
largest rule file — build-quality.md at 8,977 B
its single longest line — 4,585 B — 3.4× the bullet EOP-35 excised, carrying five version literals
.opencode/rules/ total — 38,259 B injected into every agent session

Proposal

A guard in the style of src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ asserting that no semantic-version literal appears in .opencode/rules/** without an accompanying ADR-0NN citation on the same line. This would have caught finding F-1 automatically.

Acceptance criteria

  • A new test fails the build on a semver literal in .opencode/rules/** that carries no ADR citation.
  • It carries its own anti-vacuity assertion, in the style of DeckArithmeticClaimsTest.shouldNotClaimTheDealIsUnevenAtEveryTableSize (:180-183), so it cannot silently degrade to matching nothing.
  • Its scope is a documented, closed enumeration — follow the principle ADR-006:59 states for this guard class ("a closed enumeration of the spellings the schema accepts, and must be revisited when the schema admits another").
  • Existing violations are either fixed or explicitly allowlisted with a traced reason; the guard is not introduced with a blanket exemption.
  • Recorded as a dated amendment to ADR-006, with docs/adr/README.md updated so AdrIndexConsistencyTest passes.
  • ./mvnw verify green.

Caution

Scope this to .opencode/rules/* only. Do *not extend it to docs/** in the same change — ADRs are supposed to carry version literals; that is the whole point of their being dated and supersedable.

Raised by @security-auditor (INFO) and @architecture-guardian (LOW), independently, during the EOP-122 DoD gate round. Approved-but-open; deliberately deferred rather than fixed inline.

Problem

EOP-122 removed the homeless liquibase-maven-plugin 5.0.3 literal from .opencode/rules/build-quality.md:6. A second standing claim of the same fact survives at pom.xml:164, in the EOP-120 comment block on the javadoc plugin:

Liquibase is not one of the six and never executes, but do not say it is unmanaged either: liquibase-maven-plugin sits in the effective pluginManagement at 5.0.3, parent-managed with no lifecycle binding, and liquibase-core runs during tests as an application dependency, which is a different thing again.

The drift argument EOP-122 used to justify dropping the rule-file literal applies to this one verbatim: same value, same owner (the Boot parent's own liquibase.version property), same absence of any test. It is a standing, present-tense claim ("sits ... at 5.0.3"), not a dated measurement record, so a Boot bump silently falsifies it with no signal and no failing build.

Inventory

A repo-wide census of 5.0.3 finds fifteen tracked text sites (note git grep also emits three Binary file ... matches notices for tracked PDFs under docs/EoP_Microsoft_Docs/, which are not text sites). Twelve concern liquibase-core. Exactly three are liquibase-maven-plugin claims:

Site Kind Action
pom.xml:164 standing present-tense claim this ticket
CHANGELOG.md:59 dated record (EOP-120 entry) none needed — a dated record states what was measured on a date and cannot go stale the way a standing claim can
CHANGELOG.md:20 dated record (EOP-122 entry) none needed, same reason

So the actionable surface is one site.

Why it was deferred rather than fixed in EOP-122

Both reviewers judged it non-blocking and recommended follow-up. Three grounds:

  1. Outside EOP-122's acceptance criterion 3, which scopes to .opencode/rules/.
  2. It is co-located with its own truth-maker — four lines from the plugin block, in the very file whose parent declaration produces the value — so it is un-tested rather than homeless. That is a materially weaker defect than a literal in a file injected into every agent's context every session.
  3. Widening a documentation-only diff into the build file would have required re-running the whole five-gate DoD round on a broader diff.

Suggested disposition

Either drop the literal on EOP-122's own reasoning (state the fact, name ./mvnw help:effective-pom as the way to read the value off), or convert the comment from a standing claim into a dated measurement record. Do not simply delete the surrounding sentence — its operative propositions are true and useful: liquibase is not one of the six declared plugins, the parent nonetheless manages one, nothing binds it to a phase, and liquibase-core running during tests as an application dependency is a different thing again.

Note for whoever picks this up: the same comment block states "the effective build/plugins binds fourteen entries" and "the effective pluginManagement carries thirty-one". Both figures are correct — verified three times during EOP-122 by parsing the effective POM for direct plugin children. Counting .//artifactId descendants instead yields 34/17 and phantom duplicates, because it picks up coordinates nested inside plugin configuration and dependencies blocks. Do not "correct" 31/14.

Acceptance criteria

  1. pom.xml no longer carries a standing present-tense claim about the liquibase-maven-plugin version, with the operative propositions preserved.
  2. No new copy of the value is created elsewhere.
  3. ./mvnw verify green.
  4. CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @architecture-guardian as a LOW finding, carried across all three rounds of the EOP-122 DoD gate round. Pre-existing; outside EOP-122's scope.

Problem

docker-compose.yml:9 pins image: influxdb:1.8, and EOP-122 anchored .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md:7 to that pin so the value now has a home. The rationale has none. ADR-016 mentions InfluxDB only at :66 (a sizing remark) and :149-150 (the known-broken metrics write path). Why the 1.x line rather than 2.x is written down nowhere.

Why this matters more than a routine missing-rationale note

InfluxDB 2.x changed the write API. The write path is exactly what ADR-016 records as broken — k6 results have never reached InfluxDB, so the Grafana dashboard is empty; k6 logs Couldn't write stats once per flush interval but exits 0, which is why thresholds still gate correctly and the JSON plus summary files in docs/performance/history/ are the real evidence.

So the major-version choice and the recorded defect touch the same subsystem. Anyone eventually repairing that write path needs to know whether 1.x is a deliberate constraint or an accident of whatever was current when the stack was first composed. Without the rationale they cannot tell whether moving to 2.x is a candidate fix or a violation of an unrecorded decision.

Secondary consideration, recorded but not the driver: influxdb:1.8 is end-of-life upstream and receives no security patches. @security-auditor verified the surrounding posture is otherwise sound and named no specific advisory, having verified none — loopback-only publish (docker-compose.yml:12 is - "127.0.0.1:8086:8086"), INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED: "true", credentials indirected through env vars with no committed literals, and it is a local development monitoring stack rather than a deployed service.

Acceptance criteria

  1. ADR-016 records why the 1.x line is pinned, or records that 2.x is a candidate for the broken write path — whichever is true. If the pin turns out to be incidental rather than decided, say so plainly; "no reason, inherited from initial setup" is a legitimate and useful finding.
  2. If ADR-016 gains an amendment, its Status line and the matching row in docs/adr/README.md move together, so AdrIndexConsistencyTest.shouldCarryAmendmentDates passes.
  3. Do not add a second copy of the version literal. docker-compose.yml:9 is the pin itself — executable, dated by version control, superseded by commits — and is already an acceptable home. A prose restatement of "InfluxDB is pinned to 1.8" in an ADR would be a copy that a future compose bump silently falsifies, which is the exact defect class EOP-35 and EOP-122 exist to eliminate.
  4. ./mvnw verify green.
  5. CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased.

Raised by @architecture-guardian as an out-of-scope finding during the EOP-41/EOP-49 gate round (PR #105). Deliberately not fixed there: that PR did not open docs/architecture/, and the C4 model was not what either ticket was about.

`docs/architecture/C4-Diagrams.md` asserts two incompatible positions about the same flag, roughly a thousand lines apart.

At :81-84, in live undated present tense:

Containment is still the feature flag ... six use-case beans and the two controllers — eight beans in all — exist only while eop.features.trick-play is true, and application.yml leaves it `false` (application.yml:75-112). It stays `false` on merge.

At :1081-1089 the same file states the correct position: three flags, all true as of EOP-82, trick-play on since EOP-70 at :129, seven use-case beans plus TrickController, ScoreController and EndSessionController.

The :81-84 passage is false on the bean count, the controller count, the flag value and the line range. It is the same defect, in nearly the same words, that EOP-41 repaired at ADR-013:179-193 — and the more serious kind, because it claims a security containment is in force when it has not been since 2026-08-17.

*Also in scope, same file:*

  • :501 — "shared with all six trick-play use cases". There are seven: DealHands, ReadOwnHand, PlayCard, GetTrickState, ResolveTrick, EndSession, GetScore.
  • :1086 — annotation range UseCaseConfiguration.java:219-373. The ten annotations span :238–:410.
  • NIT: eight C4 edges with identical semantics carry two labels — :321 reads "first port call", while :290, :293, :296, :320, :322, :355, :362 read "first statement". Every one is accurate as written, because :321 is the PlayCardUseCase edge and that is the only use case for which "first statement" is false. Unify for consistency; this is not a correctness defect.

Confirmed already correct, needing nothing: C4-Diagrams.md:191, :193, :194 (Mermaid labels conditional in form, and :193/:194 already count /score sixth and /end seventh), :321, :502, :1082, :1113, :1164; docs/architecture/runtime-view.md:36-37 and :620 (already cites the re-derived DealHandsUseCase.java:133).

Re-derive, never adjust by an offset. grep -rn 'trick-play' --include='*.java' src/main/java | grep ConditionalOnProperty prints exactly ten lines; grep -n 'trick-play' src/main/resources/application.yml prints 129: trick-play: true.

Acceptance criteria

  • :81-84 no longer asserts containment in the present tense; superseded in place with an ISO-dated note carrying a ticket key, on the docs/adr/ADR-027-singleton-subresource-naming.md:81-82 pattern. Never rewritten, never renumbered.
  • The two positions in the file agree, or the historical one is explicitly marked as historical.
  • :501 and :1086 corrected, each number re-derived from source first.
  • Every count in the file that mentions the trick-play surface either carries a date or is currently true.
  • ./mvnw verify green, with the prose gates in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ passing — note MermaidSequenceTextTest polices every sequenceDiagram label in this file.
  • No cardinal or citation introduced without being re-derived from source first.

ADR-013 describes the flag register as two artefacts — the ADR and src/main/resources/application.yml. EOP-41 corrected the ADR half. This is the other half, and ADR-013's own amendment sends readers here with grep -n 'trick-play' src/main/resources/application.yml.

  • :115-116 names six gated use-case beans. There are seven — EndSessionUseCase is missing (UseCaseConfiguration.java:238, :269, :295, :331, :353, :384, :410).
  • :118 names "TrickController and ScoreController". There are three — EndSessionController is missing (TrickController.java:70, ScoreController.java:42, EndSessionController.java:54).
  • :119 lists six routes. There are seven — {{POST / {sessionId}

    /end}} is missing (EndSessionController.java:76).

Two mitigations, which are why this is MINOR rather than a blocker. The flag's value is correctly recorded and dated at :111 and :122-128 ("Enabled by EOP-70 (2026-08-17)"), so nothing here asserts the flag is off. And the stale arity sits inside a counterfactual "while it is off" clause, so it misleads about the size of the governed surface rather than about its current reachability — and it understates, which is the fail-safe direction.

Re-derive, never adjust by an offset. grep -rn 'trick-play' --include='*.java' src/main/java | grep ConditionalOnProperty prints exactly the ten gated declarations.

Acceptance criteria

  • The comment block names seven use-case beans, three controllers and seven routes, each re-derived from source before being written.
  • The flag's value and its dated flip note are left exactly as they are — this ticket changes the arity only.
  • Prefer a form that cannot rot again: either no enumeration at all, pointing at ADR-013 and the regeneration command, or an enumeration carrying its own re-derivation date. A bare corrected list will drift the same way.
  • No behavioural change: the property value is untouched, so TrickPlayDisabledIntegrationTest and ShippedFeatureFlagDefaultsTest must pass unchanged.
  • ./mvnw verify green.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @tester-unit-and-quality during the EOP-41/EOP-49 gate round (PR #105), and independently the root cause of both tickets in that PR.

The gap. Roughly thirty line citations across docs/ point into src/. Nothing in the build checks a single one. They rot silently whenever a source file grows, and the only thing that catches one is a human or an agent re-deriving it by hand. EOP-49 existed solely because seven anchors had drifted onto javadoc @throws tags around forty lines above the code they named, so a reader following one arrived at documentation and could confirm nothing. Worse, EOP-49's own ticket body carried replacement numbers that were themselves stale by 24 lines, because they were derived arithmetically rather than re-read.

The precedent. src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ already holds five text-comparison gates that read repository files as text during verify — AdrIndexConsistencyTest, TrickPlayExceptionOriginTest, DeckArithmeticClaimsTest, EnumMirrorParityTest, MermaidSequenceTextTest. A sixth would need no new tooling.

Sketch, not a specification. Parse Foo.java:123 and Foo.java:123-456 out of docs/*/.md, resolve the filename under src/, assert the cited line exists. The interesting design question is what to assert about it, since bare existence catches almost nothing. Options worth weighing: require the citation to carry a quoted token that must appear at that line; or assert the line is neither blank nor inside a javadoc comment, which would have caught every EOP-49 defect. Prefer a check that fails on the observed failure mode over one that is theoretically complete.

Two constraints inherited from the existing gates. Their matchers are phrase lists, so a green build proves only that known-stale phrasings are absent, never that documentation is correct — do not oversell what this adds. And their coverage is hand-written, so if this gate can only see citations in one syntax, say so in its Javadoc and carry a minimum-count floor in the style of MermaidSequenceTextTest's MINIMUM_SEQUENCE_DIAGRAMS, so it cannot silently pass by matching nothing.

Weigh the cheaper alternative first, and record the decision either way. EOP-41 and EOP-49 both moved toward embedding a re-derivable grep beside a claim instead of a line number, on the principle that a citation which teaches re-verification cannot rot into a lie the way a number can. If that is judged sufficient, close this as won't-do with an ADR-006 amendment saying so, rather than leaving it open indefinitely.

Acceptance criteria

  • Either a gate exists under src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ that fails on a drifted citation, or this closes with a recorded decision and a dated ADR-006 amendment explaining what is relied on instead.
  • If built: demonstrate it failing on a deliberately drifted anchor; state its coverage limits in its own Javadoc; carry a floor so it cannot pass by matching nothing.
  • If built: it must not fail on the citations currently in docs/, all of which were re-derived on 2026-08-21 under EOP-41/EOP-49.
  • If it becomes unfireable, delete it rather than leave it passing — per the branch-coverage lesson in ADR-006.
  • ./mvnw verify green.

comments.body:
Built, not closed won't-do. The cheaper alternative the ticket asked to be weighed first — an embedded re-derivable grep instead of a line number — is subsumed rather than rejected: the anchor is that grep, and it is machine-checked instead of relying on a reader to run it.

PR: https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/121 (commit 12a33bc, branch eop-130-line-citation-gate)

Two corrections to the ticket's own figures

  • "Roughly thirty" citations was a five-fold undercount — there are 171 named citations across 21 documents.
  • src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ held seven gates, not five, so this is the eighth, not the sixth. The two the ticket omitted are JoinCodeSpaceClaimsTest (EOP-56) and OpenApiContractDriftTest (EOP-95).

What was built

src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/SourceCitationAnchorTest.java — 585 lines, 9 tests. Three checks:

Check Scope
Cited path resolves against a tracked file universal — all 171
Cited start and end lines exist universal — all 171
Explicit `{{ (anchor: }}token{{) }}` occurs inside the cited range opt-in — 21 today

Why anchoring is opt-in, and why the ticket's favoured option was wrong

The ticket preferred "assert the line is neither blank nor inside a javadoc comment", saying it "would have caught every EOP-49 defect". Measurement contradicts this: ~58 citations deliberately target javadoc, so a blanket comment rejection would produce dozens of false failures.

Automatic anchor inference was then prototyped and measured: it flagged 36 of 67 inferred anchors. The noise is irreducible, not a tuning problem — it cannot distinguish "cites the javadoc on purpose" from "drifted onto the javadoc", and drift-onto-javadoc was EOP-49's failure mode.

Opt-in bought a second, structural property the ticket did not anticipate: a citation quoted inside an immutable dated amendment block stays truthful as history. Two live cases depend on it — this ADR's own 2026-08-18 blockquote cites GlobalExceptionHandlerTest.java:553's new NoTamperingCardDealtException(78) when the live code is (68) at line 674, and ADR-006:44 states dated amendment blocks are immutable records; and ADR-027:77-78 carries a stale anchor that EOP-131 explicitly forbids editing in place. A semantically complete gate would have had to falsify history or grow an opt-out marker.

The tree was not clean on arrival — acceptance criterion 3's premise was false

The criterion assumed the citations "were all re-derived on 2026-08-21 under EOP-41/EOP-49". They were not; only those two tickets' own scope was. Seventeen live citations across six documents were drifted and are repaired.

The most serious was not a wrong number but a false architectural claim: ADR-023:1291 said Trick.reconstitute was the only caller of Trick.winningPlay(). reconstitute (line 147) takes a winner parameter and never calls it — the only caller is resolved() at Trick.java:438. Also: CARD_PLAYED's publish point was cited as PlayCardUseCase.java:229 (a closing brace) in three documents while a fourth already had the correct :253; and three application.yml flag citations pointed at a rate-limit key, a comment tail and a blank line.

The gate caught its own author twice

  1. The ADR amendment used invented placeholders File.java:123 to describe the syntax; shouldResolveEveryCitedPath failed on them within minutes of the gate landing.
  2. Sixteen anchors were written but only fourteen enforced, because two used a placement the pattern of the day rejected. A ninth test shouldParseEveryAnchorMarkerItFinds now fails the build on any anchor: marker the parser did not bind — an anchor that reads as enforced but is not is worse than no anchor.

A third instance came from the gate round: @code-reviewer found Dockerfile sat in the extension list but could never match, because the pattern demands a literal . before the extension. ui/Dockerfile:13 was silently ignored. Same hollow-coverage class; fixed with a dedicated alternation branch.

Acceptance criteria

  1. ✅ Gate exists under src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/.
  2. ✅ Demonstrated failing on deliberate drift. Perturbing ADR-023:1290 from Trick.java:441 to :400 produced: docs/adr/ADR-023-…:1290 cites Trick.java:400 (anchor: winningPlay) — not found in the cited range; it occurs at lines 438, 441. Coverage limits are stated in the class Javadoc. Two floors carried: MINIMUM_CITATIONS = 150 (171 exist) and MINIMUM_ANCHORED_CITATIONS = 18 (21 exist) — both have been observed failing, so neither is vacuous.
  3. ⚠️ Satisfied, but the premise was false — see above. The two universal checks pass on the tree as it stands; the seventeen repairs were needed for the anchored subset.
  4. ✅ Retirement rule recorded in the Javadoc and the ADR amendment, citing ADR-006's branch-coverage lesson.
  5. ✅ ./mvnw clean verify → EXIT=0, Tests run: 1360, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS. JaCoCo 97.0% instruction / 88.9% branch.

Limits, stated plainly

  • ~122 bare `` `:N` `` continuation references are unchecked. They collide with port numbers (`{{ }}:8080{{ }}{{, }}{{ }}:5173{{ }}`) and their antecedent file is not mechanically recoverable — binding by "last named file" produced 17 spurious failures in the survey. Worth a follow-up to convert them to named form.
  • Presence, not position — an anchor found anywhere in the range passes.
  • No proof of truth — the gate checks that a citation points where it claims, never that the claim is correct.
  • Two third-party ChangeSet.java references into liquibase-core are allow-listed.
  • CHANGELOG.md is at the repository root, so citations written there are not scanned.

EOP-132 warned this gate would be blinded by line-oriented scanning of long table rows. It is not: every regex match on every line is parsed, and docs/adr/README.md:23 alone contributes two anchored citations from one 1,271-word row.

Definition of Done — five of five approved

Gate Verdict
@tester-unit-and-quality APPROVE — 3 MINOR (2 stale Javadoc counts, since fixed), 6 NIT
@tester-api APPROVE — change verified API-neutral, no new API test warranted
@security-auditor APPROVE — no ReDoS, path traversal rejected, .tmp pruning verified, no posture change
@code-reviewer APPROVE — all 17 repairs verified line by line; raised the Dockerfile bug, now fixed
@architecture-guardian APPROVE — amendment correct over a new ADR on the ADR-054 precedent

Documentation: dated 2026-08-23 amendment to ADR-006, docs/adr/README.md status row, CHANGELOG.md under ### Added, and .opencode/rules/build-quality.md — whose prose-gate bullet was also missing JoinCodeSpaceClaimsTest entirely.

Raised by @architecture-guardian during the EOP-41/EOP-49 gate round (PR #105), then downgraded by @security-auditor on re-review after reading the surrounding context properly. Filed for the record with that correction attached, because the obvious "fix" here is the wrong move.

docs/adr/ADR-027-singleton-subresource-naming.md:77-78 reads:

eop.features.trick-play still ships false (src/main/resources/application.yml:112)

Both halves are stale: the flag is true, and it is at :129. The stale anchor is the worse half, because application.yml:112 today is session-lifecycle: true — a different flag that happens to be true — so a reader who follows the citation finds a plausible-looking true and cannot tell the reference has rotted.

But that sentence sits inside a dated block, and the block below it already supersedes it. :71-80 is itself (Amended 2026-08-14, EOP-14 Slice E — …), and :81-82 reads:

(Amended 2026-08-17, EOP-70 — `eop.features.trick-play` is now `true`. All three predecessors (ADR-026, EOP-48, EOP-15) are discharged. See ADR-013 and ADR-026 for the full record.)

So ADR-027 is not merely mitigated — it is already fully superseded in place, two lines below the stale sentence. It is the exemplar the whole EOP-49 remediation copied: @security-auditor identified it as the one place in the repository that had already handled this exact sentence correctly.

The residue is a stale anchor inside a dated historical block, and rewriting that is precisely what the pattern forbids. Editing :112 to :129 inside an EOP-14 Slice E amendment would put a 2026-08-21 fact inside another story's dated record — the thing every ADR convention here exists to prevent.

So the likely correct outcome is to close this as won't-do, recording that the passage is intentionally frozen. Only two things could justify any edit:

  1. If the anchor misleads badly enough to warrant it, add a new dated note beneath :81-82 saying the :112 citation inside the block above now resolves to a different flag. Never touch the block itself.
  2. If a future reader is observed being misled by it, that observation is the trigger — not a tidiness impulse.

Acceptance criteria

  • Either this closes as won't-do with a one-line rationale (the passage is superseded at :81-82 and frozen), or a new dated note is added below :81-82 without altering any existing dated block.
  • Under no circumstances is :77-78 edited in place, and no anchor inside a dated block is renumbered.
  • No ADR renumbered; no status line changed unless an amendment date is added, in which case docs/adr/README.md carries it too.
  • ./mvnw verify green, AdrIndexConsistencyTest passing.

This ticket's own description notes the likely correct outcome is to close it: the stale anchor sits inside a dated historical block in ADR-027 that is already superseded at lines 81–82 of the same document. Correcting a historical record that is already marked as superseded adds no value and risks introducing confusion. The surrounding context makes the flag identity clear to any reader.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @architecture-guardian across three gate rounds on PR #105 (EOP-41/EOP-49). It began as a NIT about one 68-word parenthetical and was re-aimed on the second re-review once the guardian measured the rows: the new parentheticals are not the problem, the row lengths are.

The measurement

wc -w per row of docs/adr/README.md:

Row ADR Words
:33 ADR-023 1,271
:41 ADR-031 381
:35 ADR-025 333
:34 ADR-024 309
:23 ADR-013 266
:39 ADR-029 160
:50 ADR-040 46

A single table row of 1,271 words is a document. Row :50 at 46 words shows what a disciplined row looks like, so the target is not hypothetical.

Why this is more than readability

A row that long defeats the `grep`-based census that EOP-49 established as the remedy for stale claims. That is not a prediction — it happened twice, to two different reviewers, on this PR:

  • @architecture-guardian ran a filtered git grep census on round two and it silently missed `docs/adr/README.md:35` (a live, false claim that application.yml "defaults to false") and docs/adr/ADR-025:397-398. Its own report: "line-oriented grep over a 333-word table row matches on some unrelated clause elsewhere in the row … That is a real, structural reason the residue survived."
  • The Tech Lead's first filter on round three truncated the same row mid-clause and had to be replaced with a clause-splitting pass over all 145 hits.

So the index's row shape actively conceals defects in the index. Two consequences worth stating:

  1. .opencode/rules/ and CHANGELOG.md now prescribe a census over every mention of a fact as the way to avoid partial fixes. That method is unsound against this file as it stands.
  2. EOP-130's proposed line-anchor prose gate would be blinded the same way, since it must locate a citation within a line to check it. Sequencing matters: capping the rows makes EOP-130 tractable, so this ticket should be considered before or alongside it, not after.

Scope

Cap an index row at what an index is for: a status, a one-line verdict, and a link. Move the narrative into the ADR it indexes, where it is subject to the ADR amendment discipline (dated notes, nothing rewritten) rather than accumulating untracked in a table cell.

Note that the narrative in these rows is not junk — much of it is the only written record of a correction. It must be relocated, not deleted. That is what makes this a real piece of work rather than a trim: :33 alone is 1,271 words that have to land somewhere defensible in ADR-023, in dated form, without duplicating what the ADR already says.

Acceptance criteria

  • No row of docs/adr/README.md exceeds a stated word budget; propose the budget in the PR and record it where a future author will see it (a comment at the head of the table, or .opencode/rules/).
  • Every clause removed from a row is either already stated in the ADR it indexes, or moved there as a dated note — nothing is lost. Show this per row.
  • AdrIndexConsistencyTest still passes; the Status column and its amendment dates are untouched by this work.
  • Demonstrate that a line-oriented git grep over the reshaped table no longer truncates a clause — ideally by re-running the round-two filter that missed :35 and showing it now finds what it should.
  • Do not correct any stale claim as part of this ticket. If relocation surfaces one, file it separately: this is a structural change, and mixing content corrections into it would make the diff unreviewable.

Provenance

@architecture-guardian, PR #105 re-review 2 (commit 3b5ce9a), graded MINOR, with the explicit note that it "is no longer only a readability nit" for the census reason above. Related: EOP-130 (line-anchor gate — blinded by the same rows), EOP-128 (C4-Diagrams.md self-contradiction).

Raised by @security-auditor as a MEDIUM while approving PR #105 (EOP-41/EOP-49). It is the one finding from that story's three gate rounds that no amount of care on EOP-49's own method would have caught, because it is a defect in the method rather than in its execution.

The problem

EOP-49 established, and wrote into ADR-013 and several amendments, that the way to check whether a claim about eop.features.trick-play has gone stale is to enumerate git grep -n 'trick-play' – docs/ and read every hit. That census was eventually run to completion — all 145 hits — and it is sound as far as it reaches.

It cannot reach a claim that never names the flag. A sentence such as "the flag stays false" or "the reasons it stays down" is a containment claim about this exact flag, is fail-dangerous when stale, and is invisible to every grep 'trick-play' that will ever be run.

@security-auditor found four such claims with a name-independent sweep, all of them stale since EOP-70 set the flag true on 2026-08-17:

  • docs/adr/ADR-031-the-score-is-read-through-its-own-route.md:296 — "the flag stays false", present tense, undated, in a ## Relations bullet. Confirmed absent from the 145: sed -n '296p' … | grep -c 'trick-play' returns 0.
  • docs/architecture/C4-Diagrams.md:87 — "The reasons it stays down are now…"
  • docs/architecture/C4-Diagrams.md:542 — "reasons the flag stays down are now the three predecessors ADR-028 names"
  • docs/architecture/runtime-view.md:1297 — "why the flag stays off"

The sweep that finds them

git grep -nE "(the flag|[Ii]t) (stays|remains|is still|was still) (\`?false\`?|off|down|unset|disabled)" -- . | grep -v 'trick-play'

That returned nine hits, of which the four above are genuine. The other five are correctly disposed and should not be touched: ADR-013:176 and :197 are past tense or quote superseded text inside an amendment; CHANGELOG.md:143 is a false positive about exception mapping; the openapi.yml, application.yml, EndSessionController.java and SessionController.java hits are counterfactual ("while the flag is off") and true at any value; and the ADR-037 / ADR-009:336 / runtime-view.md:273 hits concern VITE_GAME_SCREEN_ENABLED, a different flag whose container default genuinely is false.

Why this matters more than the four sites

Fixing four lines is an afternoon. The durable problem is that the census command recorded in ADR-013 is documented as the way to check, and it has a blind spot that a future author will not know about. Whatever else this ticket does, the blind spot must end up written down next to the command it qualifies.

Note also the interaction with the fix EOP-49 actually landed: every corrected site now delegates the flag's value and arity to ADR-013 rather than restating them, which shrinks this class over time — an anaphoric claim is only possible where a document is making its own assertion about the flag. So the population here should be finite and shrinking, not growing.

Scope

  • Correct the four sites listed above, superseding in place on the docs/adr/ADR-027-singleton-subresource-naming.md:81-82 pattern — tense-pin, append a dated note, delegate the live value to ADR-013. Never delete, never renumber, never edit inside another story's dated block (append after it instead).
  • C4-Diagrams.md:87 and :542 overlap EOP-128, which owns that file's self-contradiction at :81-84 but whose acceptance criterion is phrased in terms of counts that "mention the trick-play surface" — it reaches :87 but arguably not :542, which names no flag. Either widen EOP-128 to name both lines explicitly and drop them from here, or take them here and say so on EOP-128. Do not leave the boundary implicit.
  • Record the name-independent sweep alongside the grep 'trick-play' census in ADR-013's amendment, so the next person to run the prescribed check learns about the blind spot from the same paragraph that prescribes it.

Acceptance criteria

  • The four sites are corrected, each carrying an ISO date and a ticket key, each delegating the live value rather than restating it.
  • ADR-013 records both sweeps, with the blind spot stated explicitly — a reader must not be able to run the documented census and believe it is complete.
  • The name-independent sweep returns no stale hit, and its false positives are enumerated somewhere durable so the next person does not re-litigate them.
  • The EOP-128 boundary is stated on both tickets rather than inferred.
  • ./mvnw clean verify green, with AdrIndexConsistencyTest and the other four prose gates passing. Check pgrep -fl MavenWrapperMain first — concurrent Maven in this tree deletes target/ mid-run and manufactures false red builds, and pgrep alone was observed to miss one.
  • Every figure re-derived from source rather than adjusted by an offset.

Not in scope

Correcting arity claims (EOP-129), shortening index rows (EOP-132), or building a line-anchor gate (EOP-130).

Raised by @security-auditor as LOW/INFO while approving PR #105 (EOP-41/EOP-49), and worth a ticket chiefly because the imprecise formula has now been copied into five documents and will be copied again.

The claim

Several ADRs, including amendments EOP-49 itself wrote, state that the trick-play surface is reachable and that "only ADR-015's token and ADR-024's authorisation stand in front of it". Sites: docs/adr/README.md:33, docs/adr/ADR-027-singleton-subresource-naming.md:110-115, docs/adr/ADR-023-deal-remainder-and-turn-order.md:1415.

What is actually there

Verified against source by @security-auditor, not against the documents:

  • No framework-level control at all. grep -n -iE 'spring-boot-starter-security|spring-security' pom.xml → no matches. No Filter, OncePerRequestFilter, HandlerInterceptor, SecurityFilterChain or WebMvcConfigurer anywhere in src/main/java/.
  • ADR-015 token — all seven handlers take @RequestHeader(… PLAYER_TOKEN_HEADER, required = false) (TrickController.java:123, :150, :180, :227, :253; ScoreController.java:79; EndSessionController.java:87). required = false, so absence is rejected downstream rather than by the framework.
  • ADR-024 authorisation — all seven use cases call ResolvePlayerUseCase, including /score and /end, which fall outside ADR-024's nominal subject.
  • A facilitator-only role check on `/deal` and `/end`, beyond mere membership: DealHandsUseCase.java:11 imports NotFacilitatorException; EndSessionUseCase.java:65 documents @throws … NotFacilitatorException if the caller is a participant.
  • Payload validation on the one route carrying a body: TrickController.java:181 @Valid @RequestBody final PlayCardRequest request.

So the two-control formula is exactly right for `/hand` — which is where ADR-027:110-115 uses it, correctly, since ReadOwnHandUseCase has token resolution and membership authorisation and nothing else. It understates for the set of seven. README.md:33 understates further still, naming only ADR-024 and dropping the token.

Why this is LOW and not a blocker

It errs in the fail-safe direction: a reader is told less protects the surface than actually does, which provokes scrutiny rather than false confidence. It is the mirror image of the defect EOP-49 existed to fix, where documents claimed containment that had lapsed.

Scope

  • Correct the three sites so each states the controls that actually apply to the routes it is talking about. Where a document speaks about one route, the two-control formula may well be right — check per route rather than replacing one blanket claim with another.
  • Prefer a form that cannot rot: name the controls by their ADR and let the reader follow, rather than enumerating exception types that will change.
  • Supersede in place on the ADR-027:81-82 pattern; ADR-023:1415 sits inside a frozen dated correction, so append rather than edit.

Acceptance criteria

  • Each of the three sites is accurate for the routes in its own scope, with every control re-derived from source and cited file:line.
  • The facilitator check and @Valid are either named or deliberately excluded with a stated reason.
  • No claim is introduced that enumerates a control set without saying which routes it applies to — that ambiguity is what produced this finding.
  • ./mvnw clean verify green, all five prose gates passing. Check pgrep -fl MavenWrapperMain first.

The remaining non-blocking findings from PR #105's three gate rounds (EOP-41/EOP-49), collected rather than left in review transcripts. All were graded MINOR or NIT by @architecture-guardian or @security-auditor, both of which approved.

1. ADR-028 still describes the feature as unreleased (MINOR, @architecture-guardian)

docs/adr/ADR-028-end-of-hand-without-release-or-score.md:136-142 — "The feature is complete and unreleased. Everything from five slices sits on main unexercised … the trick-play code is now the largest body of work in the repository whose only exercise is its own test suite." Undated, present tense, false since EOP-70 on 2026-08-17.

This is the same class as ADR-031:194 ("Nothing shipped here is reachable in a deployed container"), which EOP-49 tense-pinned. It was found by neither gate's census and neither of EOP-49's own, because the passage never names the flag — so it also belongs to the defect class in the anaphoric-claims ticket, and whichever is taken first should say so.

Mitigation, and why it is MINOR: the dated amendment at ADR-028:7-11 states the flag is now true, and a reader cannot reach :136 without passing it. @security-auditor separately noted :94 and :97 as the same shape, superseded only at a distance of 87 lines.

2. ADR-013:136 (LOW/INFO, @security-auditor)

A present-tense containment claim superseded only by the register's live statement at :190-192, far below it.

3. Stale bean count under src/test (LOW/INFO, @security-auditor)

src/test/resources/application.properties:20 — a comment saying the test "asserts the eight beans are absent". There are ten. Same class as EOP-129 and, like it, understating in the fail-safe direction. Note this is a .properties file, so it falls outside the Markdown-only boundary EOP-49 held to; it is small enough to take with either this ticket or EOP-129, but decide deliberately rather than by accident.

4. ADR-031's spent-conditions note omits condition 4 (NIT, @architecture-guardian)

docs/adr/ADR-031-the-score-is-read-through-its-own-route.md:229 names conditions 1, 2 and 5 as spent. Condition 4 — rewrite SessionStatus's javadoc — is also spent: grep -n "EOP-14" src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/entity/SessionStatus.java returns nothing, so the offending clause is gone. Conditions 3 and 6 genuinely still stand. Condition 4 is a task rather than a containment claim, which is why EOP-49 did not widen the note to cover it.

5. ADR-024:238 (NIT, @architecture-guardian)

"which Slice C1 does not ship and Slice C2 may not merge without" — present tense about a discharged slice obligation. No containment claim.

6. Nothing gates ADR-013's arity figures (raised by @architecture-guardian while approving)

EOP-49's durable fix was delegation: every corrected site now points at ADR-013 rather than restating the flag's value or arity, so the next flip has one place to change rather than eleven. @architecture-guardian judged that trade sound but named its residual risk precisely — if ADR-013 goes stale, every delegating site is now silently stale by reference.

Partly mitigated already: ShippedFeatureFlagDefaultsTest.java:85-90 fails the build if application.yml stops saying trick-play: true, so the value is gated. The arity is not — add an eleventh gated bean and the register goes quietly wrong, and now so does everything that delegates to it. A src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ gate comparing ADR-013's stated counts against grep -c of the annotations would close it. That overlaps EOP-130's line-anchor gate and should be weighed with it rather than built separately.

Acceptance criteria

  • Items 1 to 5 corrected or explicitly declined with a reason, each correction carrying an ISO date and a ticket key, superseding in place on the ADR-027:81-82 pattern.
  • Item 6 either implemented as a prose gate or closed as won't-do with the reasoning recorded in a dated ADR-006 amendment — the risk must not simply be dropped.
  • The .properties scope decision on item 3 stated rather than implied.
  • Every count re-derived from source rather than adjusted by an offset.
  • ./mvnw clean verify green, all five prose gates passing. Check pgrep -fl MavenWrapperMain first — concurrent Maven in this tree manufactures false red builds and pgrep alone was observed to miss one.

renderedFields.description:
Follow-up carrying forward the residual risk from EOP-31 item 4, which was closed with a recorded reason rather than fixed because the fix is an infrastructure change disproportionate to a hygiene sweep.

The risk

Two repository adapters decide which uniqueness violation occurred by matching the constraint name as a lower-cased substring of the JDBC exception message, walking the cause chain:

  • SessionRepositoryAdapter.mentions() — two constraints (uq_game_session_join_code, uq_player_session_seat)
  • TrickPlayRepositoryAdapter.mentions() — seven constraints (trick sequence, hand-per-seat, hand-seat, play-per-seat, play-per-player, play-per-card, play-seat)

Matching on constraint name rather than exception type is the right instinct: the exception type says only that some uniqueness was violated, and the adapters need to tell a retryable seat collision from a genuine conflict. Anything unrecognised is rethrown, so a new constraint fails loudly rather than arriving as a silent retry loop. That part is sound and documented.

The problem is where it is measured. The whole test suite runs on H2 — src/test/resources/application.properties sets jdbc:h2:mem:eop-test, and there is no MODE=PostgreSQL anywhere in the repository, so it is not even H2's PostgreSQL compatibility mode. Production is PostgreSQL 17. A message-format change in either engine would silently turn a retryable seat collision into a 500, and no test would notice.

This is not speculative — the suite already says so

Eight test sites openly mark PostgreSQL behaviour as unmeasured rather than verified:

  • TrickPlayUniqueConstraintTest:51 — "Which one PostgreSQL 17 reports has not been measured"
  • TrickPlayUniqueConstraintTest:340,378
  • SessionRepositoryAdapterIntegrationTest:418 — SQL state 23513 on H2, 23514 on PostgreSQL
  • HandAndTrickUniqueConstraintTest:106 — a test that would fail on PostgreSQL 17, where evaluation order is not guaranteed to agree
  • MappedSchemaValidationIntegrationTest:25
  • SeatAndSequenceBoundsTest:66
  • SessionExpiryMigrationTest:49-50,77

The prose is honest — it does not over-claim. But honesty about a gap is not coverage of it.

Scope

Adopt Testcontainers (no such dependency exists today — grep -rn 'testcontainers' pom.xml src/test/java/ returns nothing) and run the constraint-name matching assertions against a real PostgreSQL 17 container, matching the production engine and the POSTGRES_IMAGE=postgres:17-alpine already in .env.example.

This needs an ADR: it adds a test-scope dependency, requires a container runtime in CI, and materially changes suite runtime. Colima is the project's runtime (ADR-016, a repository document under docs/adr/, not a Jira issue) — Docker Desktop is deliberately not installed, so the ADR must establish that Testcontainers works against Colima in both local and GitHub Actions environments before the dependency lands.

Acceptance criteria

  1. An ADR records the decision to adopt Testcontainers, including the Colima constraint and the CI implications.
  2. Every constraint name matched by either mentions() implementation has a test asserting the match holds against real PostgreSQL 17.
  3. The eight test sites listed above are revisited: each unmeasured claim is either measured and corrected, or left with its disclaimer intact and a reason.
  4. ./mvnw verify stays green, and CI stays green.
  5. The residual-risk note recorded on EOP-31 is superseded and that supersession is recorded.

comments.body:
Scope addition raised during the EOP-31 five-gate review round, recorded here rather than by rewriting the description.

@architecture-guardian rated this MAJOR while reviewing EOP-31, and it is a distinct deliverable from adopting Testcontainers: the H2-versus-PostgreSQL-17 constraint-name residual has no durable home in the repository. It currently lives in exactly two places, a ## [Unreleased] bullet in CHANGELOG.md and this ticket. The changelog bullet becomes archaeology under a version heading at the next release, and this ticket disappears the moment it is closed — including if it is closed as won't-do. So the record gap can outlive every possible outcome of the work described above.

Two specific gaps were measured, not inferred:

First, docs/adr/ADR-024-trick-play-persistence.md is entirely silent on the subject. Grepping it for H2, Postgres, constraint name, substring and Testcontainers returns no output at all. The ADR that owns the trick-play persistence boundary says nothing about how that boundary translates constraint violations, nor on which engine that translation is verified.

Second, neither adapter's Javadoc mentions either engine. SessionRepositoryAdapter.java:217-234 and TrickPlayRepositoryAdapter.java:893-916 both carry good prose defending the choice to match on constraint name rather than exception type, and both state that an unrecognised name is rethrown so a new constraint fails loudly. That reasoning is sound, but it answers a different question. Nothing at either site says the names are matched against H2 message text while production runs PostgreSQL 17.

Added to the scope of this ticket, and each is worth doing independently of whether Testcontainers is ever adopted:

  • A Consequences entry in docs/adr/ADR-024-trick-play-persistence.md naming the engine gap explicitly.
  • One sentence at SessionRepositoryAdapter.java:217-234 recording that the two constraint names there are matched against H2 message text and are unverified on PostgreSQL.
  • The same at TrickPlayRepositoryAdapter.java:893-916 for its seven names.
  • If this ticket is ever closed without adopting a real engine in the test path, those three records must still be in place first. That is the condition that stops the residual becoming invisible.

h2. The risk

Two repository adapters decide _which_ uniqueness violation occurred by matching the constraint name as a lower-cased substring of the JDBC exception message, walking the cause chain:

* {{SessionRepositoryAdapter.mentions()}} — two constraints ({{uq_game_session_join_code}}, {{uq_player_session_seat}})
* {{TrickPlayRepositoryAdapter.mentions()}} — seven constraints (trick sequence, hand-per-seat, hand-seat, play-per-seat, play-per-player, play-per-card, play-seat)

Matching on constraint name rather than exception type is the right instinct: the exception type says only that _some_ uniqueness was violated, and the adapters need to tell a retryable seat collision from a genuine conflict. Anything unrecognised is rethrown, so a new constraint fails loudly rather than arriving as a silent retry loop. That part is sound and documented.

The problem is where it is measured. The whole test suite runs on H2 — {{src/test/resources/application.properties}} sets {{jdbc:h2:mem:eop-test}}, and there is no {{MODE=PostgreSQL}} anywhere in the repository, so it is not even H2's PostgreSQL compatibility mode. Production is PostgreSQL 17. A message-format change in either engine would silently turn a retryable seat collision into a 500, and no test would notice.

* {{SeatAndSequenceBoundsTest:66}}
* {{SessionExpiryMigrationTest:49-50,77}}

Raised by @security-auditor during the EOP-31 gate round. Both findings are pre-existing, rated MEDIUM, and were explicitly ruled not blockers for EOP-31 — the file was last changed by 7b58192 on 2026-08-05 under EOP-16, sixteen days before that story, and EOP-31 does not touch it. The auditor's words: "Blocking EOP-31 on it would be gate creep."

Finding 1 — Grafana publishes on all interfaces.

docker-compose.yml:29-30 declares a ports: entry of "3000:3000" with no host-IP prefix, so Grafana binds every interface. Its sibling in the same file does not: docker-compose.yml:11-12 binds InfluxDB as 127.0.0.1:8086:8086. The asymmetry reads as an oversight rather than a decision.

This matters because of what EOP-31 just changed. The GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD key in .env.example now ships the literal placeholder CHANGE_ME, and GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED: "false" at docker-compose.yml:32 means the admin password is the only gate, with GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER defaulting to admin at :33. A developer who copies the template and does not read SETUP.md therefore exposes admin plus that placeholder to their whole LAN. The auditor was explicit that this all-interfaces binding is "the single reason the CHANGE_ME residual has any real-world reach at all".

Two mitigations keep it MEDIUM rather than HIGH: anonymous auth is off, and :34 interpolates the password variable with no :- default, so an unset variable makes the stack fail rather than boot on admin/admin.

Finding 2 — the image tag is mutable.

docker-compose.yml:27 reads image: grafana/grafana:latest. The local monitoring stack therefore pulls whatever latest resolves to on any given day. This is a supply-chain reproducibility hole in exactly the direction tools/supply-chain/expected-plugins.json exists to close for the npm layer, and it contrasts with the pinned influxdb:1.8 sibling in the same file (see .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md, which records that pin).

Acceptance criteria

  1. docker-compose.yml:29-30 binds Grafana to loopback (127.0.0.1:3000:3000), matching the InfluxDB sibling — or the all-interfaces binding is documented as deliberate with its reason.
  2. docker-compose.yml:27 pins an exact Grafana version rather than latest, and the pin is recorded wherever the InfluxDB pin is recorded.
  3. Whichever choice is made for (1), SETUP.md and .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md agree with the file.
  4. docker compose up -d still brings the monitoring stack up and Grafana still reads the InfluxDB k6 database on :3000.
  5. Consider whether the same audit applies to the remaining published ports in docker-compose.yml and compose.app.yml — note compose.app.yml gives postgres no ports: stanza at all, which is the correct shape.

Note on this description: an earlier revision contained a literal environment-variable assignment, which the VibeGuard redaction plugin masked on the way out, and a fenced code block, which the Markdown-to-Jira converter escaped. Both are avoided above.

Raised by @architecture-guardian during the EOP-31 DoD gate round as a MAJOR, pre-existing finding. Non-blocking for EOP-31, which is why it is filed rather than fixed there.

Two adjacent bullets in docs/adr/ADR-011-graphify-knowledge-graph.md are measurably false, and the file has no Amendments section to hold a correction.

Finding 1 — the edge-ratio bullet at line 47. It reads, in substance, that of 542 edges 96 percent are ON_BRANCH, PARENT_OF and MODIFIES, that only 21 edges describe code structure, and that the ratio worsens until real domain code lands. Every figure is now wrong, and the prediction is falsified in the opposite direction to the one it feared. Measured from .graphify/GRAPH_REPORT.md line 10: 10874 edges total. Git-metadata edges are ON_BRANCH 4172 plus MODIFIES 1177 plus PARENT_OF 498, which is 5847, a share of 53.8 percent rather than 96 percent. Structural edges are method 2150 plus calls 1819 plus contains 603 plus imports 315 plus inherits 71 plus imports_from 35 plus implements 27, which is 5020 rather than 21. The top hub is GlobalExceptionHandler with 38 edges, not the test class the ADR names. So the ratio improved substantially as domain code landed.

Finding 2 — the corpus-size bullet at line 48, which is worse because it cites a specific line by number. It quotes .graphify/GRAPH_REPORT.md line 4 as saying the corpus is around 40,457 words, fits in a single context window, and that you may not need a graph. That line now reads that this is a large corpus of 569 files and roughly 1,100,936 words. The ADR therefore cites a line for a claim that the line now contradicts. The operational advice it draws from that quote — reach for grep instead of the graph — also contradicts the Context Optimization Rule that every agent in this repository operates under, which directs agents to the graphify tools before grepping.

Why this matters beyond tidiness. ADR-011 is one of the ADRs an agent reads to decide whether to trust or reach for the knowledge graph. A reader who takes line 48 at face value will skip the graph on the grounds that the corpus is small, when it is twenty-seven times larger than the figure quoted.

Note that a third bullet in the same file, at line 45, is accurate and was relied on during EOP-31: it records that check-update normally reporting pending semantic updates is the expected steady state, and that the accompanying built-from-versus-HEAD line is the signal worth acting on. Do not disturb it.

Additional stale claims (absorbed from EOP-119)

The following lines also carry stale figures and should be corrected in the same amendment pass:

Line Stale claim Current measurement
12 "88 lines of Java across 4 files" far larger; the domain code the graph was installed ahead of now exists
22 "27,989 ignored files", "24,194 under tools/graphify", "3,652 under .opencode" 38,777 ignored, 569 included of 639 candidates
23 "52 of 94 tracked files are Markdown", "8 distinct source_file values", "all eleven ADRs" 7 source values; 45 ADRs exist
42 "The nine communities carry meaningful names" 248 communities; only first nine are named
43 "coverage reached 26/26 describable nodes" 3531 nodes, descriptions: 0/3531 real

The two ratio-derived consequences (lines 47 and 48) are the highest-priority corrections because they affect agent behaviour. The table above is secondary — correct them in the same pass but do not let them block the primary fix.

Acceptance criteria

  • The line 47 bullet either carries corrected figures or is explicitly retired, with the correction dated.
  • The line 48 bullet no longer quotes a line of GRAPH_REPORT.md that says something else, and no longer advises grep in a way that contradicts the Context Optimization Rule.
  • The stale claims in the table above are corrected or removed in the same amendment.
  • docs/adr/ADR-011-graphify-knowledge-graph.md gains an Amendments section in the house style used by docs/adr/ADR-014-realtime-transport.md, so this and future corrections have a dated home.
  • Any figure written into the ADR is either measured at the time of writing and dated as such, or expressed as a property that cannot go stale. A bare count with no date is what produced this defect.
  • docs/adr/README.md still passes AdrIndexConsistencyTest, including its amendment-date check if a dated amendment is added.
  • ./mvnw verify is green.

|23|"52 of 94 tracked files are Markdown", "8 distinct source_file values", "all eleven ADRs"|7 source values; 45 ADRs exist|
|42|"The nine communities carry meaningful names"|248 communities; only first nine are named|
|43|"coverage reached 26/26 describable nodes"|3531 nodes, descriptions: 0/3531 real|

The two ratio-derived consequences (lines 47 and 48) are the highest-priority corrections because they affect agent behaviour. The table above is secondary — correct them in the same pass but do not let them block the primary fix.

* {{docs/adr/README.md}} still passes {{AdrIndexConsistencyTest}}, including its amendment-date check if a dated amendment is added.
* {{./mvnw verify}} is green.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @architecture-guardian during the EOP-31 DoD gate round: one MINOR finding on the ADR body and one MINOR on the index row. They are bundled because the fix for the second is to move text into the section the first amends. Both are non-blocking for EOP-31.

Part 1 — docs/adr/ADR-014-realtime-transport.md lines 60 to 67 infer a measurement from an absence.

The passage asserts that server-sent events ask nothing of the reverse proxy that Caddy does not already do, that Caddy does not buffer proxied responses by default, and then concludes that the ui/Caddyfile which resulted contains no buffering directive because none is needed, so the prediction held.

The factual premise is true. A search of ui/Caddyfile for buffer or flush returns nothing, and the handle /api/* block at lines 200 to 207 carries only a request-body size limit of 16KB and a reverse proxy to the app on port 8080. But the inference is circular: the absence of a buffering directive is that file's default state whether or not SSE was ever exercised through the proxy. Nobody had to omit anything for the file to look like that. So the sentence cites its own silence as evidence.

The thing that would actually evidence it is the one-off manual observation EOP-31 has just dated in the index: on 2026-08-05, under EOP-10, commit 87d8c49, the stream was read on a real socket through Caddy with retry and heartbeat frames observed — covering only the two events that existed then. The sentence in question dates to commit bc3e4e8 on 2026-08-10, so it was written after that observation existed but does not cite it.

The correction belongs in the ADR's Amendments section, whose heading is at line 164 with the latest entry at line 198. It should say that the no-buffering property was observed once, manually, on 2026-08-05, on two of the five events now published, and that the Caddyfile's silence is the file's default rather than a measurement.

Part 2 — docs/adr/README.md line 24 now carries 1,183 characters of narrative history in a summary index cell.

That is a measured character count, not an estimate. Every sentence in it is accurate — EOP-31 wrote it deliberately, to date the observation, scope it to two events, and record that the three EOP-14 Slice E events were folded into the same sentence on 2026-08-14 in commit 43f0cbc without the verification claim being re-checked. The objection is placement only. An index row is a pointer. The history of how a claim silently widened belongs in the ADR's Amendments section, with a one-line pointer from the row.

Do this as part of Part 1 so the history lands in the section being amended anyway.

Acceptance criteria:

  • docs/adr/ADR-014-realtime-transport.md lines 60 to 67 no longer present the Caddyfile's silence as evidence, and the qualification is dated in the Amendments section.
  • The widening history moves out of docs/adr/README.md line 24 into ADR-014's Amendments, leaving a short pointer in the index cell.
  • The index cell's status column is untouched, so AdrIndexConsistencyTest still agrees with the ADR's own status line.
  • If a dated amendment is added, its date appears wherever AdrIndexConsistencyTest requires it. Note EOP-138 covers a related blind spot in that test.
  • No claim about behaviour through Caddy is stated more strongly than the evidence supports. If the observation is repeated or scripted, say when and on which events.
  • ./mvnw verify is green.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @architecture-guardian during the EOP-31 DoD gate round as a MAJOR structural finding. Non-blocking for EOP-31 — no guard regressed and EOP-31 introduced nothing here — but it is the reason a documentation defect went undetected for a week and was then found by a human reading rather than by the build.

The defect. src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/AdrIndexConsistencyTest.java lines 113 to 131, the shouldCarryAmendmentDates case, iterates statusCells(). That helper is defined at lines 72 to 80 against STATUS_COLUMN = 3, so it reads column 3 and only column 3. The test then extracts dates from the ADR file's own status line and {{continue}}s when it finds none.

docs/adr/ADR-014-realtime-transport.md carries a bare status line reading Accepted, with no date. So for the ADR-014 row the assertion never executes at all. Meanwhile the dates that matter — 2026-08-05 for the original manual observation and 2026-08-14 for the commit that widened it — live in column 4, the Implemented? column, which no date guard inspects.

Why this is the interesting shape rather than a missing assertion. The test exists so that a stale row cannot look current. It ended up watching the one cell in the table that cannot go stale: a status of Accepted stays true indefinitely. The narrative claims about what has actually been verified all live in column 4, and that is exactly where commit 43f0cbc on 2026-08-14 folded three new events into a sentence ending in a verification claim, silently widening a two-event observation to five, with no test able to notice. EOP-31 fixed that row by hand.

This is the same failure mode as the StrideCategory unregistered-mirror lesson recorded in the build-quality rules: a prose gate whose coverage is a hand-written list, passing because nothing told it to look.

Two legitimate outcomes, and either is acceptable.

  • Extend the guard so column 4 is inspected too. Note this is harder than it sounds, because column 4 is free narrative rather than a status word, so the assertion has to be about something structural — for instance, that a cell asserting a verification carries a date, or that a cell citing a commit hash cites one that exists.
  • Or explicitly bound the guard: record in the test itself that it deliberately covers only the status column, and say what is therefore unguarded. That is the honest option if extending it would produce a matcher too loose to be meaningful. A named limit a reader can see beats an implied guarantee that does not hold.

What is not acceptable is leaving the test as-is with its current name and no disclosure, because the name promises more than the body delivers.

Acceptance criteria:

  • Either column 4 is covered by a date or citation guard, or the test carries an explicit written statement of what it does not cover and why.
  • If a new matcher is added, at least one deliberately-broken fixture proves it fails — a guard that has never been seen to fire is not evidence.
  • The four existing cases still pass, and the ADR index still round-trips.
  • If the guard turns out to be unfireable in some respect, delete that part rather than leaving it passing vacuously, per the branch-coverage lesson in ADR-006.
  • ./mvnw verify is green.

renderedFields.description:
Context & Provenance

These two findings were raised by @architecture-guardian during the Definition-of-Done gate round for EOP-67 (merged as commit e648cd7, PR #107, merge commit b6e8447; EOP-67 is now Done). Both were tagged MINOR and explicitly judged pre-existing — inherited, not introduced by EOP-67. The architecture gate did not hold on them; they belong on a dedicated ticket owning the front-end C4 section. This is follow-up work, not a regression from EOP-67.

Every line/byte figure below was verified against main at b6e8447.

Finding 1 — MINOR — docs/architecture/C4-Diagrams.md:831 — stale helper enumeration

The sentence currently reads:

"All five server calls honour this boundary: createSession, joinSession, getSession, startGame, and subscribeToSession are all exported from api.ts."

It is stale by eight. There are thirteen exported helpers in ui/src/api.ts, verified by:

grep -n "^export async function\|^export function" ui/src/api.ts

Results:

  • fetchCards:334
  • createSession:457
  • joinSession:477
  • getSession:497
  • startGame:515
  • subscribeToSession:547
  • getLeaderboard:651
  • startNewGame:666
  • dealHands:841
  • fetchHand:856
  • getTrickState:872
  • playCard:888
  • resolveTrick:907

The sentence is also self-contradicted seventeen lines later at :848, which correctly counts 10 parsed + 3 parser-free = 13. Two adjacent paragraphs in the same section give incompatible counts.

Suggested fix (states the invariant that actually matters and cannot go stale on the fourteenth helper):

"All thirteen server calls honour this boundary — every one is exported from api.ts and no component issues its own fetch"

Finding 2 — MINOR — docs/architecture/C4-Diagrams.md:819 — container diagram omits the deal edge and the leaderboard/new-game edges

The edge at :819 reads:

LOBBY -->|"getSession / startGame<br/>credentialed via api.ts"| API

LobbyScreen calls three helpers, not two — ui/src/components/LobbyScreen.tsx:163 calls dealHands inside handleStartGame. The container diagram therefore omits the very edge whose non-atomicity docs/adr/ADR-040-trick-play-flag-on.md:78-84 documents as an accepted architectural risk. That is a real comprehension gap: the documented risk is invisible in the diagram.

:821 has the same class of gap — it omits getLeaderboard and startNewGame.

Implementation notes:

  • The fence at :798-823 is a flowchart TD, so MermaidSequenceTextTest does not bind it (that gate only forbids ; and # in sequenceDiagram labels).
  • The section's sequenceDiagram at :857-920 models reconnect/live-update and is correctly unrelated to start-then-deal — do not edit it for this finding.
  • Editing any docs/*/.md file can still turn ./mvnw verify red via the five prose gates in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/. Run ./mvnw verify before pushing.

Definition of Done

  • :831 sentence updated to state the count-invariant form (or equivalent accurate phrasing).
  • The self-contradiction between :831 and :848 is resolved.
  • Container diagram at :819 updated to include dealHands alongside getSession / startGame.
