renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a player reading my hand or observing the current trick

I want to hover over (or tap on mobile) any card to see a circular magnifying-glass lens that enlarges the card content to 2×

So that I can read the card art and suit details clearly without needing to pick up or play the card

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: EOP-59 — Game Screen UI: play a trick from the browser
  • Target Persona: Any player at the game table, especially on smaller screens or with lower visual acuity
  • Value Proposition: Cards are rendered at 80×120 px (hand) and 64×96 px (trick zone) — small enough that fine detail in the card art is hard to read. A CSS lens effect gives instant, zero-latency magnification without navigating away or disrupting game flow.

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag Name: eop.features.card-magnifier
  • Deployment Behavior: Code merged to main and continuously deployed with flag set to OFF.
  • Release Condition: Enable flag once all Acceptance Criteria pass and @product-owner approves release.

Scope

In scope:

  • Hand cards (CardFace component, 80×120 px) — hover on desktop, tap on touch
  • Trick-zone cards (inline card divs inside the central drop zone, 64×96 px) — hover on desktop, tap on touch

Out of scope:

  • The drag ghost (already in motion; magnifying a ghost is disorienting)
  • CardBack components (face-down; nothing to magnify)
  • CardCatalogue (reference table, not a game surface)

Technical Constraint

Option A — CSS lens effect (pure front-end, no re-render).

A circular overlay appears centred on the cursor (or tap point on touch). The pixels already rendered within the circle are scaled to 2× using CSS transform: scale(2) with overflow: hidden on the lens container. This is a visual zoom of the rendered pixels — it does not add new DOM text. The threatPrompt text is not currently rendered visibly on the card face (it is in the aria-label only), so the lens will magnify the card image art. This is the explicitly chosen approach; Option B (re-rendered overlay with DOM text) is out of scope for this story.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: Lens appears on hand card hover (feature enabled, desktop)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.card-magnifier is ON
  • And the game screen is showing the player's hand
  • When the player moves the mouse pointer over a hand card
  • Then a circular lens overlay appears centred on the cursor
  • And the card content within the lens circle is rendered at 2× the original size
  • And the lens follows the cursor as it moves across the card

Scenario 2: Lens appears on trick-zone card hover (feature enabled, desktop)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.card-magnifier is ON
  • And the trick zone contains one or more played cards
  • When the player moves the mouse pointer over a played card in the trick zone
  • Then a circular lens overlay appears centred on the cursor
  • And the card content within the lens circle is rendered at 2×

Scenario 3: Lens appears on tap (feature enabled, touch)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.card-magnifier is ON
  • And the player is on a touch device
  • When the player taps a hand card or a trick-zone card
  • Then a circular lens overlay appears centred on the tap point
  • And the lens dismisses on a second tap or on tap-outside

Scenario 4: Default fallback (feature disabled)

  • Given feature flag eop.features.card-magnifier is OFF
  • Then no lens overlay appears on hover or tap
  • And the eop.features.card-magnifier bean is absent from the application context, not merely unreachable

Scenario 5: Lens does not interfere with card play

  • Given feature flag eop.features.card-magnifier is ON
  • And it is the player's turn
  • When the player hovers over a hand card (lens visible) and then clicks or drags to play it
  • Then the card play is submitted normally
  • And the lens dismisses as the pointer leaves the card

Scenario 6: Lens does not appear on disabled cards

  • Given feature flag eop.features.card-magnifier is ON
  • And it is NOT the player's turn (hand cards are disabled)
  • When the player hovers over a hand card
  • Then the lens still appears (the card is readable even when not playable)

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • UI implementation conforms to GOV.UK accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2 AA) — lens must not trap keyboard focus; keyboard users must be able to dismiss it; the lens is aria-hidden="true" (it is a visual aid, not new information).
  • Sub-second Vitest unit/component tests written with high branch coverage — at minimum: lens renders on hover, lens dismisses on mouse-leave, lens does not render when flag is OFF.
  • Feature flag eop.features.card-magnifier added to src/main/resources/application.yml (default false) and to src/test/resources/application.properties (set true for the test suite).
  • No security regressions or plaintext secrets introduced.
  • CHANGELOG.md updated under ## [Unreleased] → ### Added.
  • All child Bug Sub-tasks resolved and verified green.
  • npm run verify passes in ui/ (typecheck, ESLint, Vitest, production build).
  • ./mvnw verify passes (1280+ tests, SpotBugs 0, JaCoCo thresholds met).

comments.body:
Delivered and merged to main via PR #114 (merge commit 3278055). CI green on all four jobs: build 1m53s, image 1m23s, ui 26s, supply-chain 29s.

Three commits: 341b2fd (feature), 86b67f9 (test remediation), be8045d (docs).

Two corrections to this ticket, both deliberate and recorded rather than quietly applied.

1. The feature flag as specified was not implementable. This ticket named eop.features.card-magnifier in application.yml, and Scenario 4 required that "the eop.features.card-magnifier bean is absent from the application context". Neither is possible, for two independent reasons: a CSS lens has no Spring bean for @ConditionalOnProperty to remove, and a Spring property is invisible to a bundle Caddy serves as static assets from a separate path (ADR-017). Per ADR-037, front-end flags are build-time Vite variables. The flag shipped is VITE_CARD_MAGNIFIER_ENABLED, wired through the seven touch points the VITE_GAME_SCREEN_ENABLED precedent establishes. Nothing was added under eop.features.*.

Scenario 4 is therefore SUPERSEDED, not dropped. It is satisfied instead by the ARG in ui/Dockerfile defaulting to false, and by the flag being tested in three positions rather than two — true, false, and unset — the last confirming that the === 'true' comparison is what makes an absent variable fail closed.

This is recorded in an ADR-037 amendment rather than fixed silently, because the ticket was written in good faith from the backend convention in feature-flags.md and the next front-end story would otherwise repeat it.

2. The magnifier magnifies pixels, not meaning. This was flagged during discovery and is worth restating on the ticket. A card's threatPrompt never reaches the visible DOM — it exists only in the card's aria-label — so a 2x scale enlarges card art and rank glyphs but does not surface threat text to a sighted player. If reading the scenario text is the real requirement, that needs a re-rendered text overlay, which is a different story and was explicitly out of scope here.

Scenario audit

  1. Lens on hand-card hover — MET
  2. Lens on trick-zone-card hover — MET (a new TrickCardFace component was extracted, because a hook cannot be called inside the .map that renders the plays)
  3. Tap to show, second tap or tap-outside to dismiss — MET
  4. No lens when the flag is off — MET as superseded, see correction 1 above
  5. Does not interfere with click or drag card play, dismisses on pointer-leave — MET. A mouse pointerdown hides the lens, because setPointerCapture would otherwise route every subsequent pointermove to the captured card and drag the lens across the table. A touch pointerdown pins it and still selects the card, because click-to-select plus "Play selected card" is the WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.7 single-pointer alternative to dragging and the magnifier must not consume it.
  6. Lens still appears on a disabled card — MET. A card you cannot yet play is precisely the one you most need to read.

Definition of Done — five of five approved

  • @tester-unit-and-quality — APPROVE, after one REJECT (see below)
  • @tester-api — APPROVE
  • @security-auditor — APPROVE, no findings
  • @code-reviewer — APPROVE, zero blockers
  • @architecture-guardian — APPROVE

The REJECT is the most useful thing in this ticket. @tester-unit-and-quality found the geometry tests were tautological: they imported LENS_ZOOM and LENS_DIAMETER_PX from the module under test and asserted against them, so mutating a constant moved the rendered value and the expectation together and the suite stayed green. The 2x was an explicit product decision, revised down from 3x during discovery, and the test meant to pin it could not. It also found the inner replica's offset — the - LENS_BORDER_PX correction that keeps the magnified pixel under the cursor — was never asserted at all, that the touch-pointermove guard was untested, and that the capture-phase document listener had no unmount test.

86b67f9 closes all of it, test-only, and each closure is proved by mutation: flipping LENS_ZOOM from 2 to 3 now fails two tests, dropping the border term fails one, removing the pointer-type guard fails one. Before the remediation all three mutations left the suite green.

Four limitations reviewed and accepted rather than fixed. Each is a trap for the next person in these files rather than a defect today, and all four are in CHANGELOG.md.

  • A flag-off build still ships the lens code. Building ui/ with the flag true, false and unset emits an identical 198,662-byte bundle with eop-card-lens present in all three. Vite substitutes the value and minifies but does not prune the component it guards, so the flag controls whether the lens renders, never whether it is compiled — an affordance control, not a security boundary. Now recorded in ADR-037 next to the analogous import.meta.glob paragraph.
  • The drag ghost duplicates CardBody and hardcodes 80/120/6 instead of the HAND_CARD_* constants, which is the exact drift CardBody was extracted to prevent. Left only because the ghost cannot itself be magnified.
  • The @media (max-width: 768px) rule shrinking .eop-card to 60x90 is dead, because CardFace sets the same properties inline and inline wins. It predates this story, but the lens geometry is now pinned to 80x120, so future responsive work must move the CSS rule and the lens constants together.
  • The 100px lens overflows the 80px card by 10px on each side with no overflow: hidden on the container, so a lens overlaps its neighbours in a dense hand. The current design accepts that in exchange for showing context around the magnified point.

Merge-dark deviation, disclosed. feature-flags.md says merge with the flag off. The ARG default in ui/Dockerfile is false, so a plain docker build ships dark, but .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/update-local.sh both pass =true so the deployed artefact carries the feature that was asked for. That is exactly the position VITE_GAME_SCREEN_ENABLED already occupies. Justified by the change being wholly presentational with no server surface, and by all five DoD gates running inside this story.

Build: npm run verify in ui/ — typecheck clean, lint clean, 240 tests in 10 files, production build green. ./mvnw clean verify — 1280 tests, 0 failures, SpotBugs 0, all coverage checks met. The five prose-integrity gates re-ran green after the docs edits (26 tests).

Pure front-end plus documentation. No Java, no endpoints, no migrations, no dependency changes — ui/package.json, ui/package-lock.json and pom.xml are byte-identical to main.

renderedFields.description:
Raised as a Warning by @code-reviewer during the EOP-89 DoD review, on two successive commits, and confirmed unremediated on 3b3cb59.

Finding

tools/supply-chain/scan-dependencies.sh runs two Python heredocs. The gating one is guarded:

python3 - "$workdir/ships.json" "$allowlist" <<'PY' || gate_status=$?

The informational one (around line 296) is not:

python3 - "$workdir/all.json" "$workdir/ships.json" <<'PY'

The script sets set -euo pipefail. If the informational block ever exits non-zero — a malformed all.json, an unhandled exception, or a future edit that adds a sys.exit(1) path — set -e kills the script before the final exit "$gate_status". The documented exit contract in the script header is 0 = clean, 1 = a gating finding or allowlist drift, 2 = could not run, and this path can produce a code that means none of those things.

This is latent, not live. The informational block has no sys.exit(1) path today, so it currently only exits 0. It fails in the safe direction (loud, not silent) and cannot produce a false clean result. That is why it was approved around rather than blocking EOP-89.

Scope

  • Guard the informational heredoc. || true is the honest choice, because that pass is explicitly informational and must never gate — matching the comment already in the script.
  • While there, decide whether the same treatment is wanted for the rm -rf "$workdir" / mkdir -p "$workdir" pair. A permissions failure there exits with the shell's code (typically 1) rather than the documented 2. tools/supply-chain/audit-plugins.sh has the identical leak, so decide for both or explicitly for neither, and say which in the commit message.
  • Do not add a test for this as part of the fix unless the harness from the sibling ticket already exists — see the note below.

Acceptance criteria

  • The informational pass cannot pre-empt the gating result, demonstrated by forcing it to fail (e.g. truncating all.json) and observing the script still exits with the gating code.
  • The exit-code contract in the script header is true of every reachable path.
  • If the rm -rf/mkdir -p leak is left in place, that is recorded as a deliberate choice rather than left unmentioned.

Note on testing

@tester-unit-and-quality established that the shell-level exit paths of this script are not reachable from a Python-fixture harness — they require stubbing trivy on PATH. So a test for this belongs with that separate harness, not bolted onto this fix.

renderedFields.description:
Raised as MEDIUM by @tester-unit-and-quality during the EOP-89 DoD review and re-confirmed unchanged on adc1a98 and 3b3cb59.

Finding

The Python gating block inside tools/supply-chain/scan-dependencies.sh is the mechanism that decides whether a HIGH or CRITICAL CVE blocks the build. It enforces five distinct failure modes. During EOP-89 all of them were demonstrated by hand — a six-step transcript reverting the real postgresql fix, adding an allowlist entry, expiring it, restoring the fix with the entry still present, and deleting it — and every step behaved as designed.

Nothing in the repository re-runs those steps. A future edit to the Python block could break the gate and no automated check would notice. The gate is a security control; a control that has fired correctly once is not a control that has been tested.

Scope — six scenarios, all against synthetic Trivy JSON fixtures

  1. An unlisted HIGH or CRITICAL finding → exit 1.
  2. A correctly-allowlisted finding → exit 0, and the suppression is printed.
  3. An allowlist entry whose expires date has passed → exit 1, with the "re-argued, not re-dated" message.
  4. An allowlist entry no longer reported by the scan → exit 1, with the "DELETE the entry" message (the anti-rot direction).
  5. An entry whose module or severity no longer matches the finding → exit 1.
  6. An entry missing any of the eleven required fields → exit 1.

Plus a control: a MEDIUM finding with no entry → exit 0, because MEDIUM is deliberately non-gating.

Explicitly out of scope, and why

@tester-unit-and-quality established that exit 2 is not reachable from this harness at all. It is produced by a shell-level guard (if ! run_trivy …), so exercising it means stubbing trivy on PATH to exit non-zero — a different vehicle testing shell plumbing rather than security policy. If that is wanted, argue for it separately rather than stretching this harness to cover it. The 429 incident during EOP-89 exercised exit 2 in production, which is the only place it has been meaningfully exercised so far.

Decisions to make and record

  • Harness choice. Plain bash with assertion helpers, bats, or a Java test under src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ following that package's read-repository-files-as-text precedent. Argue the choice; do not just pick one. Note that a Java test would run inside ./mvnw verify and so would gate on every commit, whereas a shell harness needs its own CI wiring.
  • Whether `tools/supply-chain/audit-plugins.sh` gets the same treatment. Its gating logic is the older and more heavily-relied-upon of the two and is equally untested. Decide explicitly — covering one and silently leaving the other is the worst outcome.
  • Fixtures must be hermetic: no network, no real trivy invocation, no dependence on what NVD happens to report today.

Acceptance criteria

  • All six scenarios plus the MEDIUM control are automated and run in CI.
  • Each asserts the exit code and the operative part of the message, so a gate that fails for the wrong reason is caught.
  • A deliberate break of the Python block turns the new tests red — demonstrated, not asserted.
  • The harness choice and the audit-plugins.sh decision are recorded in the commit message or an ADR amendment.

renderedFields.description:
Raised independently by @code-reviewer (Warning) and @tester-unit-and-quality (INFO) during the EOP-89 DoD review, and recorded as the first negative consequence of ADR-050.

Finding

EOP-89 closed six CVEs by overriding four versions the Spring Boot parent manages, in pom.xml's <properties>:

<postgresql.version>42.7.12</postgresql.version>
<jackson-2-bom.version>2.21.5</jackson-2-bom.version>
<jackson-bom.version>3.1.5</jackson-bom.version>
<log4j2.version>2.25.5</log4j2.version>

Each holds a library at a version chosen to close a CVE rather than one the Boot parent tested against. That is correct today and rots tomorrow. The XML comment above them says so and ends: "Check with `./mvnw help:effective-pom` after a parent bump; nothing automated catches this."

That admission is the whole ticket. The instruction is only discoverable if someone happens to read the comment while bumping the parent, and a Boot bump in an unrelated PR will not prompt a reviewer to run help:effective-pom.

Two distinct failures, which must be messaged differently

  1. Redundant override — the parent's managed version has reached the override. The override is now noise that reads as a security fix. Delete it.
  2. Override now below the parent — the parent has moved past the override, so the override is actively holding a library back from a newer, presumably more secure version. This is a security regression wearing the clothes of a security fix, and it is the dangerous case. It must not be reported with the same wording or the same severity as case 1.

Note that case 2 would not necessarily be caught by the CVE scanner either: if the newer parent version fixes a CVE that was never reported against the pinned one, there is no finding to gate on.

Scope

  • A check that compares each CVE-driven override against the parent's own managed value and fails when the override is redundant or, worse, behind.
  • Follow the src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ precedent — those tests read repository files as text and run inside ./mvnw verify, so the check gates on every commit with no new CI wiring. The parent's managed values are obtainable from ./mvnw help:effective-pom, though a test that shells out to Maven from inside Maven needs thought; parsing the resolved spring-boot-dependencies POM from ~/.m2/repository may be cleaner.
  • The check needs to know which overrides are CVE-driven. Today that is expressed only in an XML comment. Consider whether a machine-readable marker is warranted, or whether the four are few enough to name in the test.
  • When this closes, amend ADR-050's first negative consequence with a dated note, per the house convention — that consequence explicitly claims nothing automated catches this, and it will have become false.

Acceptance criteria

  • A redundant override fails the build with a message telling the author to delete it.
  • An override that has fallen behind the parent fails with a distinct, sharper message naming it as a potential security regression.
  • Both are demonstrated by temporarily editing a version, not asserted.
  • ADR-050 is amended in place with a date.

renderedFields.description:
Recorded as the intended end state in ADR-050 and flagged as MEDIUM by @tester-unit-and-quality during the EOP-89 DoD review.

Finding

EOP-89 added a dependency-cve job to .github/workflows/ci.yml that gates HIGH and CRITICAL CVEs across both dependency trees. It exits non-zero and shows red on a gating finding, but it is not a required status check, so a red result does not block a merge.

That was a deliberate choice, and the reasoning was deliberately narrower than the sibling supply-chain job's. That job is non-required because "a new advisory published against a transitive dependency of a developer tool is a thing to know about, not a reason to block a merge of unrelated application code" — and that argument does not transfer, because these dependencies execute in production. The actual reason is different: a CVE gate goes red on a third-party publication against unchanged code, so requiring it lets someone else's release schedule block an unrelated PR.

Preconditions before promoting — do not skip these

  1. At least one real HIGH or CRITICAL handled in anger. The allowlist ships empty and the gating tier is currently empty, so the failure policy rests entirely on EOP-89's manual demonstration. Requiring a gate whose suppression path has never been used on a real finding is how a gate gets switched off in a hurry.
  2. Enough weekly cron runs to know the false-positive rate. The workflow already runs schedule: cron '0 6 * * 1'. One known false-positive class exists by design: the scan reads the resolved tree, so ADR-047's exclusion of H2 from the deployable jar is not honoured and an H2 CVE would gate even though H2 does not ship. Establish how often that actually fires before making it blocking.
  3. [EOP-147](https://maglez.atlassian.net/browse/EOP-147) resolved or explicitly accepted. Promoting a gate whose own logic is untested raises the cost of a logic bug from "a red job someone investigates" to "nobody can merge".
  4. [EOP-146](https://maglez.atlassian.net/browse/EOP-146) resolved, so every reachable path honours the documented exit contract.

Note on where the change actually lives

Branch protection is configured in the GitHub repository settings, not in .github/workflows/ci.yml. No comment in the workflow can make a job required, and no commit closes this ticket on its own — the repository setting has to change too. Say so in the closing comment, and update the job comment and ADR-050 in the same change, since both currently state it is not required.

Acceptance criteria

  • All four preconditions above are met or explicitly waived with reasoning.
  • dependency-cve is a required status check on main.
  • The job comment and ADR-050 are amended (in place, dated) to say so, rather than left claiming the opposite.
  • A documented escape hatch exists for the case a third-party advisory blocks an unrelated PR — either the allowlist with an expiry, or a named person who can temporarily lift the requirement. Decide which, and record it.

renderedFields.description:
Raised as two MEDIUM findings (F3 and F4) by @tester-api during the EOP-89 DoD review, re-confirmed unchanged across three commits. Both are pre-existing gaps exposed by EOP-89's Jackson bumps rather than introduced by them.

F4 — no test pins a complete response contract

Every API integration test uses point-path jsonPath assertions. @tester-api enumerated the suite and found no test that asserts the complete field set of any response body — no content().json(…, true), no JSONCompareMode.STRICT, no assertion that unexpected fields are absent.

The consequence: a serialisation change that added a field, renamed a field not currently asserted, or altered null-versus-absent handling would pass the entire 1280-test suite silently.

Concrete examples @tester-api cited:

  • Strongest existing test: TrickTransportTest — the only test asserting field absence, via 14 doesNotContain checks on notes, winningSeat, ledSuit, seatToPlay, nextLeaderSeat. This is the shape to generalise from.
  • Weakest: GameOverControllerIntegrationTest — asserts only $.rows size and $.sessionStatus. "A complete rename of every other field in the leaderboard response would pass."
  • CardControllerIntegrationTest.shouldReturnASingleCard() asserts cardId, suit, rankSymbol, threatPrompt but not rank, rankValue or id.

This matters most for the four DTOs carrying @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) — TrickDto, TrickStateDto, TrickPlayDto, ScoredPlayDto — because conditional inclusion is exactly the mechanism the EOP-89 Jackson CVEs concerned (@JsonView bypass, ignored-property handling).

F3 — TrickTransportTest does not use Spring's ObjectMapper

src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/web/TrickTransportTest.java:54:

private static final ObjectMapper MAPPER = new ObjectMapper();

A bare, unconfigured mapper. It therefore tests @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) against Jackson's defaults, not against the auto-configured mapper the application actually serialises with. If Spring's mapper ever gains a module or a changed inclusion default, the strongest serialisation test in the suite would not notice.

What is explicitly NOT the gap

EnumMirrorParityTest passes 8/8 and holds four enums in three-way agreement across Java, docs/api/openapi.yml and ui/src/api.ts. That covers enum member names only. It gives no coverage of field names, field presence, null handling, or the @JsonView/ignored-property mechanisms. Do not cite it as coverage of this gap.

Scope and decisions to record

  • Route TrickTransportTest's assertions through Spring's configured ObjectMapper (inject it, or use a slice test) rather than a bare instance.
  • Add complete-contract assertions. Choose deliberately between strict JSON comparison and an explicit expected-field-set assertion, and record why — strict comparison is stronger but brittle against additive contract evolution, which the project may well want to allow.
  • Name the endpoints excluded and why. A blanket "every endpoint" is unlikely to be right; an unexplained subset is worse.
  • Note the parallel with .opencode/rules/error-handling.md's recorded gap on the client side: nothing detects a field added to a DTO interface but not to its ui/src/api.ts parser. The same class of defect on both sides of the wire suggests a shared answer — possibly a text-comparison build gate in the style of src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/, which that rule already names as a candidate. Consider whether one mechanism closes both.

Acceptance criteria

  • No production DTO serialisation test uses a bare new ObjectMapper().
  • At least the four @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) DTOs have a complete-contract test that fails on an added, renamed or removed field — demonstrated by making such a change and watching it go red.
  • The strict-versus-explicit choice, and the excluded endpoints, are recorded.

Noticed during the EOP-89 DoD review and deliberately not fixed there on scope-discipline grounds — correcting unrelated documentation drift inside a security PR muddies the diff. @architecture-guardian independently confirmed the count and endorsed leaving it.

Finding

The supply-chain job comment in .github/workflows/ci.yml (around line 306) says it guards six plugins pinned in the plugin array of .opencode/opencode.json.

There are seven: VibeGuard, DCP, Supermemory, type-inject, scheduler, goal-plugin, smart-title. AGENTS.md lists all seven, and tools/supply-chain/expected-plugins.json is the authoritative baseline.

ci.yml is the stale side. Confirmed independently by @architecture-guardian.

Scope — and the preferred fix is deletion, not correction

Prefer removing the hand-counted number to updating it. The count is already derivable from tools/supply-chain/expected-plugins.json, and audit-plugins.sh's roster-drift check fails if that baseline and .opencode/opencode.json disagree — so the number in the comment is redundant and unguarded. Replacing "six" with "seven" reinstates exactly the same rot the moment an eighth plugin is pinned. Phrase it as "the plugins pinned in the plugin array" and let the baseline carry the count.

Before editing, grep for other stale copies. A hand-counted number that drifted in one place has usually drifted in several. Check at minimum AGENTS.md, docs/, CHANGELOG.md, the tools/supply-chain/ scripts and their JSON _comment blocks, and any ADR that mentions the plugin roster. Fixing one instance and leaving another is worse than leaving both, because it removes the inconsistency that would have prompted someone to look.

While there, consider whether any other hand-counted number in ci.yml or the supply-chain tooling has the same shape and should be dereferenced the same way.

Acceptance criteria

  • No document states a plugin count that can drift silently from tools/supply-chain/expected-plugins.json.
  • Every stale copy found by the grep is dealt with in the same change, or explicitly listed as out of scope with a reason.
  • tools/supply-chain/audit-plugins.sh still exits 0.

Context

EOP-88 added SlidingWindowCounter (src/main/java/org/maglez/eop/adapter/web/SlidingWindowCounter.java) as the counting mechanism behind ReadRateLimitInterceptor. It is a general-purpose per-key sliding window: 60-second window, prune-check-insert under one lock per key, fail-closed when the key table saturates, Retry-After floored at one second, refused calls not counted.

The same algorithm already existed twice before EOP-88, in InMemoryJoinAttemptLimiter and InMemorySessionCreationLimiter. EOP-88 deliberately did not migrate them, and ADR-051 records why: ADR-019 designates the join-attempt throttle a primary security control, and refactoring it in the same change as a brand-new untested limiter would have put both in one review. @code-reviewer assessed that call during the EOP-88 Definition of Done gate and found it defensible, observing that SlidingWindowCounter is in effect the extracted abstraction the other two would become.

So the algorithm currently exists in three places. This ticket closes that.

Scope

Migrate both existing limiters onto SlidingWindowCounter, preserving every behaviour their tests pin:

  • InMemorySessionCreationLimiter — one window per address, but note it counts successes rather than failures and follows a reserve-before-work pattern: recordCreation is the authoritative atomic gate called before any database write, and refundCreation returns the slot when the downstream use case throws. SlidingWindowCounter has no refund operation today, so this is the substantive design question — either add one or keep the reservation logic in the limiter and use the counter only for the window.
  • InMemoryJoinAttemptLimiter — two windows (per address and per code) rather than one, so it needs two counters rather than one, and it counts failed attempts.
  • Both expose a lock-free checkAllowed pre-check for use-case early exit. SlidingWindowCounter deliberately has none, because an interceptor has no database work to avoid and acting on a stale answer would reintroduce the race the lock closes. Decide whether to add one to the counter or keep it in the adapters.
  • The UNKNOWN_ADDRESS_KEY sentinel ("\u0000unknown") and its non-collision guarantee with resolved addresses must survive.

Constraints

  • The join-attempt throttle is a primary security control under ADR-019, not defence in depth. A six-to-eight character join code is only unguessable while guessing is slow.
  • Do this as its own change, with the existing InMemoryJoinAttemptLimiterTest and InMemorySessionCreationLimiterTest passing unmodified wherever possible. A test that has to be rewritten to accommodate the refactor is a behaviour change and needs justifying individually.
  • Amend ADR-051 in place with a dated note when this lands, and delete accepted limitation 8 ("the algorithm exists in three places") from it.

Acceptance criteria

  1. InMemoryJoinAttemptLimiter and InMemorySessionCreationLimiter both delegate their window arithmetic to SlidingWindowCounter; no third copy of prune-check-insert remains in src/main/java.
  2. Every pre-existing test in InMemoryJoinAttemptLimiterTest, InMemorySessionCreationLimiterTest and ForwardedForThrottleBypassIntegrationTest still passes, and any that had to change is justified in the PR description.
  3. The reserve-before-work and refund semantics of session creation are preserved, with a test proving a refused creation commits no row and a failed downstream call returns the slot.
  4. Fail-closed saturation behaviour is preserved for all three limiters.
  5. ADR-051 is amended and its accepted limitation 8 removed.

Epic: Performance Testing Infrastructure

Business Value

The project has a k6 load-testing setup (test/k6/) with an InfluxDB + Grafana monitoring stack, but k6 metrics have never reached InfluxDB — the Grafana dashboard has always been empty. ADR-016 documents this as a known-broken "Neutral" consequence and explicitly states "Repair belongs in its own story."

The user requirement is: "I want k6 run on every pipeline build."

Scope

This Epic covers two independently shippable stories:

  1. EOP-153 (Story A) — Repair the k6 → InfluxDB write path so the local Grafana dashboard shows real data.
  2. EOP-154 (Story B) — Add k6 as a regression canary on every CI build.

Why two stories?

These are separate concerns with different risk profiles:

  • Story A is a local developer-experience fix with no CI impact. It requires investigating an unresolved 401 from InfluxDB and amending ADR-016 plus three other documentation files.
  • Story B is a CI pipeline change that must work without InfluxDB/Grafana and must not depend on Story A being done first.

Sequencing: Story B can be delivered independently. Story A is recommended first only because it closes the ADR-016 disclosure cleanly and gives developers a working dashboard before CI numbers appear — but it is not a hard dependency.

Out of scope

  • Resilience4j (no external calls exist yet — see resilience.md)
  • LOAD_STAGES or STRESS_STAGES profiles in CI
  • Any new monitoring infrastructure beyond what already exists in docker-compose.yml

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a developer running load tests locally

I want k6 metrics to actually reach InfluxDB and appear in the Grafana dashboard

So that I can analyse latency distributions, VU ramp behaviour and threshold breaches visually rather than reading raw k6 terminal output

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: EOP-153 — Performance Testing Infrastructure
  • Target Persona: Developer running test/k6/run.sh on their local machine
  • Value Proposition: The k6 + InfluxDB + Grafana stack has existed since the project was set up, but the Grafana dashboard has always been empty. ADR-016 (lines ~147–163) documents this as a known-broken "Neutral" consequence and explicitly states "Repair belongs in its own story." This is that story.

Why this is Story A (not bundled with CI)

This is a local developer-experience fix with zero CI impact. The unresolved 401 from InfluxDB is the genuine blocker and requires investigation, not a config tweak. Story B (CI regression gate, EOP-155) must work without InfluxDB/Grafana and must not depend on this story being done first — they are independently shippable.

Known Causes (from ADR-016)

Three independent causes were identified:

  1. Already fixed: .env.example shipped INFLUXDB_URL=http://influxdb:8086 — a container hostname unresolvable from the host, also missing the /k6 database path. The tracked file now reads http://localhost:8086/k6.
  2. Shell environment: direnv exports the stale value into an already-running shell, so editing .env appears to have no effect. The developer's local .env:65 does set INFLUXDB_URL. Documenting the direnv reload / shell restart workflow is sufficient here.
  3. UNRESOLVED BLOCKER: The stack sets INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED: "true" while the k6 output URL carries no credentials. A direct credentialed write still returned 401, and why the configured admin credentials are refused is unknown. This is the core work of this story.

k6 exit-code trap

k6 logs Couldn't write stats once per flush interval (41 messages in a 40s run) but exits 0. Any verification step must assert on more than the exit code — check that the k6 measurement actually appears in InfluxDB after the run.

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag: Not applicable — this is a local tooling fix with no application code changes.
  • Deployment Behaviour: Changes are to docker-compose.yml, .env.example, and documentation files only. No Spring Boot code is touched.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: k6 metrics reach InfluxDB

  • Given the monitoring stack is running (docker compose up -d)
  • And the developer has run direnv reload (or opened a fresh shell) after editing .env
  • When test/k6/run.sh completes a SMOKE_STAGES run
  • Then the k6 measurement exists in the InfluxDB k6 database (verifiable via curl http://localhost:8086/query?db=k6&q=SHOW+MEASUREMENTS)
  • And the Grafana dashboard at http://localhost:3000 shows non-empty time-series data for http_req_duration and http_reqs

Scenario 2: Authentication is resolved

  • Given INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED is set in docker-compose.yml
  • When k6 writes metrics to http://localhost:8086/k6
  • Then the write returns HTTP 204 (no auth error)
  • And no Couldn't write stats lines appear in k6 output

Implementation options to investigate (choose one and document the decision):

  • Option A: Embed credentials in the k6 output URL (http://admin:password@localhost:8086/k6) — simplest, but puts credentials in .env.
  • Option B: Set INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED: "false" in docker-compose.yml — acceptable for a loopback-bound stack with no external exposure; eliminates the credential management problem entirely.
  • Option C: Investigate why the configured admin credentials are refused (may be an InfluxDB 1.8 initialisation issue with INFLUXDB_ADMIN_USER / INFLUXDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD env vars not being picked up on a pre-existing volume).

Scenario 3: direnv / shell reload is documented

  • Given a developer edits .env to set INFLUXDB_URL
  • When they consult README.md or docs/performance/TRENDS.md
  • Then they find a clear note that direnv reload (or opening a new shell) is required for the change to take effect

Scenario 4: "Known broken" disclosures are retired

  • Given this story is complete and metrics are flowing
  • When a developer reads any of the four documentation locations listed below
  • Then none of them contain the "known broken" disclosure about k6 → InfluxDB

The four locations that must be updated together (they move as one atomic change):

  1. docs/adr/ADR-016-*.md — retire the "Neutral" known-broken consequence (lines ~147–163)
  2. .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md — remove the > *Known broken:* blockquote
  3. docs/performance/TRENDS.md — remove the disclosure at the foot of the file
  4. CHANGELOG.md — move from "Known issues" to "Fixed" under ## [Unreleased]

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • Root cause of the 401 identified and resolved (with chosen option documented in ADR-016 amendment).
  • test/k6/run.sh completes a SMOKE_STAGES run with zero Couldn't write stats lines.
  • InfluxDB k6 database contains http_req_duration and http_reqs measurements after the run (verified by query, not just exit code).
  • Grafana dashboard at http://localhost:3000 shows non-empty data.
  • All four documentation locations updated atomically (ADR-016, performance-testing.md, TRENDS.md, CHANGELOG.md).
  • direnv reload / shell restart workflow documented.
  • No secrets committed in plaintext — credentials (if Option A is chosen) go in .env (gitignored), not in docker-compose.yml or .env.example.
  • All child Bug Sub-tasks resolved and verified green.

Technical Notes

  • InfluxDB version is 1.8 (pinned in docker-compose.yml). The INFLUXDB_ADMIN_USER / INFLUXDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD env vars are the 1.8 initialisation mechanism — they only take effect on a fresh volume. If the volume already exists from a previous run without auth, the credentials may not have been set. docker compose down -v followed by docker compose up -d may be required to reproduce the 401 cleanly.
  • run.sh streams with k6 run --out influxdb="$INFLUXDB_URL". The InfluxDB output plugin in k6 uses the URL scheme http://[user:pass@]host:port/database.
  • tools/supply-chain/ audits only the seven OpenCode npm plugins — no action needed here for supply-chain compliance.
  • Commit prefix for this story: EOP-154 Done

comments.body:
Delivered on PR #123 — awaiting human approval to merge

Branch eop-154-repair-k6-influxdb-write-path, commits 392f898 (the repair) and d710ed4 (gate-review remediations).

The handed-down root cause was wrong, and there were three faults, not one

The diagnosis in this ticket — that the influxdb_data volume predated auth being enabled, so no admin user exists and every write 401s — does not reproduce. Probed against the live stack:

probe result
write with no credentials 401
write with the container's own $INFLUXDB_ADMIN_USER:$INFLUXDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD 204
write with deliberately wrong credentials 401

Real credentials succeeding and wrong ones failing is a working auth setup. The timeline says why: auth was enabled on 2026-07-27 (cb9bd34), and the volume actually in use, eop-monitoring_influxdb_data, was created 2026-08-05 — after, so the seed credentials were honoured on its first init. (The older eop-threat-medeling_influxdb_data is the pre-name: orphan ADR-016 warns about; nothing mounts it.) The ticket's question "why are the configured admin credentials refused" is therefore void — they are not refused. That clause has been deleted from ADR-016 rather than carried forward.

The actual write-path fault is mundane: INFLUXDB_URL=http://localhost:8086/k6 carries no userinfo, so every k6 write was unauthenticated, and correctly 401'd.

Two further faults on the read path, recorded in no ticket, would each have left the dashboard empty on their own:

  1. The provisioned datasource took {{url: $ {INFLUXDB_URL}

    }} — a host address. access: proxy means Grafana makes the call itself, and inside that container localhost:8086 is Grafana. Proved from inside eop-grafana: curl localhost:8086/ping → connection refused (exit 7), curl influxdb:8086/ping → 204. One variable was serving two consumers with mutually incompatible requirements.

  2. The datasource declared no uid, so provisioning generated one (observed P951FEA4DE68E13C5) while all ten dashboard panels reference "uid": "InfluxDB". No panel could resolve its datasource.

Chosen option: B (auth disabled), per the PO's recommendation

INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED: "false", and INFLUXDB_ADMIN_USER/INFLUXDB_ADMIN_PASSWORD deleted. Rationale, recorded in the ADR-016 amendment and accepted by @security-auditor: the port binds to 127.0.0.1 only, the database holds load-test timing samples with no application or personal data, and k6's only authentication route is embedding a password in the --out influxdb=$INFLUXDB_URL URL that test/k6/run.sh echoes to the terminal — so auth bought no confidentiality against this threat model while guaranteeing a secret in scrollback, shell history and any CI log.

Consequently INFLUXDB_USER/INFLUXDB_PASSWORD are removed from .env.example and SETUP.md — a variable nothing reads is worse than absent. Grafana's own admin credentials are untouched.

No `docker compose down -v` was needed. With auth off InfluxDB ignores the users the volume already holds, so the existing metric history survived. What was needed, and is now documented as a finding, is a deleteDatasources block: pinning a uid for a datasource whose name Grafana's sqlite volume already knows under a generated uid makes provisioning abort startup — Datasource provisioning error: data source not found, cascading through five modules to exit 1.

AC verification — by query, never by exit code

A real test/k6/run.sh SMOKE_STAGES run:

  • Zero Couldn't write stats (41 before the fix). AC-2.
  • SHOW MEASUREMENTS → 16 k6 measurements including http_req_duration and http_reqs.
  • count(value) = 221 for both, matching k6's own reported 221 requests exactly — the independent cross-check this ticket demanded instead of trusting the exit code.
  • Through Grafana's own datasource proxy at uid/InfluxDB, a percentile(value, 95) query returned a non-empty series (5 buckets, first 16.108 at 16:12:10Z) — which proves the pinned uid and the container-network URL together, not just that InfluxDB has data. AC-1.
  • 663/663 checks passed, p95 10.13 ms against the 200 ms threshold.
  • My two manual probe measurements were dropped afterwards, so the 16 are genuine k6 output.

AC-3 — the direnv reload requirement is documented in docs/performance/TRENDS.md, .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md, .env.example and SETUP.md.

AC-4 — all four disclosures retired atomically in one commit: ADR-016's Neutral consequence (rewritten to past tense, superseded by a dated amendment), the .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md blockquote, the docs/performance/TRENDS.md blockquote, and CHANGELOG.md's ### Known issues section (deleted; the entry moved to ### Fixed, and a dangling "see Known issues" cross-reference fixed). The replacement is not silence — the k6 exit-0 trap is a property of k6 and did not go away, so both rule and TRENDS blockquotes now carry a standing "verify by query, never by exit code" warning with the SHOW MEASUREMENTS command.

Gates

./mvnw clean verify cold and serial: exit 0, 1360 tests, 0 failures, coverage met (96% instruction / 88% branch). All eight prose gates ran, AdrIndexConsistencyTest included, which is what holds the amended ADR status line against docs/adr/README.md.

All five DoD gates returned VERDICT: APPROVE. Three MINOR findings were remediated in d710ed4 (a stale INFLUXDB_* instruction in SETUP.md, a misattributed ADR-043 citation in CHANGELOG.md, and a missing EOP-154 entry in ADR-016's ## Related); @security-auditor and @code-reviewer were then re-dispatched against d710ed4 and both approved again. Two reviewer claims were checked rather than accepted: a red-build report that proved to be an artefact of five agents building concurrently in one worktree, and an assertion that ADR-016 cites ADR-043 at line 255 — grep -c returns 0.

No secret value appears anywhere in the diff; the only credential-shaped lines are removals.

Deliberately deferred → EOP-161

Nothing mechanically keeps the datasource uid in step with the ten dashboard panel references, nor holds INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED at "false". Two of this story's three faults were exactly that class of unguarded cross-file mismatch, so a consistency gate is warranted — filed as EOP-161 along with pinning grafana/grafana:latest.

Closed — PR #123 merged to main

PR #123 was merged to main on 2026-08-23T17:00:59Z (d710ed4 → base a91366a, 10 files, +241/−51). This ticket's status had lagged at To Do despite the merge; transitioned to Done now.

No further work outstanding on this story. The deferred consistency gate (datasource uid ↔ dashboard panel references, and holding INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED at "false") remains tracked separately as EOP-161.

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a developer merging code to main

I want k6 to run a smoke test on every CI build

So that a performance regression is caught at the PR stage rather than discovered manually after deployment

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: EOP-153 — Performance Testing Infrastructure
  • Target Persona: Developer / reviewer on a PR to main
  • Value Proposition: The user requirement is "I want k6 run on every pipeline build." This story delivers that. It adds k6 as a regression canary — not SLO verification — on every CI build.

Why this is Story B (independent of Story A)

Story A (EOP-154) repairs the local InfluxDB/Grafana write path. This story must work without InfluxDB/Grafana and must not depend on EOP-154 being done first. The CI run writes no metrics to any database; results go to a workflow artifact only.

Framing: regression canary, not SLO verification

The existing image job runs on a shared 2-vCPU GitHub Actions runner — not a production-like environment. Golden Rule 1 of performance-testing.md states "Always run against a production-like environment." This story deliberately frames the CI k6 run as a regression canary rather than SLO verification. The current headroom is ~20× (p95 baseline 9.86ms vs 200ms threshold), so runner noise is unlikely to cause flakes — but this framing must be explicit in the ADR (see DoD).

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag: Not applicable — this is a CI pipeline change with no application code.
  • Deployment Behaviour: Changes are to .github/workflows/ci.yml only (plus a new ADR). No Spring Boot or front-end code is touched.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: k6 smoke test runs on every CI trigger

  • Given a push to main, a PR targeting main, the weekly cron, or a workflow_dispatch
  • And the image job has started the application stack via docker compose -f compose.app.yml up -d
  • When the CI workflow runs
  • Then a new k6-smoke step (or job) runs test/k6/health-check.js (or equivalent) using the SMOKE_STAGES profile (40s, 5→10 VUs)
  • And LOAD_STAGES and STRESS_STAGES profiles are never used in CI

Scenario 2: k6 is installed in CI without a new unvetted action

  • Given k6 is not pre-installed on ubuntu-latest
  • When the CI workflow runs
  • Then k6 is installed via a method that has been assessed for supply-chain risk
  • And the chosen installation method and its supply-chain assessment are documented in the new ADR

Note: `grafana/setup-k6-action` is the canonical approach but adding a new third-party GitHub Action is a supply-chain consideration. `tools/supply-chain/` currently audits only the seven OpenCode npm plugins, not GitHub Actions. The ADR must record the assessment explicitly — do not silently add a third-party action without it.

Scenario 3: Threshold breach behaviour is explicit

  • Given the k6 thresholds are p(95) < 200ms, max < 1000ms, http_req_failed rate < 0.001 with abortOnFail: true on the first two
  • When a threshold is breached on a CI run
  • Then the behaviour is one of the following (chosen in the ADR, not left implicit):
  • Option FAIL: The CI step exits non-zero and the build fails. Chosen if the team accepts that a flaky perf gate may block merges. Note: build is currently the only required status check on main — state in the ADR whether the new k6 step/job becomes a required check.
  • Option WARN: The CI step always exits 0 but emits a warning annotation. Chosen if the team prioritises merge availability over hard enforcement.

Recommendation (see below): start with WARN, promote to FAIL after observing runner variance over ≥10 builds.

Scenario 4: CI results are not written to docs/performance/TRENDS.md

  • Given a CI k6 run completes
  • When the run finishes (pass or fail)
  • Then results are uploaded as a workflow artifact (e.g. k6-results.json) and are never committed to docs/performance/TRENDS.md
  • And the step description or ADR explicitly states: "CI runner numbers must not be mixed into the curated baseline. The baseline (p95 9.86ms) was measured on a developer Mac via Colima against a `t3.small`-bound topology. Mixing runner numbers would repeat the 2026-08-05 baseline reset."

Scenario 5: Exit code is not the sole success signal

  • Given k6 exits 0 even when it cannot write stats (known behaviour — 41 Couldn't write stats lines in a 40s run)
  • When the CI step completes
  • Then the step asserts on threshold results from the k6 JSON output, not solely on the process exit code
  • And the step fails (or warns, per Scenario 3) if the JSON output is absent or malformed

Scenario 6: InfluxDB/Grafana are absent from CI

  • Given the CI environment has no InfluxDB or Grafana container
  • When the k6 smoke test runs
  • Then k6 runs without --out influxdb=... — no attempt is made to write to InfluxDB
  • And the step does not fail due to a missing InfluxDB endpoint

Scenario 7: BASE_URL is correct for the CI stack

  • Given the image job polls https://localhost/health through Caddy with curl -fsSk
  • And run.sh already defaults BASE_URL to https://localhost and passes --insecure-skip-tls-verify for Caddy's self-signed tls internal cert
  • When the CI k6 step runs
  • Then BASE_URL=https://localhost is set (or confirmed as the default) and --insecure-skip-tls-verify is passed

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • k6 runs on every CI trigger (push to main, PR to main, weekly cron, workflow_dispatch) using SMOKE_STAGES only.
  • k6 is installed in CI; supply-chain assessment documented in the new ADR.
  • Threshold breach behaviour (FAIL vs WARN) decided and documented in the ADR; whether the new step/job becomes a required status check on main is stated explicitly.
  • CI results uploaded as a workflow artifact; never committed to docs/performance/TRENDS.md.
  • Step asserts on JSON output, not solely on exit code.
  • No --out influxdb=... flag in the CI step.
  • BASE_URL=https://localhost and --insecure-skip-tls-verify confirmed.
  • New ADR filed and linked here (flag for @architecture-guardian).
  • CHANGELOG.md updated under ## [Unreleased] → Added.
  • All child Bug Sub-tasks resolved and verified green.

Open Questions / Flags for @architecture-guardian

  1. ADR required: The decision to add a CI performance gate, the profile choice (SMOKE_STAGES), the fail-vs-warn decision, the supply-chain assessment of the chosen k6 install method, and the explicit non-goal of mixing CI numbers into the curated baseline all warrant a new ADR. Flag this for @architecture-guardian before delivery begins.
  2. Required status check: Does the new k6 step/job become a required status check on main? Currently only build is required. Adding a flaky perf gate as required would block all merges on runner variance. Decide in the ADR.
  3. `grafana/setup-k6-action` vs `apt-get`: apt-get install k6 via the Grafana apt repo is an alternative to the GitHub Action and avoids adding a new action dependency. Both options have supply-chain surface; the ADR must record which was chosen and why.

Recommendation: Fail vs Warn

Start with WARN (Option WARN), promote to FAIL after ≥10 builds.

Rationale: the ~20× headroom (9.86ms vs 200ms) makes a genuine regression very unlikely to be masked by runner noise, but unlikely is not impossible — a shared runner under load could add 50–100ms. A flaky required check that blocks all merges on a 2-vCPU runner spike is a worse outcome than a missed regression. Observe runner variance over 10+ builds, then promote to FAIL if the p95 never exceeds ~80ms on a clean run.

Technical Notes

  • The image job is at .github/workflows/ci.yml:134. It already does docker compose -f compose.app.yml up -d and polls https://localhost/health — this is the natural host for the k6 step.
  • run.sh already handles BASE_URL and --insecure-skip-tls-verify. The CI step can call run.sh directly or inline the equivalent k6 run command.
  • SMOKE_STAGES is defined in test/k6/config/options.js: 40s, ramps 5→10→0 VUs.
  • Commit prefix for this story: EOP-155 In Progress

comments.body:
*PR opened: 122(https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/122)* — eop-155-ci-k6-regression-canary → main, three commits.

What shipped

k6 runs SMOKE_STAGES (40s, 5→10 VU) as a step inside the existing image CI job, which already stands up the full Postgres + app + Caddy stack for its smoke test — so no new infrastructure was needed. Decided in [ADR-055|docs/adr/ADR-055-k6-performance-check-in-ci.md].

All seven acceptance criteria met, each confirmed with a file:line by @code-reviewer.

Key decisions

Decision Rationale
Digest-pinned grafana/k6:2.2.0@sha256:9bd01d69… container Avoids grafana/setup-k6-action, which would have been the first unaudited third-party Action in the pipeline. The image carries provenance + SBOM attestations.
Relaxed CI thresholds, split by metric class http_req_failed rate < 0.001 fails hard (a non-2xx is never runner noise). Latency gets a relaxed CI budget — p(95) < 500, max < 2000 — immune to 2-vCPU jitter but still catching gross regression.
Assert on the k6 JSON, not just the exit code Two genuinely independent signals. ADR-016 is the motivating case: the InfluxDB write failure logs errors on every flush yet exits 0.
--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" with /scripts:ro + separate writable /results The image defaults to uid 12345, which cannot write a 0755 runner-owned mount — the original form would have failed every build. Chosen over chmod 0777 as least privilege.

Why this is a canary, not an SLO measurement

Golden Rule 1 of .opencode/rules/performance-testing.md requires a production-like environment. A shared 2-vCPU GitHub runner is neither the developer Mac nor the t3.small target, so CI numbers are never written to `docs/performance/TRENDS.md` — doing so would repeat the exact error that forced the 2026-08-05 baseline reset. Results go to a k6-results workflow artifact only.

Evidence

  • ./mvnw clean verify → BUILD SUCCESS, exit 0, 1360 tests, 0 failures, all coverage checks met
  • The JSON gate was negative-tested in ten cases (missing file, empty file, malformed JSON, wrong JSON type, threshold added, threshold removed, threshold breached, non-boolean value, k6 exit 99 with healthy JSON, healthy run) — nine exit 1, only the healthy case exits 0. So it provably cannot silently no-op.
  • The --network host path was verified with a real 40s run against the live stack: 663/663 checks, http_req_failed 0.00%, p95 10.51ms, max 39.53ms — roughly 48× headroom against the CI budget.
  • Five-gate DoD round: @tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian — all five APPROVE.

⚠️ Action required from the repository owner

The image job is not a required status check, so a k6 breach fails loudly without blocking merges. Promoting it is a GitHub branch-protection setting — merging this PR does not self-effect it. ADR-055 records it as Outstanding.

Follow-ups accepted, not fixed here

  1. GET /health is shallow — it touches no database or business path, so it cannot catch the N+1 / missing-index regressions ADR-055 names as motivation. A second scenario against /api/v1/cards would fix this.
  2. The "response time < 100ms" check is ungated — k6 check() failures never affect the exit code and no checks_failed threshold exists, so it reads as a constraint while enforcing nothing.
  3. A build gate for the EXPECTED_THRESHOLD_COUNT=3 ↔ options-ci.js coupling, in the style of AdrIndexConsistencyTest.
  4. --network host grants whole-host network access, not just port 443 — acceptable on an ephemeral runner but not minimal.
  5. Bringing the k6 container under tools/supply-chain/ — the Actions and container layer is a pre-existing audit gap.

Moved to In Progress rather than Done, pending merge.

Raised by @tester-api during the EOP-155 DoD gate round. Non-blocking follow-up.

Problem

The CI canary added by EOP-155 loads only GET /health, which returns a static OK string and touches no database, no JPA repository and no business code path. ADR-055 names "N+1 queries, missing indexes, 50x slowdown" as the motivation for the canary, but the current scenario cannot catch that class of regression.

What it genuinely proves is narrower: the JVM is alive, Tomcat is accepting connections, Caddy is proxying, and the stack serves under 10 VUs.

Proposed fix

Add a scenario against GET /api/v1/cards?size=1. This is already known-good in CI because the image job's smoke test asserts "totalElements":68 against it, and it exercises PostgreSQL, the Liquibase schema, JPA mapping, the catalogue query and Page<T> serialisation.

Acceptance criteria

  • SMOKE_STAGES only — never LOAD_STAGES or STRESS_STAGES in CI
  • Thresholds still sourced from test/k6/config/options-ci.js
  • If the threshold count changes, EXPECTED_THRESHOLD_COUNT in .github/workflows/ci.yml is updated in the same commit (see the sibling follow-up proposing a build gate for that coupling)
  • Results go to the k6-results workflow artifact; nothing is written to docs/performance/TRENDS.md
  • ADR-055 amended so its coverage claim matches its stated motivation

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @tester-api during the EOP-155 DoD gate round. Non-blocking follow-up.

Problem

test/k6/health-check.js carries a check() named "response time < 100ms". In k6, a check() failure does not affect the exit code, and no threshold on checks or checks_failed exists in either test/k6/config/options.js or test/k6/config/options-ci.js.

Consequence: a response between 100ms and 500ms fails that check silently while passing every threshold. On a shared 2-vCPU GitHub runner, 100ms is plausibly exceeded with no build consequence at all. The check reads as a gate but gates nothing.

The real gate is the p(95) < 500 threshold.

Options

  1. Delete the check and rely on p(95) < 500. Simplest, removes the false impression.
  2. Add a checks_failed threshold to make it real. Leaning reject — this reintroduces exactly the runner flakiness that ADR-055 deliberately designed out by relaxing latency to 500ms.
  3. Rename it to mark it advisory (e.g. "response time < 100ms (advisory, not gated)"), keeping the finer-grained signal in the uploaded artifact.

Prefer option 1 or 3. Whichever is chosen, record the reasoning — the value of the check is artifact readability, not gating.

Recommended by @tester-unit-and-quality during the EOP-155 DoD gate round. Non-blocking follow-up.

Problem

.github/workflows/ci.yml hardcodes EXPECTED_THRESHOLD_COUNT=3 in the k6 assertion step. That constant is coupled to the number of thresholds declared in test/k6/config/options-ci.js by comment only — nothing enforces it.

The constant exists for a good reason: it is what makes the generic threshold-flattening gate fail loudly when a threshold is added or removed, instead of silently passing. But if the two drift, the protection quietly weakens.

Proposed fix

A JUnit text-reading test in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/, in the established style of AdrIndexConsistencyTest and DeckArithmeticClaimsTest:

  • Parse EXPECTED_THRESHOLD_COUNT=<n> out of .github/workflows/ci.yml
  • Count threshold: entries in test/k6/config/options-ci.js
  • Assert equality
  • Also assert -e K6_ENV=ci is present in the docker run invocation

Zero new dependencies; consistent with the existing prose-gate precedent.

Important nuance to preserve

The K6_ENV assertion is the non-obvious half. If -e K6_ENV=ci were dropped, health-check.js would fall back to THRESHOLDS from options.js — which also has exactly 3 thresholds — so the count check would still pass. That is a safe failure mode (stricter local SLO thresholds, not looser) but an invisible one. Asserting on K6_ENV is what makes it visible.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @security-auditor during the EOP-155 DoD gate round, explicitly non-blocking.

Problem

EOP-155 introduced the first pinned external container into CI:

grafana/k6:2.2.0@sha256:9bd01d6941fca969cb61bb57d2da5ee9b385fe2aa8881df3798c196564d6ace6

tools/supply-chain/audit-plugins.sh covers only the seven OpenCode npm plugins baselined in tools/supply-chain/expected-plugins.json. The GitHub Actions / container layer and the whole Maven plugin layer are uncovered.

This is a monitoring gap, not an exposure — the image is digest-pinned and carries buildx provenance and SBOM attestations, which is stronger supply-chain posture than the unpinned Actions already in the workflow.

Two pinning traps that MUST be preserved

Both were hit empirically during EOP-155 and are recorded in ADR-055 amendment 2. Any tooling built here must encode them:

  1. The tag is `2.2.0`, NOT `v2.2.0`. docker manifest inspect grafana/k6:v2.2.0 fails.
  2. The pin must be the OCI *index digest*, read from the top-level Digest: of docker buildx imagetools inspect. Never a per-platform sub-manifest (pinning the arm64 one breaks ubuntu-latest with "no matching manifest for linux/amd64"), and never the output of docker inspect on a developer Mac, which returns a different digest again.

Scope options — decide in an ADR first

  1. Container only — smallest, closes the gap this story opened.
  2. Also the GitHub Actions. None are digest-pinned today (actions/checkout@v4, docker/build-push-action@v6, actions/upload-artifact@v4, …). This is pre-existing posture, not an EOP-155 regression.
  3. Also the Maven layer. 14 bound plugins, ~31 in effective pluginManagement, so a Boot parent bump moves ~30 versions in one line. Largest real uncovered surface.

Whichever scope is chosen, a new expected-containers.json baseline (or an extension of the existing one) is needed, plus the rule from AGENTS.md: update the baseline in the same commit as the pin change, never to turn a red job green.

renderedFields.description:
Raised by @security-auditor during the EOP-155 DoD gate round, severity MEDIUM — judged acceptable on an ephemeral runner, but not minimal.

Problem

The k6 CI step runs docker run --network host … so the container can reach Caddy on 127.0.0.1:443. That places the container in the host network namespace, which grants:

  • every host port and every loopback service, not just 443
  • the ability to bind arbitrary host ports

.opencode/rules/security.md mandates least privilege — minimal access per operation. Only outbound access to port 443 is actually needed.

Context — this was a deliberate, verified choice

It is not an oversight. The path was verified working both locally under Colima and on real GitHub runners (CI runs 32644143043 and 32644675531), and ADR-055 amendment 1 records the evidence. The rest of the step is already least-privilege: --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)", /scripts mounted :ro, and only /results writable.

Options

  1. Join the app's Compose network (eop-app_default) and address Caddy by service name. Needs a check on TLS/SNI behaviour and the BASE_URL value, since the cert is tls internal for localhost.
  2. Run k6 as a Compose sidecar. Cost: entangles the load-testing tool with the shipping application topology — which is precisely why it was kept out of compose.app.yml in the first place.
  3. Accept and document the trade-off via an ADR-055 amendment.

Option 3 is a legitimate outcome. If options 1 and 2 both cost more than the risk they remove, the right answer is an explicit, reasoned acceptance rather than a change for its own sake — but that acceptance should be recorded, not left implicit.

renderedFields.description:
Follow-up to EOP-154, raised by the DoD gate agents on PR #123 and explicitly deferred there as non-blocking.

Why

EOP-154 repaired a metrics pipeline that had been silently broken for four weeks. Two of the three faults were wiring mismatches between files that nothing compares:

  1. tools/monitoring/grafana/datasources/datasource.yml declared no uid, so Grafana's provisioner generated a random one (observed P951FEA4DE68E13C5) while all ten panels in tools/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/k6-load-testing.json reference "uid": "InfluxDB".
  2. That datasource took {{url: $ {INFLUXDB_URL}

    }}, a host address unreachable from inside the Grafana container.

Both are now fixed and both are explained by inline comments — but a comment is the only thing preventing a future edit from re-introducing either. The repository already has the pattern for closing exactly this class of gap: the text-comparison gates in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/, of which EnumMirrorParityTest holds three files in agreement rather than each against a constant.

Scope

A. Monitoring-stack consistency gate (@tester-unit-and-quality specified this in its EOP-154 review):

  • Parse tools/monitoring/grafana/datasources/datasource.yml; assert uid is InfluxDB.
  • Parse tools/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/k6-load-testing.json; assert every datasource.uid equals the datasource's own declared uid — the two must be compared with each other, not each against a hardcoded literal, or the test drifts with the thing it guards. There are 10 occurrences today (lines 53, 107, 160, 215, 309, 329, 350, 438, 458, 536), enumerated by @architecture-guardian.
  • Assert docker-compose.yml still sets INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED: "false" — the deliberate ADR-016 decision that must not silently revert, since reverting it re-breaks every write.
  • Consider also asserting the datasource url is a Compose service address rather than localhost, which is the second read-path fault.
  • Plain JUnit 5 reading the files as text/YAML/JSON, no Spring context, sub-second. Mirror the existing docs/ gate style, including a minimum-count floor so the test cannot silently match nothing (cf. MermaidSequenceTextTest's MINIMUM_SEQUENCE_DIAGRAMS).

B. Pin `grafana/grafana:latest` (docker-compose.yml:33) — pre-existing, and the only unpinned image in the monitoring stack (influxdb:1.8 is pinned). The risk is reproducibility drift rather than security exposure: a docker compose pull can change Grafana's provisioning or dashboard-schema behaviour with no signal. @code-reviewer accepted deferring it precisely because doing it properly means choosing a version or digest and then re-verifying the provisioned datasource and dashboard still load against it — which is this story's work, not a one-line edit.

Out of scope

  • Grafana's 0.0.0.0:3000 publication (docker-compose.yml:36). Pre-existing, raised as INFO by @security-auditor on EOP-154, and a separate decision with its own threat-model argument.
  • The two now-inert INFLUXDB_USER/INFLUXDB_PASSWORD lines that may linger in a developer's gitignored .env. Nothing reads them; no repository change can remove them.

Acceptance criteria

  • The gate fails when datasource.yml's uid and the dashboard's panel references are made to disagree, and when INFLUXDB_HTTP_AUTH_ENABLED is flipped to "true". Demonstrate both by deliberately breaking each and showing the build red, then restoring.
  • ./mvnw verify green with the gate in place.
  • The Grafana image carries an explicit version or digest, and the dashboard still renders k6 data against the pinned version — verified by query through the datasource proxy, not by the container merely starting (EOP-154's lesson: a green exit code proved nothing).
  • ADR-016 amended if the pinning choice is worth recording; CHANGELOG.md updated under ## [Unreleased].
