renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a contributor reading ADR-008

I want to understand why XML changelogs were chosen over Liquibase's own formatted-SQL format

So that the decision is grounded in verifiable evidence rather than bare team preference, and future contributors can evaluate it honestly

Context & Business Value

docs/adr/ADR-008-database-migration-liquibase.md records the decision to use Liquibase. Its Decision section (line 19) states: "Adopt *Liquibase* with *XML changelogs* as the sole mechanism for all DDL and reference data DML changes".

The gap: the ADR's comparison table is Liquibase-vs-Flyway only. It never justifies choosing XML changelogs over Liquibase's own formatted-SQL changelog format. The only row touching format choice is line 30, | Team preference | XML format preferred | — | — bare preference, not a rationale. The repo owner has asked for that rationale to be written down, specifically centred on rollback, and the supporting evidence has already been verified against the repo.

Evidence verified against the repo

All ten changelogs live in src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/:

001-card-catalogue.xml, 002-real-deck.xml, 003-session-lifecycle.xml, 004-trick-play-schema.xml, 005-seat-and-sequence-bounds.xml, 006-session-expiry.xml, 2026-08-16-game-result.xml, 2026-08-17trim-deck-to-74-printed-cards.xml, 2026-08-18remove-ace-cards.xml, 2026-08-22-widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml.

  1. Changesets and `<rollback>` blocks are 1:1 — 26 each. Per file: 2/2, 2/2, 2/2, 9/9, 3/3, 2/2, 2/2, 1/1, 1/1, 2/2.
  1. Composition of the 26 rollback blocks: <dropTable> 10, <insert> 10 (51 <column> children), raw <sql> 9, <dropForeignKeyConstraint> 3, plus 1–2 each of <delete>, <dropColumn>, <dropUniqueConstraint>, <modifyDataType>, <addCheckConstraint>, <update>. The majority are dialect-agnostic declarative operations; raw SQL is the minority.
  1. Two engines, per ADR-008's own "Database targets" section: H2 in tests, PostgreSQL 17 in production. Declarative rollback elements render per-dialect; formatted SQL would mean writing each rollback twice or targeting the dialect intersection.
  1. `006-session-expiry.xml` is the worked example. Two changesets (001-add-expires-at-postgresql, 001-add-expires-at-h2) differ only in defaultValueComputed — NOW() + INTERVAL '24 hours' vs CURRENT_TIMESTAMP + INTERVAL '24' HOUR — selected by <preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN"><dbms type="postgresql"/></preConditions> and <dbms type="h2"/>. Its header comment states "H2 and PostgreSQL 17 use different interval syntax". XML localises the dialect divergence to one attribute; formatted SQL would fork the whole file.
  1. Reference-data rollback is the sharpest case. The 10 <insert> rollbacks belong to the deck-trimming and ace-removal migrations: reversing a DELETE means re-seeding exact rows, expressed once and portably via <insert>/<column>.
  1. Schema validation: every changelog carries xsi:schemaLocation to dbchangelog-latest.xsd, so a malformed rollback is a parse-time failure. In formatted SQL the equivalent is a --rollback comment, which the SQL parser must ignore — a mistyped directive silently yields no rollback at all. This is sharpened in this repo because Liquibase runs during the test suite, so a malformed changelog fails ./mvnw verify.
  1. No `.sql` file exists anywhere under `src/`.

Honesty constraints (explicit non-goals — must appear in the amendment)

  • Do NOT claim "rollback for free". Liquibase's auto-inference of inverses (createTable→dropTable) is real and structurally impossible in formatted SQL, but this repo does not rely on it — the 26/26 count proves every rollback is written out by hand, including the addColumn/createIndex pair in 006 that would have been inferred. The defensible claim is portable, schema-validated rollback.
  • Do NOT claim portability via a `dbms=` attribute. grep -rn 'dbms=' . returns nothing; it is a <dbms type="…"> element inside <preConditions>.
  • The genuine cost must be recorded: raw <sql> was still needed 9 times, so XML confines dialect-specific text rather than eliminating it.

Deployment & Feature Flag Strategy

  • Feature Flag: N/A — documentation-only change, no code deployed.
  • Deployment Behavior: PR merged directly to main; no flag required.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: Amendment block added

  • Given docs/adr/ADR-008-database-migration-liquibase.md exists
  • When the amendment is authored
  • Then a dated amendment block (2026-08-23) is appended, matching the pattern of the existing 2026-08-10 (EOP-27) and 2026-08-19 (EOP-35) blocks
  • And the amendment states the XML-over-formatted-SQL rationale, rollback-first, citing the verified evidence above

Scenario 2: Bare-preference row corrected

  • Given line 30 currently reads | Team preference | XML format preferred | — |
  • When the amendment is applied
  • Then the format-choice row is updated so format choice is no longer recorded as bare preference
  • And the correction is made within the amendment block (prior content is left byte-identical as immutable history)

Scenario 3: Honesty constraints honoured

  • Given the amendment is written
  • Then the stated cost (9 raw <sql> rollbacks) appears explicitly
  • And the non-claim about auto-inference appears explicitly (the repo does not rely on Liquibase's inferred inverses)

Scenario 4: ADR index kept consistent

  • Given ADR-008's status line is updated to name the new amendment
  • When the commit is made
  • Then the matching row in docs/adr/README.md is updated in the same commit
  • And AdrIndexConsistencyTest passes (it fails the build if the two are out of sync)

Scenario 5: Build passes

  • Given only documentation files are modified
  • When ./mvnw verify is run
  • Then all eight prose-integrity gates pass (including DeckArithmeticClaimsTest, AdrIndexConsistencyTest, SourceCitationAnchorTest, MermaidSequenceTextTest, EnumMirrorParityTest, OpenApiContractDriftTest, TrickPlayExceptionOriginTest, JoinCodeSpaceClaimsTest)

Scenario 6: Prior history preserved

  • Given existing dated amendment blocks (2026-08-10 (EOP-27) and 2026-08-19 (EOP-35)) are immutable history
  • When the new amendment is authored
  • Then prior amendment blocks are left byte-identical

Scenario 7: Scope boundary respected

  • Given this is a documentation-only story
  • Then no changelog file, no Java source, and no build configuration is modified

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • docs/adr/ADR-008-database-migration-liquibase.md gains a 2026-08-23 amendment block with the XML-over-formatted-SQL rationale, rollback-first.
  • The bare-preference row (line 30) is corrected within the amendment.
  • The stated cost (9 raw <sql> rollbacks) and the explicit non-claim about auto-inference both appear.
  • ADR-008 status line updated; docs/adr/README.md row updated in the same commit.
  • ./mvnw verify passes — all eight prose-integrity gates green.
  • Prior dated amendment blocks left byte-identical.
  • No changelog, Java source, or build configuration modified.
  • Commit message starts with [EOP-NNN] docs: ... per git-commits convention.

comments.body:
Delivered and awaiting human review on PR #124 — https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/124

Branch eop-162-adr-008-xml-over-sql-rationale, cut off origin/main at 467466d. Two commits: 5d93172 (the amendment) and 731b399 (remediation of a gate finding). Diff is two files, documentation only — docs/adr/ADR-008-database-migration-liquibase.md and docs/adr/README.md. No changelog, Java source or build configuration touched.

What was written

ADR-008's Decision asserted "Liquibase with XML changelogs" but the only rationale on record for the format was the comparison-table row Team preference | XML format preferred | —. A dated amendment block now records the rollback-centred rationale in three parts — declarative dialect-agnostic rollback, schema-validated rollback, and reference-data rollback — plus the 006-session-expiry.xml worked example and an explicit cost paragraph. The superseded table row is left physically in place and superseded in prose; both gates that ruled on this confirmed it as correct ADR practice, since prior content is immutable history.

Honesty constraints held

Two claims were deliberately not made, both verified absent from the committed text:

  • Not "rollback for free." Liquibase can auto-infer inverses, but this repository writes all 26 rollback blocks explicitly (1:1 with 26 changesets), so the claim would be falsified by its own changelogs. The amendment says so.
  • No `dbms=` attribute portability. grep -rn 'dbms=' . returns nothing — the mechanism is a <dbms type="…"/> element inside <preConditions>.

The cost is stated rather than buried: five of the 26 rollback blocks fall back to raw <sql>, confined to 005-seat-and-sequence-bounds.xml and 006-session-expiry.xml.

Three drafting defects found and corrected before commit

@architecture-guardian drafted the amendment, returned VERDICT: APPROVE and claimed it had independently verified every figure. Three claims were then proven wrong by direct inspection, and all were corrected:

  1. Direction inverted. It claimed the rollbacks "reverse <insert> operations" and should be written "as <delete>". The truth is the opposite — the forward changesets <delete>, and the rollbacks are the <insert>}}s. {{2026-08-18-remove-ace-cards.xml opens its rollback <!- Re-insert the six deleted Ace cards in their original order. -->.
  2. Non-existent elements. Item 1 listed <addColumn> and <addCheckConstraint> as rollback elements. Neither appears in any rollback block.
  3. Two wrong counts. "nine of the 26 rollbacks use raw <sql>" (actually five blocks, seven elements) and "51 <column> children" (actually 50).

Gate outcomes — all five APPROVE

@tester-unit-and-quality, @tester-api, @security-auditor, @code-reviewer, @architecture-guardian. Every figure was independently re-derived by XML parse by three separate gates.

@security-auditor raised one MEDIUM: the worked example quoted onFail="MARK_RAN" approvingly and without qualification, risking normalisation of a fail-open pattern. Remediated in 731b399, which records that MARK_RAN is a portability trade-off rather than a general pattern, sound here only because the two changesets are mutually exclusive alternatives covering every supported target. Re-dispatched and confirmed closed.

One inter-gate discrepancy was adjudicated rather than accepted on report: @architecture-guardian reported "2 forward deletes" against @code-reviewer's "4 and 6". An independent parse confirmed 4 and 6 — its third miscount on this story. The committed text was unaffected.

Verification

./mvnw verify run directly by the Tech Lead on the remediated tree: exit 0, 1360 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS. Both prior dated amendment blocks (2026-08-10 EOP-27, 2026-08-19 EOP-35) confirmed byte-identical in the diff; the only line naming them is the status line that enumerates them, paired with the docs/adr/README.md index row for AdrIndexConsistencyTest.

Follow-up recommended, not filed

@tester-unit-and-quality recommends a machine-read gate — a RollbackInventoryClaimsTest under src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/docs/ parsing the changelogs and asserting the amendment's figures — since prose figures can drift silently as changelogs are added. Explicitly a follow-up, not a blocker for this PR.

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a database operator or on-call engineer

I want to have a trustworthy, honest rollback path for the join-code widening migration

So that I can reason correctly about what a rollback will do — and not silently corrupt live session data or hard-fail under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on a populated table

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: None (standalone — prior ADR/docs stories in this project are standalone)
  • Target Persona: On-call engineer, database operator
  • Value Proposition: The current rollback in 2026-08-22--widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml passes every automated gate (XSD-valid, dialect-agnostic, 1:1 with its forward changeset) while being silently broken on any table the application has written to. Fixing it prevents a false sense of safety and removes a latent incident trigger.

Verified Defect Detail

The changelog src/main/resources/db/changelog/changes/2026-08-22--widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml contains two changesets, both author="miguel":

  • Changeset `001` — widens game_session.join_code from VARCHAR(6) to VARCHAR(8) via <modifyDataType> (eight Crockford base32 characters, forty bits of entropy — EOP-24, ADR-019).
  • Changeset `002` — pads pre-existing six-character codes via <update> with valueComputed="join_code || '00'" and <where>LENGTH(join_code) = 6</where>.

Liquibase rolls back in reverse order, so rollbackCount=2 runs 002's rollback then 001's. Both steps are broken on real data:

Step 1 — 002's rollback is lossy

It truncates with <column name="join_code" valueComputed="SUBSTRING(join_code, 1, 6)"/> and <where>LENGTH(join_code) = 8 AND join_code LIKE '%00'</where>. The changeset's own inline comment concedes: "A genuinely-generated code ending '00' would also match, which is why this rollback is paired with 001's narrowing rather than offered on its own — run them together (rollbackCount=2) or not at all."

With a 32-character Crockford alphabet, 1 in 1024 of all live join codes end in '00' and would be silently truncated from eight characters to six, breaking those sessions' reconnect path. Pairing the two rollbacks is not a mitigation — see Step 2.

Step 2 — 001's rollback then hard-fails

After Step 1, every genuinely generated eight-character code that does not end '00' — i.e. 1023/1024 of them — is still eight characters. <modifyDataType newDataType="VARCHAR(6)"/> therefore fails outright on PostgreSQL: ERROR: value too long for type character varying(6). The inline comment claims "Narrowing back is only safe once no eight-character code remains, so the rollback of 002 must run first" — but 002's rollback only removes padding, never genuine eight-character codes, so that precondition is never actually satisfied on a table the application has written to.

Root cause

Once the application has generated any genuine eight-character code, this migration is not reversible — narrowing must either fail or lose data. There is no correct rollback to write. This is exactly why nobody noticed: the changeset passes every automated gate.

Scale asymmetry (worth recording)

Widening VARCHAR(6)→VARCHAR(8) is binary-coercible and metadata-only on PostgreSQL (no table rewrite, O(1)). Narrowing is not coercible — had it succeeded it would be a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE plus a verification scan (O(table)). An O(1) forward migration has an O(table) exclusive-lock rollback.

Constraints

  • The existing changesets are immutable and MUST NOT be edited. Changeset identity is id + author + filepath; modifying a merged changeset causes checksum failures on every environment that has already run it. Add a new dated changelog file only.
  • New changelog file must follow the YYYY-MM-DD-description.xml naming convention (today is 2026-08-23). The NNN prefix sequence is frozen at 006- and must not be extended.
  • Every new changeset requires a <rollback> block. A <rollback> whose only child is a <comment> is an accepted pattern in this repo (002-real-deck.xml) — but the comment must state why the rollback is inert (not merely be empty), so the reader understands the honest position rather than assuming it was overlooked.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: Honest non-reversible marker supersedes the broken rollback

  • Given the existing changesets in 2026-08-22--widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml are left byte-identical
  • And a new dated changelog file is added (e.g. 2026-08-23--fix-join-code-rollback-marker.xml)
  • When a developer inspects the rollback for the join-code widening
  • Then the <rollback> block contains a <comment> that explicitly states the migration is not reversible on populated data and that recovery requires a forward migration
  • And the comment does not merely say "not reversible" but explains why (genuine eight-character codes cannot be narrowed back without data loss or hard failure)

Scenario 2: Round-trip test demonstrates the failure on seeded data (pre-fix)

  • Given a migration test under src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/migration/ that seeds the game_session table with at least one genuinely-generated eight-character join code
  • When liquibase.rollback(2, ...) is called against that seeded state
  • Then the test asserts the rollback fails (or produces data loss) — demonstrating the defect before the fix is applied

Scenario 3: Build stays green

  • Given the new changelog file and the round-trip test are committed
  • When ./mvnw verify is run
  • Then all checks pass, including Liquibase checksum validation, XSD validation, and the new migration test

Scenario 4: Feature flag not applicable

  • Given this is a database migration fix, not a user-visible feature
  • Then no feature flag is required

Dependencies

  • EOP-??? (Testcontainers PostgreSQL story) — the round-trip test in Scenario 2 is most meaningful when run against PostgreSQL 17 (the production engine). That story is an enabler for this one's full round-trip coverage. The round-trip test may be written against H2 first and upgraded once Testcontainers support lands.

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • Existing changesets in 2026-08-22--widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml are byte-identical (not edited).
  • New dated changelog file added with an honest <rollback><comment> explaining non-reversibility.
  • Round-trip migration test under src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/migration/ demonstrates the failure on seeded data.
  • ./mvnw verify green (Liquibase checksums, XSD, Checkstyle, SpotBugs, JaCoCo, Javadoc gates all pass).
  • No security regressions or plaintext secrets introduced.
  • Commit message starts with [EOP-NNN] fix: ... per git-commits convention.

comments.body:
Cross-reference correction. The description was drafted before issue keys were assigned and contains EOP-??? placeholders. The actual keys are:

  • EOP-164 — Run Liquibase migration tests against PostgreSQL 17 via Testcontainers. Linked as blocks this issue. This story can be started against H2, but the apply → rollback → apply round-trip test over seeded data is only fully meaningful once EOP-164 lands.
  • EOP-165 — Narrow the schema-validation argument in ADR-008's 2026-08-23 amendment. Related; no delivery dependency.

Read any EOP-??? in the description as one of the two above. The Jira issue links carry the authoritative dependency.

EOP-164 has measured this rollback on PostgreSQL 17, and this ticket's premise is wrong

EOP-164 (PR #125) now runs the whole changelog and its rollbacks against a real PostgreSQL 17 container. That turned this ticket's title — "lossy *and hard-failing* rollback" — into something testable for the first time, and the hard-failing half does not happen on the engine production runs. What happens instead is worse.

Finding 1 — the rollback silently truncates every eight-character join code

Seed one session with ABCDEFGH and roll back 2026-08-22--widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml. Changeset 002's rollback correctly leaves the row alone, because ABCDEFGH does not match WHERE LENGTH(join_code) = 8 AND join_code LIKE '%00'. The code then meets changeset 001's modifyDataType back to VARCHAR(6), and Liquibase reports:

Rolling Back Changeset: ...::002::miguel
Rolling Back Changeset: ...::001::miguel
Rollback command completed successfully.

game_session.join_code afterwards holds ABCDEF. No error, no warning.

The cause is that Liquibase's PostgreSQL modifyDataType generator narrows the column with an explicit cast, and an explicit cast to varchar truncates in PostgreSQL rather than raising value too long for type character varying(6). So the defect is not confined to the one-in-1024 codes ending 00 that changeset 002's rollback mishandles — it silently rewrites every live eight-character code, and it does so while reporting success. A seated player's code stops resolving and nothing in the log says why.

Pinned by PostgresRollbackRoundTripIT.rollingBackTheWideningSilentlyTruncatesAGenuineEightCharacterCode.

Finding 2 — the genuine hard failure exists, but it is data-dependent

There is a hard failure, and it is arguably the more dangerous shape. Seed two live sessions whose codes share a six-character prefix — say ABCDEFGH and ABCDEFJK, both perfectly legitimate — and the narrowing truncates both to ABCDEF, which uq_game_session_join_code forbids. The rollback aborts with a constraint violation. PostgreSQL's transactional DDL means nothing is half-applied: both rows and the column width survive intact.

The operational consequence is the part worth dwelling on. Whether this rollback succeeds depends on the data, not the schema. Rehearsed against an empty or lightly-seeded database it passes cleanly; run against production with two unlucky sessions in flight it aborts. That is precisely the property a migration rollback must never have.

Pinned by PostgresRollbackRoundTripIT.rollingBackTheWideningCanCollideTwoSessionsOnTheUniqueConstraint.

What this means for this ticket

  • Restate the problem. The primary defect is silent data loss on success, not a hard failure. The hard failure is a secondary, data-dependent symptom. Fixing only the LIKE '%00' predicate in 002's rollback would leave finding 1 completely untouched.
  • Three tests are waiting for you. All three carry @DisplayName}}s beginning {{DEFECT (EOP-163) in src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/migration/PostgresRollbackRoundTripIT.java, and each has a // DEFECT: comment naming what its assertion must become once this ticket lands. They assert the current broken behaviour, so your fix will turn them red — that is the signal, not a regression. Invert them; do not delete them.
  • Deleting them is how this got here. The class Javadoc says so explicitly. A characterisation test that is removed because it reads unhappily is what let the defect ship.
  • A worked counter-example already exists in the repository. roundTripsASixCharacterSessionWithoutLoss shows the shape a correct rollback has: a legacy six-character session survives rollback and re-apply with its players, identity hashes, game_result and game_result_player rows all intact, and join_code padded back to eight characters.
  • One direction to consider. A <preConditions onFail="HALT"> on 001's rollback asserting that no eight-character code remains would convert both findings into a loud, honest refusal at the point of rollback. Refusing to unwind is a defensible outcome; silently rewriting live codes is not.

Dependency

EOP-164 blocks this ticket and is now complete, so the harness you need is on main as soon as PR #125 merges. Nothing here changes 2026-08-22--widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml — Golden Rule 1 means the fix is a new changelog, not an edit to a merged changeset.

Full reasoning is in ADR-056 under Consequences.

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a developer or CI pipeline

I want to execute Liquibase migration tests against a real PostgreSQL 17 instance via Testcontainers

So that the changeset that runs in CI is the same changeset that runs in production, and schema/entity agreement is verified against the actual production engine before it meets production traffic

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: None (standalone — prior ADR/docs stories in this project are standalone)
  • Target Persona: Developer, CI pipeline, on-call engineer
  • Value Proposition: Two independent expert advisors (@expert-dave-farley, @expert-alex-xu) named this the single highest-value change available — above the entire XML-vs-SQL format question. The current test/production engine gap means the PostgreSQL-specific migration branch is never exercised in CI, and a full apply→rollback→apply cycle on seeded data would have caught the defect described in the companion story (EOP-???) on the first run.

Verified Gap Detail

The changeset that runs in CI is not the changeset that runs in production

006-session-expiry.xml contains two changesets that differ only in one attribute — PostgreSQL defaultValueComputed="NOW() + INTERVAL '24 hours'" vs H2 defaultValueComputed="CURRENT_TIMESTAMP + INTERVAL '24' HOUR" — selected by <preConditions onFail="MARK_RAN"><dbms type="postgresql"/></preConditions> and <dbms type="h2"/>. The file's own header comment states: "H2 and PostgreSQL 17 use different interval syntax." The H2 branch runs in CI; the PostgreSQL branch runs only in production, verified by nothing.

ddl-auto: validate validates against the H2-rendered schema

So the PostgreSQL-rendered schema is never checked against the entity mappings before it meets production traffic. The project is relying on the fidelity of Liquibase's PostgreSQL generator — a third-party code path never executed in CI — as its guarantee of schema/entity agreement.

H2 cannot establish production semantics

H2 also cannot establish:

  • Lock behaviour (e.g. ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on column type changes)
  • Table-rewrite behaviour on narrowing operations
  • Transactional-DDL semantics (PostgreSQL has transactional DDL; H2 implicitly commits around DDL, so mid-changeset failure recovery differs between test and production)

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: Migration tests execute against Testcontainers PostgreSQL 17

  • Given Testcontainers is added as a test dependency
  • And a PostgreSQL 17 container is started for migration tests
  • When the full Liquibase changelog is applied
  • Then all 26 changesets execute successfully against PostgreSQL 17
  • And ddl-auto: validate confirms schema/entity agreement against the PostgreSQL-rendered schema

Scenario 2: Both branches of 006-session-expiry.xml are exercisable

  • Given the Testcontainers PostgreSQL 17 test suite
  • When the migration runs
  • Then the PostgreSQL-specific defaultValueComputed="NOW() + INTERVAL '24 hours'" branch executes (not the H2 branch)
  • And the H2 branch continues to execute in the fast unit suite

Scenario 3: Apply-all → rollback-all → apply-all cycle on non-trivially seeded data

  • Given the Testcontainers PostgreSQL 17 instance
  • And the database is seeded with representative data (including at least one game_session row with an eight-character join code)
  • When liquibase.rollback(N, ...) is called for all changesets, then the full changelog is re-applied
  • Then the cycle completes without data loss or hard failure for all changesets with valid rollbacks
  • And any changeset with an honest non-reversible marker produces the expected rollback-impossible error (not a silent data corruption)
  • Note: This scenario is the test that would have caught the defect in EOP-??? (broken join-code rollback) on the first run.

Scenario 4: Fast unit suite keeps H2

  • Given the Testcontainers suite is added
  • When ./mvnw test is run (unit suite only)
  • Then the fast unit tests continue to use H2 in-memory and complete in sub-second time
  • And the Testcontainers PostgreSQL tests are scoped to integration tests (e.g. ./mvnw verify or a dedicated Surefire/Failsafe configuration)

Scenario 5: CI runtime impact assessed and stated

  • Given the Testcontainers suite is integrated into CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
  • When the PR is raised
  • Then the PR description states the measured CI runtime delta (before vs after)
  • And the delta is acceptable (to be agreed at implementation time, but container startup should be amortised across the suite)

Scenario 6: Build stays green

  • Given the Testcontainers dependency and new migration tests are committed
  • When ./mvnw verify is run
  • Then all checks pass, including Liquibase checksum validation, Checkstyle, SpotBugs, JaCoCo (≥80% instruction, ≥70% branch), and Javadoc gates

Dependencies & Sequencing

  • Enabler for EOP-??? (Fix broken join-code rollback) — the round-trip test for that story is most meaningful when run against PostgreSQL 17. This story should be delivered first or in parallel.
  • No feature flag required — this is a test infrastructure change with no user-visible behaviour.

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • Testcontainers PostgreSQL 17 dependency added to pom.xml.
  • Migration integration tests execute the full changelog against PostgreSQL 17.
  • Both branches of 006-session-expiry.xml are exercisable (PostgreSQL branch in Testcontainers suite, H2 branch in fast unit suite).
  • Apply-all → rollback-all → apply-all cycle on non-trivially seeded data included and passing.
  • CI runtime delta measured and stated in PR description.
  • Fast unit suite (H2) unaffected — sub-second execution preserved.
  • ./mvnw verify green (all quality gates pass).
  • No security regressions or plaintext secrets introduced.
  • Commit message starts with [EOP-NNN] feat: ... per git-commits convention.

comments.body:
Cross-reference correction. The description was drafted before issue keys were assigned and contains EOP-??? placeholders. The actual keys are:

  • EOP-163 — Fix the lossy and hard-failing rollback in 2026-08-22--widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml. This issue is linked as blocking EOP-163: the apply → rollback → apply cycle over non-trivially seeded data delivered here is what would have caught that defect on the first run.
  • EOP-165 — Narrow the schema-validation argument in ADR-008's 2026-08-23 amendment. Related; no delivery dependency.

Read any EOP-??? in the description as one of the two above. The Jira issue links carry the authoritative dependency.

Delivered — PR #125, awaiting human approval

https://github.com/maglez/eop-threat-medeling/pull/125 — branch eop-164-liquibase-postgres-testcontainers, tip a086dfc. CI run 32661263948 on that commit: completed / success.

What now runs against PostgreSQL 17

Three failsafe integration tests under src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/migration/, sharing one postgres:17-alpine container (pinned to compose.app.yml's default) started once and amortised across all three classes:

  • PostgresChangelogIT (5 tests) — all 26 changesets apply; the PostgreSQL branch of 006-session-expiry.xml is EXECUTED while the H2 branch is MARK_RAN, which is the mirror image of what the fast suite proves and the assertion H2 structurally cannot make; the expires_at default really is rendered with PostgreSQL's own now() interval syntax; and a directory scan of the changelog files cross-checks the 26 so the constant cannot go stale.
  • PostgresSchemaValidationIT (2 tests) — a Spring context wired to the same container by @ServiceConnection, so Hibernate ddl-auto: validate finally validates the mappings against the PostgreSQL-rendered schema. Every mapped entity is read from the JPA metamodel rather than a hand-kept list.
  • PostgresRollbackRoundTripIT (6 tests) — apply-all, rollback-all, apply-all on seeded sessions, players and game results, including the dedicated round-trip of 006 and the eight-character join-code cases.

Acceptance criteria

AC Evidence
1. All 26 changesets apply; ddl-auto: validate against the PG schema Liquibase logged Run: 26 / Total change sets: 26; PostgresSchemaValidationIT asserts validate plus product name PostgreSQL and major version 17
2. Both 006 branches exercisable PG branch EXECUTED / H2 branch MARK_RAN on the container; the H2 suite still runs the H2 branch unchanged
3. Apply, rollback, apply on seeded data with an eight-character join code 6 tests, seeding the real foreign-key chain rather than suppressing referential integrity
4. ./mvnw test unaffected 1360 tests, no failsafe execution, no container, no Docker daemon needed
5. Wired into CI, runtime delta stated in the PR No workflow change needed — the build job already runs ./mvnw verify on a runner with a daemon. build job 119 s to 146 s (+27 s); the Maven step 110 s to 131 s (+21 s)
6. ./mvnw verify green BUILD SUCCESS 01:13; surefire 1360 passed; failsafe 13 passed; Checkstyle, Javadoc, SpotBugs clean; JaCoCo 147 classes, all coverage checks met

The finding worth reading

The rollback of 2026-08-22--widen-join-code-to-8-characters.xml does not hard-fail on PostgreSQL. Liquibase narrows the column with an explicit cast, and an explicit cast to a bounded varchar truncates instead of raising an error, so the rollback reports success while silently discarding two characters of every live eight-character join code — not merely the one-in-1024 ending in double zero. A genuine hard failure exists but is data-dependent: two sessions sharing a six-character prefix collide on the join-code unique constraint, so a rollback rehearsed on a lightly-seeded database proves nothing about production. EOP-163's premise is corrected in detail in a comment on that ticket. Three tests here pin the current behaviour with display names beginning DEFECT (EOP-163); the fix must invert them, not delete them.

Definition of Done — five gates

Gate Verdict
tester-unit-and-quality REJECT, then APPROVE after remediation
tester-api APPROVE
security-auditor APPROVE — no findings above INFO
code-reviewer APPROVE — no blockers or majors
architecture-guardian APPROVE after two documentation corrections

The unit-test gate's rejection was correct on both counts: the hand-kept table list was one entry short (trick_play_component), and there was no dedicated PostgreSQL rollback test for 006 despite that being the only engine-gated changelog. Both are fixed, and the table list is now cross-checked against the tables the migrated schema actually holds. The architecture gate required ADR-056 to stop claiming the seven-plugin constraint had disappeared — ADR-047 invited the revisit, and the cost is still real — and required an ADR-016 amendment recording the Testcontainers and Colima socket configuration. Both done.

Also changed

ADR-056 (new), an ADR-016 amendment, the ADR index, CHANGELOG under Unreleased, and a SETUP.md section on the two environment variables a Colima developer needs. pom.xml gained three test-scope dependencies and a bare maven-failsafe-plugin declaration — the seventh declared plugin, and its comment records at length why it must not be deleted as redundant: the parent supplies its goal bindings through pluginManagement, which only materialise when the plugin is declared, so an effective-POM reading taken with the declaration present is circular. Deleting it during this story made ./mvnw clean verify run zero integration tests and still report BUILD SUCCESS with every coverage check met.

renderedFields.description:
User Story

As a developer reading ADR-008

I want to find an accurate, honest account of what XSD validation does and does not guarantee for Liquibase rollbacks

So that I do not mistake a green build for a safety property it does not provide, and I can locate the actual rollback trustworthiness evidence (the three round-trip tests)

Context & Business Value

  • Epic: None (standalone — prior ADR/docs stories in this project are standalone)
  • Target Persona: Developer, code reviewer, future maintainer
  • Value Proposition: The 2026-08-23 amendment to ADR-008 (added under EOP-162, currently in open PR #124) argues three properties of XML over formatted SQL. Its second argument — that a bad XML rollback fails at parse time against dbchangelog-latest.xsd — was called the weakest by all four expert advisors, and is disproved by two files already in the repository tree. Leaving it uncorrected converts a green build into false confidence.

Verified Corrections Required

Correction 1 — The schema-validation argument is disproved by two files in the tree

The amendment claims XSD validation catches bad rollbacks at parse time. Two counterexamples already exist:

  1. `002-real-deck.xml:90-95` — a <rollback> whose only child is a <comment>. Schema-valid. Does nothing.
  2. `001-card-catalogue.xml:125-127` — <delete tableName="card"/>, unqualified, as the inverse of a six-row insert. Schema-valid, and it truncates the entire table.

@expert-uncle-bod's formulation: "A schema stops you writing nonsense; it never stops you writing the wrong thing correctly."

@expert-alex-xu: presenting XSD validation as a rollback safety property "is worse than not claiming it, because it converts a green build into false confidence."

The replacement argument, which is stronger and true: rollback trustworthiness here comes from executing the inverse in a test, not from the XSD. src/test/java/org/maglez/eop/migration/ contains three genuine round-trip tests:

  • DeckTrimMigrationRoundTripTest — calls liquibase.rollback(...), asserts 78 cards restored, then re-applies
  • SessionExpiryMigrationTest
  • TrickPlaySchemaRoundTripTest

The honest figure to publish: 3 of 10 changelog files have rollback round-trip coverage.

Correction 2 — "silently" overstates the formatted-SQL mistype behaviour

The amendment claims a mistyped formatted-SQL --rollback directive yields a silent no-op. This overstates it: a mistyped directive yields no rollback and Liquibase then refuses with a rollback-impossible error — not silent, but also not a parse-time failure. The word "silently" should be narrowed accordingly.

Correction 3 — The "forking the file" claim about formatted SQL is wrong

The amendment claims formatted SQL "would require forking the file entirely" for the 006-session-expiry.xml dialect split. This is incorrect: formatted SQL carries the same dbms attribute inline (--changeset eop:001-add-expires-at-postgresql dbms:postgresql) and would fork the same two changesets inside the same one file — the same structure, different syntax.

Constraints

  • Prior dated amendment blocks in ADR-008 are immutable history and must stay byte-identical. The fix is a new dated amendment block appended to the ADR.
  • docs/adr/README.md index row for ADR-008 must be updated in the same commit so AdrIndexConsistencyTest stays green.
  • This ticket is best done after PR #124 merges, to avoid amending an amendment that is still in review. State this as a sequencing note on the ticket (it is recorded here).

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin BDD Format)

Scenario 1: New dated amendment block narrows argument 2

  • Given PR #124 has merged (the 2026-08-23 amendment is on main)
  • When a new dated amendment block is appended to docs/adr/ADR-008-*.md
  • Then argument 2 is narrowed to distinguish malformed XML (caught by XSD) from semantically wrong rollback (not caught by XSD)
  • And the two counterexamples (002-real-deck.xml:90-95 and 001-card-catalogue.xml:125-127) are cited
  • And @expert-uncle-bod's formulation is recorded: "A schema stops you writing nonsense; it never stops you writing the wrong thing correctly."

Scenario 2: Replacement argument cites the three round-trip tests and the 3-of-10 figure

  • Given the new amendment block
  • When a developer reads the rollback trustworthiness section
  • Then the three round-trip tests (DeckTrimMigrationRoundTripTest, SessionExpiryMigrationTest, TrickPlaySchemaRoundTripTest) are cited by name
  • And the honest figure "3 of 10 changelog files have rollback round-trip coverage" is published
  • And the argument is that rollback trustworthiness comes from executing the inverse in a test, not from the XSD

Scenario 3: Two further corrections recorded

  • Given the new amendment block
  • When a developer reads the formatted-SQL comparison
  • Then "silently" is narrowed to reflect that a mistyped --rollback directive produces a rollback-impossible error (not a silent no-op)
  • And the "forking the file" claim is corrected to note that formatted SQL carries the same dbms attribute inline and would fork the same two changesets inside the same one file

Scenario 4: Prior amendment blocks are byte-identical

  • Given the new amendment is committed
  • When git diff HEAD~1 docs/adr/ADR-008-*.md is inspected
  • Then all content before the new dated amendment block is byte-identical to the pre-commit state

Scenario 5: AdrIndexConsistencyTest stays green

  • Given the ADR-008 amendment is committed
  • When ./mvnw verify is run
  • Then AdrIndexConsistencyTest passes — the docs/adr/README.md index row for ADR-008 reflects the updated status/date in the same commit

Scenario 6: Build stays green

  • Given the ADR amendment and README index update are committed
  • When ./mvnw verify is run
  • Then all checks pass, including AdrIndexConsistencyTest, DeckArithmeticClaimsTest, SourceCitationAnchorTest, and all other prose gates

Sequencing Note

This ticket should be picked up after PR #124 merges. Amending an amendment that is still in open review creates a merge conflict and risks the amendment being superseded before it lands. The sequencing dependency is on PR #124, not on the other two stories in this advisory batch.

Definition of Done (DoD)

  • New dated amendment block appended to docs/adr/ADR-008-*.md (prior blocks byte-identical).
  • Argument 2 narrowed: XSD catches malformed XML, not semantically wrong rollbacks; two counterexamples cited.
  • Three round-trip tests cited by name; "3 of 10 changelog files" figure published.
  • "silently" narrowed and "forking the file" claim corrected.
  • docs/adr/README.md index row updated in the same commit.
  • ./mvnw verify green (all prose gates, AdrIndexConsistencyTest, and all other quality gates pass).
  • No security regressions or plaintext secrets introduced.
  • Commit message starts with [EOP-NNN] docs: ... per git-commits convention.

renderedFields.description:
Context

The Jira Free account for maglez.atlassian.net expires imminently. All 163 issues in the EOP project (EOP-3..EOP-165) must be exported and imported into GitHub Issues on maglez/eop-threat-medeling before access is lost.

Scope

  • Full-fidelity raw JSON export of every issue, comment, issue link and project metadata, committed to docs/jira-export/ as JSON only (never Markdown — the repository's prose build gates walk docs/*/.md).
  • Deterministic ADF to GitHub-Flavored Markdown conversion. The corpus uses only 16 node types and 5 mark types, all of which map cleanly.
  • Two-pass import: create all issues to learn their GitHub numbers, then rewrite the 2062 EOP-N cross-references and 2055 dying maglez.atlassian.net URLs.
  • Parent/child relationships wired via GitHub's native sub-issues API. Typed issue links rendered as a relationships section, since GitHub has no typed link equivalent.
  • Issues in Done are created and then closed as completed.

Known limitations

  • GitHub's API cannot backdate created/updated or attribute authorship, so original timestamps, reporter and status are preserved in a provenance block in each body.
  • GitHub shares one number sequence between issues and pull requests. This repository already has 125 pull requests, so EOP-N to #N alignment is impossible; the mapping is recorded per issue rather than computed from an offset.

Out of scope

Priority (uniformly Medium), assignees (all but one unassigned), watchers, worklogs, sprints and boards. Changelogs are captured in the export but not rendered into issue bodies.

Acceptance criteria

  • docs/jira-export/ contains the raw export and the key-to-issue-number mapping.
  • Every Jira issue exists as a GitHub issue with its labels, hierarchy and comments.
  • No surviving atlassian.net URL in any imported body or comment.
  • ./mvnw verify passes after the export is committed.
